News.title: Kane ends England’s 25-year wait to win men’s Ballon d’Or award
News.content:
Harry Kane has become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others.

Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom.

Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three.

"Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane told Dazn.

"I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now.

"I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination.

"I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better."

England manager Thomas Tuchel said he was "delighted" to see Kane win the award as he hailed the forward's success as a "huge honour".

Prince William, meanwhile, said the former Tottenham Hotspur player was a "brilliant captain" and "remarkable player".

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals - plus eight assists - in 65 matches.

Only one player at a club in Europe's top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season.

But he wins it despite not lifting either of football's biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals.

Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981.

To celebrate Kane's success, the Wembley arches were lit up in gold on Monday night.

BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies.

News.title: Chris Mason: Budget is imminent as tricky issues pile up for Burnham
News.content:
Last week, Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh approved drilling in the Jackdaw field in the North Sea, about 150 miles east of Aberdeen.

This is principally a gas field and Fahnbulleh grounded her justification in providing the UK with greater energy security, at a time of war in Ukraine and in the Middle East.

The gas, she said, could be tapped into and serve British homes and businesses pretty much straight away, with the tax revenue put into an "energy wealth fund", with the aim being to invest in renewable and low carbon energy projects.

But what about the Rosebank field, 80 miles north west of the Shetland islands, with its focus on oil?

Labour figures in and outside government acknowledge this is a much, much harder sell to plenty in their own party and beyond. Some, who want to see the project go ahead, fear that the energy secretary is not likely to be convinced that it should.

It is in that context that we should see allies of the chancellor pointedly making it known that he is in favour of it.

His public language was quite telling on the day Jackdaw was approved, when he was talking about the Energy Wealth Fund: "It means the extra tax revenues that come from North Sea oil and gas can be directed into developing more clean energy projects for the future."

Note his reference to oil. Fahnbulleh said that Rosebank was "a different proposition" to Jackdaw.

Can those who worry, in particular, about the emissions from a new oil field, be won over by an argument grounded in this being a geopolitically pragmatic and environmentally credible part of transition to cleaner fuels?

Some Labour MPs hope so, but they know it's a tall order to persuade some, including some in government â which could, if it was approved, raise the question of ministerial resignations. Let's see.

News.title: Healey vows cheaper marmalade and gherkins in pre-Budget package of 'everyday fixes'
News.content:
John Healey will remove import taxes on marmalade, gherkins and more than 100 products in a bid to give families "breathing space" with the cost of living at the Budget.

The chancellor on Wednesday will promise a fresh series of "everyday fixes" to ease the pressure on households.

The measures will also include an end to the so-called cliff-edge for those receiving carer's allowance payments and higher tax-free mileage rates being made permanent.

But the Conservatives said the offer of "cheaper gherkins" was "an insult to families hammered by Labour's tax rises".

Ahead of the Budget, the government said it is removing tariffs on more than 100 "family favourite" products, while supporting farmers facing higher fertiliser costs and households reliant on heating oil.

The government says the changes could save households up to Â£21 per year when combined with existing tariff suspensions on products including pasta, fruit juice and tuna.

News.title: Israel and the US are both going to the polls - the consequences will be global
News.content:
In the next week, two sets of elections will be held on two continents, the outcomes of which could have profound consequences for the world.

By a fluke of electoral timetabling, millions of voters around 6,000 miles apart will unite in exercising their democratic rights within days of each other.

Voters in Israel go to the polls on Tuesday to elect a new parliament; a week later, voters in the United States will elect a new Congress.

A former speaker of that Congress, Tip O'Neill, may have once said that "all politics is local". But the consequences of these elections will undoubtedly be global.

For these elections are not just proximate, they are intertwined.

The future governance of Israel will have a lasting impact on the Middle East and wars raging across the region.

And any change in the electoral map of America could shape not just those wars but also the future of the global economy.

Between the two there is a physical connection: the lobby group Republicans Overseas Israel estimates about half a million Israelis with American passports can vote in both polls.

News.title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed
News.content:
Two men who killed a mother and her four-year-old daughter as they raced their high-performance cars along a Leeds city centre road have been jailed.

Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her daughter Lena Czepczor were killed when they were hit by an Audi TT RS as they walked to the girl's nursery on the A61 Scott Hall Road on 16 January 2023.

At Leeds Crown Court on Monday, Hardeep Bhachu, 29, was jailed for 12 years and Jasskamal Riyat, 37, for 16 years.

Sentencing the men, Judge Singh said the road was "not a race track" and told them the deaths had consequences that were "immeasurable", with an "immense" impact on those left behind.

Bhachu, of Grant Row in Adel, had earlier admitted two counts of causing death by dangerous driving, while Riyat, of Buckstone Avenue in Moortown, was convicted by a jury after denying he had been racing him.

The court heard the pair, who did not previously know each other, accelerated away from traffic lights on Scott Hall Road shortly before the crash.

Prosecutors said Riyat's BMW reached speeds of up to 89mph in the 40mph zone before Bhachu lost control of his Audi, mounted the pavement and struck Hulboj and her daughter.

News.title: Storm Boelo leaves 22,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning
News.content:
A clean-up operation is under way in parts of the UK after Storm Boelo caused flooding and property damage, leaving thousands without power.

The Energy Networks Association (ENA) said around 22,600 properties were still without power as of Monday afternoon.

Two men were killed by falling trees during the storm on Sunday - a man in his 20s whose car was hit in north London and a 60-year-old man in Dumfries and Galloway identified as Richard Baines, the long-serving curator of Logan Botanic Garden.

A yellow warning for strong winds came in effect at 18:00 on Monday across the west coast of England, Wales and Scotland and eastern parts of Northern Ireland and will last until 03:00 on Tuesday.

The Met Office has warned that further power cuts in areas covered by the warning are likely and people should make sure they have essentials prepared, including torches and batteries.

Coastal communities could also be affected by spray or large waves, while travel delays are expected.

Boelo is the second storm to have hit parts of the UK in recent days, following Storm Austen.

Leo Slade, CEO of the ENA said it had been "a tough weekend" and that efforts to reconnect some properties were being hampered by the weather, with sustained winds of 50-85mph across parts of Scotland and northern England.

"Until that weather system passes, we can't safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up, so today is going to be a hive of activity in getting engineers out into the field," Slade told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

He stressed that the UK's power network was very resilient and money was spent to prepare for these sorts of scenarios, but said a debate was needed over how much more investment was required to mitigate for further storms brought by climate change.

News.title: Busted's James Bourne says 'hero' brother saved his life with kidney donation
News.content:
Busted star James Bourne has said his brother "saved my life" by donating a kidney, after doctors had given him "a few years left to live".

The guitarist, 43, dropped out of an arena tour featuring his band and fellow punk-pop favourites McFly in September 2025, just a day before it began.

He blamed health problems and was replaced by his younger brother Chris.

James later said he needed major surgery to "extend my life", and has now thanked his "hero" Chris and said they are both recovering from their transplant operations.

News.title: Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets with screen problems
News.content:
Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets that have developed problems with their screens just days after the highly-anticipated smartphone went on sale.

Photos posted by social media users show lines that appeared on the screens of the technology giant's first ever foldable device, which has a starting price of Â£1,999 ($2,668) in the UK.

Apple said it is aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of units and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement.

The Duo's launch, which attracted long queues at Apple stores around the world last week, comes as the brand tries to reinvigorate its catalogue and challenge the foldable phones offered by rivals.

Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen's centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device.

The Duo's 7.6-inch (19.3cm) inner display is held together by a central hinge - a complex piece of engineering that has resulted in flaws in the folding devices made by some of Apple's competitors.

Samsung's first foldable phone, the Galaxy Fold, suffered an early setback in 2019 when reviewers reported broken screens on the devices.

News.title: DUP MLA joins Lockhart's call for O'Neill's removal as first minister
News.content:
A Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) assembly member has joined MP colleague Carla Lockhart's calls for Stormont's First Minister Michelle O'Neill to be "removed from office".

Diane Forsythe said "profound consequences" pledged over the Sinn FÃ©in vice-president's handling of the Drumcree parading dispute "must be honoured".

Lockhart last week stepped down from the DUP's officer board in response to party leader Gavin Robinson not removing their deputy first minister to force O'Neill from the joint office.

It follows unionist anger over the first minister's involvement in protests on the Garvaghy Road, which blocked a contentious Orange Order parade from passing along the mainly nationalist street in Portadown, County Armagh.

O'Neill and several other senior Sinn FÃ©in figures have been interviewed by police investigating the demonstrations, with unionists accusing the party of acting unlawfully.

The Sinn FÃ©in deputy leader has defended her attendance at the demonstrations last month, saying she would "continue to stand with the Garvaghy Road residents".

The political row has sparked differences of opinion over how to respond within the DUP, which shares power with Sinn FÃ©in in Stormont's devolved government.

Forsythe is an assembly member for the South Down constituency and part of the DUP's party officer team.

In a post on Facebook on Monday night, Forsythe said she was "pleased" to show her support for Upper Bann MP Lockhart at a recent rally in Portadown.

She accused Sinn FÃ©in of "arrogance" and described the feelings of anger in the unionist community over O'Neill's actions as "immense".

"There have been commitments made to deliver profound consequences and that it cannot be business as usual. These must be honoured," she added.

"It is my view that Michelle O'Neill should be removed from office. The assembly and other ministerial offices would continue until the next election."

Forsythe added that in the absence of such "meaningful action", official engagements as first minister through the joint Executive Office should be stopped immediately as a "bare minimum".

Last week Robinson said he was "sorry" to see Lockhart quit the DUP's officer board but added that she remained "a key part of our team".

Speaking on the BBC's The View programme, the DUP leader said the party had reached a democratic decision on how to deal with the Drumcree fallout.

He questioned whether it was necessary to "punish everyone in Northern Ireland when actually we should be punishing those who broke the law".

"We have considered all options and we keep all options on the table," he added.

News.title: More than third of deaths of ex-prisoners on probation drug related, says report
News.content:
More than a third of deaths of former prisoners on probation in Wales in a year were drug related, according to a new report.

The Wales Governance Centre at Cardiff University, which has published the report, is urging politicians to tackle "systematic failures" in the criminal justice system.

The deaths figure is higher than the proportion recorded across England and Wales as a whole, where deaths in this category accounted for just over a fifth of the total.

Report author Dr Robert Jones called on the UK and Welsh governments to find a solution to the "tragic" situation.

The Welsh government said it was working to reduce "harms caused by substance misuse".

The UK government said it was spending Â£3.4m on services to help support prison leavers overcome addiction.

According to the report, 37% of all deaths among prison leavers supervised by probation in Wales in 2024-25 were drug related.

The number of drug poisonings where the intent was "undetermined" in Wales accounted for 19 of the 52 who died.

Jones said this was "substantially higher" than the proportion across England and Wales as a whole, where deaths in this same category accounted for just over a fifth (21%) of the total - 131 out of 620.

Criminal justice in Wales is controlled by Westminster.

The Plaid Cymru Welsh government, and the previous Labour administration in Cardiff before it, argue it should be devolved.

Speaking to BBC Wales, Jones said the research looked at UK government data including Freedom of Information requests.

He said: "The added shock value to this is that these data point towards some systematic failures with incredibly tragic circumstances and consequences.

"Yet there isn't really a particular debate or discussion ongoing at the moment about these deaths, and indeed their causes, and how we might actually find a solution to them."

Jones said many areas of social policy, including "responsibility for tackling substance use, housing, education and local government" were devolved to the Welsh government.

"So what tends to happen is that criminal justice matters can often fall between the gaps between debates in the Senedd and debates in Westminster," he added.

Jones said the report raised "important questions about the current devolution settlement and whether the Welsh government has the powers and levers necessary to address the underlying causes of many of the challenges facing Wales".

He added: "Only by confronting the realities highlighted throughout this report can politicians and policymakers hope to overcome the many challenges facing communities across Wales."

News.title: Independent review announced into murder of student Henry Nowak
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent review into the murder of Henry Nowak.

The 18-year-old student was fatally stabbed in Southampton in December by Vickrum Digwa, who falsely claimed he had been racially abused and had acted in self-defence. Digwa was jailed for life on 1 June, with a minimum term of 21 years.

Following the teenager's murder, police bodycam footage of him being handcuffed as he lay dying led to intense scrutiny of the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary and sparked wider debates around knife laws, race, policing and public trust.

The review, which was welcomed by Nowak's family, will be led by former Justice Secretary Alex Chalk KC.

"We must get to truth of what happened before, during and after that awful night and we must do everything in our power to ensure that no family suffers the same fate," Mahmood told the House of Commons on Monday.

Mahmood said the review will investigate what was known about Nowak's killer and if there were missed opportunities to intervene as well as the treatment of his family in the justice system and whether they received enough support.

In a statement published on Monday, the Home Office said the review will be carried out in two parts.

Phase one will cover the police, health services, local authorities educational institutions and faith organisations, including if any concerns were raised relating to weapon possession and violent behavior, the statement said.

It will also look to determine if there were missed opportunities to prevent Nowak's murder.

Phase two will follow after the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has concluded its investigation into the actions of police officers who attended the scene.

It will consider the actions of the IOPC and "if necessary" the police, the Home Office added.

The IOPC launched its own investigation into the response on the night of Nowak's death after bodycam footage showed the 18-year-old was handcuffed and left dying on the floor despite informing officers of his injuries.

The investigation was launched despite a sentencing judge ruling Nowak would not have survived his injuries, however quickly he received treatment.

The Nowak family described the announcement as a "significant moment in our fight for justice."

"We hope this review, alongside the ongoing investigations and inquest, will finally uncover the full truth and deliver the accountability and meaningful change we have fought so hard for," they added in a statement.

"Our experience of the criminal justice system has been deeply disappointing, and we are determined that no other family should have to endure what we have."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch welcomed the decision to launch the review.

"There must be proper accountability for those who failed Henry and his family," she said.

The review is due to report in five months.

News.title: No 10 appears to backtrack on PM's freedom of movement referendum suggestion
News.content:
Downing Street has appeared to backtrack on the prime minister's suggestion that he could call another referendum on whether to join the EU's freedom of movement.

Asked earlier by broadcasters if he could introduce freedom of movement without a referendum, Andy Burnham said "no".

But sources told the BBC no decision on that has been made and the prime minister's deputy spokesperson later said the government was not going to "get ahead" of how to consult the public.

Burnham has ruled out major changes to the UK's relationship with the EU before the next general election but says he wants start a conversation about potential options.

He told broadcasters that he would "never move ahead of the British public when it comes to Brexit".

Migration dominated debate during the 2016 Brexit campaign, with the Leave campaign raising issues about freedom of movement allowing any EU citizen to move to the UK.

Burnham has said he is committed to Labour's 2024 election manifesto, which ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

And he has previously stressed any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is due by 2029.

After lengthy questioning about the issue, Number 10 sought to clarify the prime minister's remarks, saying: "The prime minister isn't proposing a return to freedom of movement or any option."

"He is crucially not leaning either way and that will be for the British public to decide," the prime minister's deputy spokeswoman said.

"What he wants to do first is have a conversation with the public. The process will follow."

She added: "The PM thinks the Brexit deal is not good enough."

Freedom of movement, which allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country, is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market.

The single market enables goods, services and people to move freely between member states, with countries also applying many common rules and standards.

News.title: Army officer killed by reversing Warrior with faulty alarm - inquest
News.content:
The armoured vehicle was stationary for between 38 and 43 seconds after the collision, the inquest heard, as soldiers shouted "wait" and horns sounded.

A stop call was sent at 10:25, which halted the exercise.

A built-in alarm system, which would have sounded a noise and shown a light to indicate the rear doors were open, did not work as a wire was broken, the inquest was told.

Col Watson said: "The built-in alarm would have alarmed because the rear doors were open, and had that gone off the driver would have almost certainly stopped."

Alarms had been installed on Warriors after two fatal incidents in the 1990s.

Col Watson said several faults with the armoured vehicles were known about, but he told the inquest that these had not meant the vehicle should have been taken out of service.

The inquest also heard the FV-511model involved in the incident was not ordinarily used for disembarking troops and close combat.

"The student commander had done the majority of his training on the FV-510, which is the platoon variant of the vehicle," Col Watson said.

"In general, the crew and service personnel within 5 Rifles were not that familiar with the FV-511 and its differences with the FV-510."

News.title: Daughter wins £127k claim for caring for mum at home
News.content:
A woman has described her "phenomenal" relief after she won a legal case that means she is entitled to be paid Â£127k from her mother's estate for caring for her in her final years.

Bern Rogers, from Bristol, told the BBC of the "harrowing and deeply sad" family dispute since her elderly mother Sheila died in 2020, which led to her facing criminal charges.

Legal experts said the "hugely significant" High Court ruling would lead to other claims.

The executor of Sheila's estate, Bern's brother Andrew, said it had "always been willing to pay" her "genuine expenses" and an extra amount for her efforts. But the estate intends to appeal against the judgment that awarded Bern Â£127,500 for care provided.

News.title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month
News.content:
Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.

The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.

This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.

The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.

Consultants â the most senior doctors in hospitals â were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.

But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.

The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.

News.title: Russell Brand asked assistant for female fan phone numbers, court hears
News.content:
A former personal assistant of Russell Brand has told a court she was instructed to get phone numbers for the entertainer from female fans when she first started working with him.

Helen Berger, who worked closely with Brand from June 2006 to February 2007, said the request "felt uncomfortable" and, after seeking advice, she told the TV personality that she would not do that anymore.

Brand, 51, is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one charge of indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.

Brand had an "insane sexual appetite", Berger told Southwark Crown Court in a written statement on Monday.

Berger left her job with Brand after she became "sick of him", she said. She added that he had sex with numerous women during the time she was his assistant.

She described a work environment where Brand would ask her if he could "go and have sex now" when frustrated with a particular task.

Berger added that she never "witnessed anything against the law" but that "everyone normalised and dismissed his behaviour" so it "made me think it was accepted."

She told the court that "peacock" Brand found random women online to satisfy his "insane sexual appetite and was sleeping with people day and night", but sex often made him depressed.

She told the court Brand used MySpace to find women for sex, and said: "At his house, women often came over and it was clear they were there for sex."

She recalled once finding a female celebrity asleep in Brand's bed while he was wandering around the house half-dressed, and said of the comedian: "He was like a peacock, women would always approach him."

Russell Brand's defence team says any sexual activity was consensual and accounts have been twisted in the light of a defamatory TV documentary in 2023 which made allegations of sexual abuse against the entertainer.

The prosecution is due to finish on Tuesday morning.

News.title: Trump rants at Obama for comparing president’s White House decor to a Cheesecake Factory
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump lashed out at Barack Obama during his Mississippi rally after the former Democratic president insulted his White House decor, comparing it to a Cheesecake Factory.

“He said, 'This isn't a Cheesecake Factory.' Can you believe it?” Trump told the crowd Monday night, apparently still irked by Obama’s dig from the weekend. “Which is a very successful company," Trump continued. “He doesn't like successful companies.”

Commentators noted on social media that Trump was “BIG MAD” after Obama ridiculed the additions to the White House — including gold accents, a ballroom and a South Lawn helicopter pad.

“Guy’s building a ballroom that’s bigger than the White House,” Obama said Saturday at an Ohio rally. “He’s paved over the Rose Garden. Put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there’s gold everywhere. What’s up with the gold? Everything, more gold!”

“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory!” Obama quipped.

open image in gallery Donald Trump lashed out at Barack Obama during his Mississippi rally after the former president insulted his White House decor, comparing it to a Cheesecake Factory ( AP )

It was the second time the president raged against Obama’s joke on Monday.

“I’ve taken care of the White House,” Trump said earlier en route to the rally. “I fixed it with the finest artisans in the world. We reskinned it. It was in horrible shape.”

“For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory...that just shows why you were a lousy president,” he said.

Journalist Aaron Rupar posted a clip of Trump’s remarks to his 1.1 million followers. “Trump is BIG MAD about Obama saying the White House now looks like Saddam opened a Cheesecake Factory,” he said.

“Obama definitely hit a nerve,” a user replied.

open image in gallery ‘He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory!’ Obama quipped at a rally this weekend, prompting a defensive response from the president ( Getty )

“Uh oh. Somebody got under the tough guy’s skin,” another said.

But Obama was accused of “snobbery” by some Republican commentators.

“Cheesecake Factory is a great option for people who can’t afford a private chef at their Martha’s Vineyard estate,” Matt Whitlock said in a post on X, referencing the Obamas’ estate on the exclusive island.

Trump’s Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, also made a statement by dining at the Cheesecake Factory in Washington, D.C. on Monday.

“I had a great meal, always have a great meal, and I would just tell the Martha’s Vineyard set to give it a try,” Bessent told Fox Business in a retaliatory dig at Obama.

News.title: Judge extends court-ordered block on Trump’s renovation plans for public golf course in Washington
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A federal judge agreed Monday to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital.

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a preliminary injunction that halts tree-cutting and other work at the East Potomac Golf Course.

On Oct. 18, President Donald Trump announced plans on social media to close the golf course for 15 months, starting Nov. 15, and redevelop the 106-year-old park and course despite a court challenge by the D.C. Preservation League and two golfers. A day later, Trump posted that the work would start immediately.

Reyes, who was nominated to the bench by Democratic President Joe Biden, previously ordered the administration to suspend work on the project until at least Oct. 26.

The plaintiffs challenging the project claim the work is inflicting irreversible damage. At a hearing, the judge excoriated the government after workers cut down at least 400 trees over a holiday weekend with little notice to the plaintiffs.

The course renovation project is part of the Republican president’s aggressive campaign to leave his personal imprint on Washington’s historic landscape, including his plans to construct a huge ballroom at the White House, to build a massive arch and to add his own name to the Kennedy Center.

Reyes rejected the administration’s request for her to recuse herself from the case. The government questioned her impartiality and accused her of engaging in “egregious” behavior from the bench during an emergency hearing in the case.

News.title: Massachusetts lesbian bar that went viral over Covid mask backlash is closing
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Massachusetts bar that drew international attention following a dispute over its Covid face-covering policy has announced that it is preparing to close.

The Last Ditch, located in downtown Greenfield, posted a message on its Instagram page saying that the business required “new owners ASAP.”

The post announced that the venue was “SOFT CLOSING effective immediately, all BOOKED events will CONTINUE, otherwise we are CLOSED,” adding, “Love and solidarity to all.”

Several scheduled events remain on the calendar for this week, including karaoke and an open mic night, according to the post.

The venue was established in 2025 by three housemates — Asa Rosario, Jackie Matellian and Sage Territo — to address a void left by the recent closures of two other local queer establishments. The owners described the bar on its website as an oasis created for lesbians, as well as “transsexuals, gender freaks, workers and their friends,” to provide safe and happy drinking in the city of about 17,000 residents.

open image in gallery The Last Ditch, a Western Massachusetts bar that drew international attention following a dispute over its face-covering policy, announced Monday that it was preparing to close ( Google Earth )

“We have put our lives on hold to foster networks of care, resources, and a home base for organizing,” the founders wrote. “It’s time we pass it on.”

The bar's profile rose in September after a report published by The Boston Globe detailed internal conflict over its Covid protocols. In an effort to boost revenue, the owners decided to relax mandatory face coverings by making masks optional on Saturday nights.

Opponents quickly criticized the decision on social media, arguing that the bar was turning its back on immunocompromised patrons and failing to remain accessible.

Other commentators began ridiculing the customers and their Covid worries.

open image in gallery The bar's profile rose in September after a report published by The Boston Globe detailed internal conflict over its Covid protocols. In an effort to boost revenue, the owners decided to relax mandatory face coverings by making masks optional on Saturday nights ( Instagram/Last Ditch Bar )

The coverage went so viral that talent agency UTA, which represents The Boston Globe, confirmed to The Independent that it had fielded inquiries from Hollywood studios regarding potential TV, film and documentary adaptations of the article.

Although the coverage brought dozens of new customers to the bar’s first mask-optional Saturday, the boost in business was not enough to keep it open.

Greenfield Community and Economic Development Director Amy Cahillane told The New York Times on Monday that “it is always a shame to lose a small business.”

News.title: Michael Carrick fights on as Man United manager after surviving initial crisis talks
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Michael Carrick remains left in the dark but will stay on as Manchester United manager for now after surviving talks between the club’s hierarchy on Monday.

Carrick had appeared to be on the brink of the sack following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday and technical director Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada met to discuss his future at the club’s Carrington training ground and sound out potential replacements.

Carrick then arrived at the training ground shortly before 2pm on Monday afternoon, just in time to watch the club’s Under-21s play a behind-closed-doors match against Hull, before he left Carrington a few hours later.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

But the popular former midfielder – who was backed by the United supporters at Old Trafford despite the abject defeat to Bournemouth – remains in charge and is continuing to prepare for this weekend’s trip to Chelsea in the Premier League as usual. United’s first-team squad will be back at Carrington for training on Tuesday, which is expected to be led by Carrick.

That’s despite United’s hierarchy reportedly sounding out potential replacements for Carrick if they are required to appoint a fourth permanent manager in the three years since the minority Ineos ownership took control of football operations from the Glazers.

Former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, the ex-Bayern Munich and Germany head coach, are both available and are considered the frontrunners for the job if Carrick is sacked. Aston Villa’s Unai Emery and Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler are admired but their clubs would demand significant compensation.

The United supporters made clear who they blame for the club’s worst start to a league season in 40 years and longest winless run since 2015 as they turned on the players and chanted against the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos hierarchy, including director of football Wilcox, on Sunday.

Carrick made the decision to drop Bruno Fernandes and leave him on the bench following the captain’s criticism of his manager’s tactics, a move that appeared to receive support from the United fans as they did not chant for the Portuguese to be introduced despite the humbling to Bournemouth.

Former United defender Gary Neville accused the United players of “downing tools”, meanwhile, as the progress they made under Carrick last season has spectacularly unravelled and revealed a fractured dressing room.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

“Michael Carrick is a brilliant man,” Neville said on Sky Sports. “He's a man of integrity, of credibility, of decency, of professionalism, of high-quality football and consistency and reliability. Everything the group of players in that dressing room aren’t.

“I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes. If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.

"There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

“Why? Because it's gone to their heads. But they still walk around like King William. They are nothing, some of those players.”

open image in gallery ( Getty )

Carrick initially returned to Old Trafford as interim manager – his second stint in caretaker role – after the dismissal of Ruben Amorim at the beginning of the year. He was rewarded with the full-time position after guiding United to third in the Premier League last term and securing a return to the Champions League.

United spent £155m on three new midfielders this summer – signing Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andre Santos, after missing out on their top targets Elliott Anderson and Sandro Tonali – but failed to sign a back-up left-back to Luke Shaw or another forward to support the injury-prone Benjamin Sesko.

Lisandro Martinez criticised the club’s hierarchy for not doing more to support Carrick following the 2-1 defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month while Fernandes questioned his manager’s tactics following the 4-1 loss at Como last week.

Carrick said Fernandes did not play against Bournemouth due to “pure football” reasons while the Portuguese was also present at Carrington on Monday, reportedly for pre-planned treatment on a pre-existing injury.

United will travel to Chelsea on Saturday before playing back-to-back home games before the international break, welcoming Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa the following Sunday in the Premier League. There are then two weeks before United face a trip to Anfield to play Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel sends message to Harry Kane after winning Ballon d’Or
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Thomas Tuchel says he has “run out of superlatives” to describe Harry Kane after the England captain won the Ballon d’Or.

Bayern Munich striker Kane pipped Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to football’s most prestigious individual prize at the London Palladium, rewarded for his staggering season in which he scored 73 goals for club and country.

The 33-year-old became the first Englishman to lift the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001.

open image in gallery Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or on Monday night ( AFP/Getty )

Under Tuchel, he led his country to the last four of the World Cup, where they suffered a devastating loss to Argentina. England nevertheless achieved their best World Cup finish since 1966, coming home with bronze after victory over France in the third-place play-off.

Following Kane’s triumph, Tuchel said: “Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon D’Or!

“I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

“To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.

“I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches.”

The FA also honoured Kane’s Ballon d’Or win by illuminating the Wembley arch in gold on Monday night.

open image in gallery Wembley Stadium’s arch was illuminated in gold to honour Kane’s triumph ( Getty )

Kane paid tribute to his England team-mates, manager and staff during an emotional acceptance speech.

“To all my England teammates, we had a special year,” he said. “It wasn't the perfect year, but we had a lot of good moments. We built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness. The way we trained, the way we played, the togetherness in the hotel in the World Cup.

“It’s truly an honour to captain you, lead you. It makes me extremely proud so this one is for all of us, for sure.

“To Thomas Tuchel and the staff at England again. The leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired and it's an honour to represent you and represent the England badge the way you do.

“I know Debbie [Hewitt, FA Chair] is here tonight as well, so Debbie, thank you very much for everything you do and everyone at the FA, it's truly an honour to be your captain.”

News.title: ‘We done it!’ Harry Kane’s emotional message for wife Katie Goodland after Ballon d’Or triumph
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Harry Kane delivered an emotional speech and thanked his wife Katie Goodland after winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday night.

England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane pipped Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the most prestigious individual prize in world football, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the award.

An emotional Kane, 33, spoke for more than 10 minutes on stage after receiving the award at the London Palladium before thanking his long-term partner, Goodland, mother to his four children.

“To my wife, Kate, my best friend,” Kane said. “We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself.

“The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it's been horrible for you, here it is - we've done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they're your dreams as well, so it wouldn't be possible without you.

“This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it's all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you.

“Can't wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.”

Kane also thanked his wider family, including older brother Charlie and his parents, whom were in attendance on Monday night.

“My brother Charlie is here tonight,” he said. It didn't seem that long ago we was kicking a ball around the garden, over the park, watching football, talking football, just football mad. I know you tell me you gave me a lot of your footballing abilities, so thank you very much. I appreciate that.

“But to have that love and support from an older brother means the world to me. You travel, you watch, you give up time with your family to support me, so thank you.

open image in gallery Kane won the 2026 Ballon d’Or on Monday ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Goodland watches from her seat as Kane is awarded the Ballon d'Or ( AFP/Getty )

“Mum and Dad sitting there as well. What a moment. All those years, the sacrifice you gave me, the support you gave me, the times taking me to training, coming to watch me play all, all around England, all around Germany, no matter where it was, even to this day you're there.

“There was never any pressure from you to become a footballer. It was always about working hard. It was always about improving. It was always about learning and all those traits that you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight. I love you. Thank you very much.

“My kids sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime, especially as we're [the ceremony] a little later than we hoped. So to Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

“I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you. I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.”

News.title: Police and fire services in UK issued urgent warning over 'significant' cyber attack threats
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Police and fire services are inadequately safeguarded against cyber attacks due to a reliance on legacy technology and insufficient safeguards against human error, a watchdog has warned.

His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire and Rescue Services (HMICFRS) reported that police and fire chiefs view obsolete systems as their single greatest IT security threat.

The watchdog also noted that employing external IT contractors poses further hazards, especially when these firms store sensitive police data.

In addition, several backup systems intended to restore operations following a cyber breach were rated as "unsatisfactory".

Having examined three police forces and three fire and rescue services in England and Wales, inspectors determined that authorities are failing to adequately minimise human mistakes that leave them vulnerable to attack.

In a new report published on Tuesday, Michelle Skeer from HMICFRS said: “Many police forces and fire and rescue services need to update their ICT systems to improve resilience.

“Leaders we spoke to in both sectors identified these ‘legacy systems’ as their highest strategic risk for cybersecurity.

open image in gallery Inspectors found some forces are not doing enough to stop human error leaving them open to attack ( PA )

“Modernising ICT across both sectors must become a priority. All the organisations we inspected relied on legacy systems to a greater or lesser extent.”

Senior leaders are left relying on younger, less experienced staff who know more about IT, the report found.

Ms Skeer said: “It wasn’t just a lack of training and awareness that created opportunities for cyber attackers.

“In some of the organisations we inspected, we found poor security controls for staff joining, moving within and leaving the organisation.

“We also found poor password management and a lack of up-to-date approaches, such as multi-factor authentication (where users must provide two or more verification methods to gain access to systems).

“Some forces and services simply aren’t doing enough to prevent human error from increasing the risk of cyber attacks.”

The report makes a series of recommendations including ensuring that all police forces and fire services reach “baseline standards” for cybersecurity, and that the management of third party contractors is improved.

“Underpinning all these problems is a leadership issue,” Ms Skeer said.

“Several senior police and fire leaders we interviewed told us that they didn’t consider cybersecurity to be part of daily operational decision-making.

“This has led to financial investment being directed to other more operational and tangible priorities.

open image in gallery Senior leaders are left relying on younger, less experienced staff who know more about IT, the report found ( PA )

“It is difficult for both sectors to keep up with rapid technological change and cybersecurity-related threats as a result.

“Most senior leaders in both sectors have operational backgrounds.

“They have an expert understanding of operational risks and the investment needed to mitigate them.

“Often, they rely on more junior technical specialists to identify and explain cybersecurity risks and mitigations.”

A national centre for digital management for the fire service should be set up, similar to that in the police, inspectors said.

Ms Skeer added that cyber security should be a “core organisational priority”, and that the major proposed reform of the police service as well as the overhaul of local government could offer a chance to improve.

She said: “The cyber threat to police forces and fire and rescue services is significant and expanding rapidly.

“A major cyberattack is not a hypothetical scenario and successful attacks have been disruptive, put the public at risk and were expensive to fix.

“While there have been gradual improvements, many forces and services still need to urgently redouble their efforts to respond to the increased risk of cyberattacks.”

News.title: Royal Mail releases new stamps honouring British armed forces on Armistice Day
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A set of six stamps honouring the service of the nation's armed forces has been revealed by Royal Mail.

The stamps go on issue on Armistice Day, 11 November.

This year, Armistice Day marks 110 years since the Battle of the Somme, which began on 1 July 1916 and became one of the defining battles of the First World War.

Specially commissioned artworks by British artist Matthew Cook feature on all six stamps, reflecting different aspects of remembrance.

Each has been painted with a colour palette inspired by the red poppy.

open image in gallery A woman salutes an RAF flypast ( PA )

“Remembrance holds a profound place in our national life,” David Gold of Royal Mail said.

“Through these stamps, we pay tribute to the service and sacrifice of those who have served our country through two world wars and many other conflicts.

“Matthew Cook’s poignant artworks provide a fitting and powerful way to reflect on the sacrifices made by so many courageous men and women across the generations.”

Mr Cook has served as a reservist in the Parachute Regiment and The Rifles and been deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan.

open image in gallery A stamp featuring people laying wreaths at Tyne Cot Cemetery, near Passchendaele ( PA )

“Remembrance has a very special place in my life,” he said.

“I was delighted to be asked to illustrate these stamps and to take on the challenge of such a sensitive and significant subject.

“It is always a privilege to illustrate stamps for Royal Mail, and this project felt particularly special.”

Mr Cook previously contributed images of Royal Ascot, the Henley Regatta and the Highland Games for a set of Royal Mail commemorative stamps.

open image in gallery One stamp depicts a Royal Marines bugler at the Cenotaph ( PA )

Armistice Day

Armistice Day is observed in Britain every 11 November and commemorates the agreement signed by the Allies and Germany that brought an end to the First World War.

It also serves as a reminder of those killed in that conflict, and in wars since.

The agreement came into effect “on the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month” of 1918.

The day is often referred to as Remembrance Day in other parts of the Commonwealth and as Veterans Day in the United States.

Peace negotiations were completed seven months after the armistice agreement, with the signing of the Treaty of Versailles.

News.title: Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

News.title: Nurse accused of spreading Ebola murdered by mob
News.content:
A nurse was killed and a teacher badly injured in a mob attack after being accused of spreading Ebola in the water supply in Congo.

The unnamed victims were set upon in Bafwasende territory of Tshopo province after a group of young people accused them of being responsible for the outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever.

The nurse was killed outright and the teacher, who local media reported was close to the health worker, only survived after being rescued by police.

The World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the attack, which is only the latest incident of health workers being attacked by suspicious, scared or angry locals.

Medical workers have been forced to deal with widespread rumours that the outbreak – the world’s second largest – is spread by them.

Other conspiracy theories claim the outbreak is a money-making hoax for aid agencies, or that foreigners are using it as a pretext to grab the country’s minerals.

Strict rules imposed on how to conduct funerals in order to stop mourners becoming infected, have become another flashpoint.

Last month, a Congolese politician was beaten to death in North Kivu after publicly defending the government’s response.

He had been calling on the public to obey response measures, particularly social distancing and hand washing, on a radio show.

News.title: ‘Our world is yellow’: Fears for children as sickening smog blankets Indonesia
News.content:
For two months now, Natanael Undas has opened his curtains not to blue skies, but a sickening sepia haze that blocks out any sunlight. As the relentless fires smoulder nearby, his city looks “more like Mars” than Indonesian Borneo.

“We start our day in yellow, and we end our day in yellow,” the 32-year-old headteacher told the Telegraph. “When you inhale and take a breath, it feels like you’re choking. Your eyes hurt, your nose hurts… when you go outside, it feels like someone is burning dry leaves next to you.”

Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan, is on the front lines of an environmental crisis that has cloaked much of Southeast Asia in a toxic haze for months.

According to Nusantara Atlas, an open-access platform that tracks deforestation, fires have torched roughly 1.9 million hectares across the archipelago so far this year – including one million hectares in September alone.

“I’ve seen burning in the city, burning in the forests, burning near the river, burning in the peatlands, burning near the street – it’s devastating,” said Mr Undas. “It’s the longest burning season I’ve seen. Usually the rainy season comes in October, but everything is still on fire.”

News.title: Britain sanctions warlords accused of rape in Sudan
News.content:
The British government is to sanction senior military and militia commanders accused of atrocities, including rape and sexual violence, during the fall of the city of El Fasher in Sudan.

At least 15 commanders from both the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been sanctioned after investigations found they used rape as a weapon of war during the brutal siege of the Sudanese city in October last year.

The siege, perpetrated by the RSF paramilitary group who have been battling SAF since 2023, resulted in the massacre of at least 60,000 people.

The fall of the city came after an 18-month blockade in which the city’s population were deliberately starved into submission, according to a report from the UK-government funded think tank the Centre for Information Resilience.

Reports from aid organisations, UN investigators, and eyewitness accounts have previously found that rape was used on a mass scale by both sides.

In one incident, aid workers said at least 54 children were raped or sexually assaulted by RSF fighters while fleeing the city to Tawila, a town 25 miles west of El Fasher.

News.title: Wolff puts ‘tequila on ice’ with Antonelli two points away from title
News.content:
Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Ferrari’s Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs. Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track made the final laps rather processional, denying the huge crowds at COTA the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot.

That might have been fun, with Verstappen having lost his cool with his team midway through the race, furious that they didn’t order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping: “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air.”

Incredibly, his third place finish in Austin means is the first time since the final race of 2020 that Verstappen has been out of title contention.

But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli who should be champion by the end of next week. Not that he was getting carried away. “It was the result we needed,” he said. “The whole team deserved it so much, bringing this [upgrade] package. It was also the perfect execution with the strategy to do the one stop.”

Asked about the title, he added: “We’re very close, we try to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon. I mean, the perfect way will be to finish in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season. I’m very aware that it’s very close, but the mindset doesn’t change. I want to finish on a high to go into 2027 with momentum.”

“Yeah, what a boy, no?” Wolff said, admiringly. “I was just saying before, I got a question about whether he was nervous before the race, and I said, ‘Oh, he just sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, ‘I’m just going to enjoy this right now, and it’s weird, I’m not thinking about the championship at all. Isn’t that funny?’”

Wolff added that there would “definitely be a lot of tequila on ice” in Mexico. In hindsight it was always going to be a more appropriate venue to crown the sport’s youngest ever champion. Antonelli is not, after all, old enough to drink yet in the state of Texas.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

Sports.title: Harry Kane enjoys best moment of career as Bayern Munich’s ‘greatest ever signing’ is handed Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE spent most of his career waiting for trophies, awards and accolades – and now they keep on coming.

At his home in Grunwald, south of Munich, there is a gleaming new arrival to his collection which will now take pride of place: a golden ball measuring 31cm x 23cm and weighing 7kg.



No one can deny Kane, a true professional on and off the pitch, the greatest individual moment of his career by being presented with the Ballon d’Or.

And in a few weeks there will be another extraordinary night for the 33-year-old when he breaks Peter Shilton’s appearances record for England by earning his 126th cap.



That game against Croatia is on November 12 at Wembley and equally, it was fitting last night’s ceremony also took place in London.

Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan (twice) and Michael Owen are the other Englishmen to have won this award.



Charlton won in 1966 after inspiring the nation to World Cup glory so in terms of success, he is ahead of Kane.

But Kane’s numbers are frankly ridiculous compared to the Manchester United legend. In the eyes of the 100 journalists who vote for this award, his 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England topped anything else achieved by the great and good of world football — and they were dead right.

During those loan periods at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester, when he struggled to convince, this special moment on stage at the London Palladium seemed utterly impossible.

Yet although he appears to be a mild-mannered and relaxed individual, Kane is an extremely determined and driven professional who has always thrived on sticking two fingers up to his many doubters. And he has done it again.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Although Kane’s club boss, Vincent Kompany, is still recovering after collapsing, there was a huge delegation from Bayern.

Apart from picking up Fifa’s Golden Boot for finishing top scorer at the 2018 World Cup, Kane had won little and suffered only heartbreak during his years at Tottenham.

But in 2023, Kane made the best decision of his life by tearing himself away from his beloved Spurs to link up with Bayern.

Although Kane was ridiculed at the end of the first season as Xabi Alonso’s unbeaten Bayer Leverkusen won the title, he got his hands on his first Bundesliga crown in 2025.



Kane then won a domestic double last season during which everything he touched ended up in the net.

He fired four hat-tricks in the Bundesliga, including one on the final day of the season to reach 36 league goals.

Bayern cruised to the title, winning by 16 points. He also scored another hat-trick in the 3-0 win over Stuttgart in the German Cup final.

So in total, he netted 61 times for Bayern with another 12 for England, including six at the World Cup.

Always hungry for success

These 73 goals made it the second-highest goalscoring season by any footballer in the 21st century, trailing only Lionel Messi’s 82-goal haul in 2011-12. Kane was Europe’s top domestic goalscorer for the second time in his career.



And for the third successive year, he was the top scorer in German football. The trophy is a cannon, which is hilarious given the dislike Arsenal fans have for him.

Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness claims Kane is the club’s greatest ever signing, which is some statement. There is, however, the argument that Kane has not delivered in the big games for England.

But a strong counter is that the rest of the team have not been good enough against the top sides to give him the ammunition. Kane won a bronze medal at this summer’s World Cup after the third place play-off win over France in Miami.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, that was little consolation to the captain, who was still hurting after the 2-1 late loss to Argentina in the semi-finals. Already, he is looking forward to Euro 2028 which England will co-host as one of the favourites.

But right now, his focus is on a third successive Bundesliga title and a first Champions League success. And never happy and always hungry for success, he will also be looking to win a second Ballon d’Or crown.

Sports.title: Ex-England star Paul Merson hit with £1,600 bill after driving untaxed car for six months in ‘honest mistake’
Sports.content:

BUNGLING ex-England football ace Paul Merson must stump up more than £1,600 after forgetting to pay his road tax.

The Sky Sports pundit apologised to magistrates for his “honest” mistake, but was still handed the stinging financial penalty.



His £20,000 VW Touareg was flagged for being untaxed for six months by an ANPR camera in Cardiff in March.

The 58-year-old, from Teddington, South West London, told JPs in Croydon, South London: “I honestly thought I’d done it.



“I’m very sorry.”

The double title winner with Arsenal was banned for six months in 2024 for speeding three times in a month in the same car.

He also received a 14-month ban in 2011 after falling asleep at the wheel and crashing into a lorry on the M40 motorway, near Warwick.

Court documents showed the £20,000 VW’s tax had expired six months earlier.

Merson pleaded guilty to using a vehicle without a valid vehicle licence under the Single Justice Procedure.

He won the league twice with Arsenal in 1989 and 1991 and secured an FA Cup and League Cup double in 1993.



Merson, who was praised for going public over his battle with alcohol, drugs and gambling addictions, won 21 England caps.
