Sports.title: Michael Carrick in limbo as Man Utd draw up succession plan after Ratcliffe joins crisis talks and Howe obstacle emerges
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED chiefs left Michael Carrick in a state of limbo on Monday night after hours of crisis talks over his job.

A stung Old Trafford hierarchy is refusing to pull the trigger on a sacking until they have a clear plan in place.



Carrick’s job is in serious doubt ten months after replacing Ruben Amorim following a day of emergency talks at the club’s Carrington training base.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada were locked in discussions on Monday with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairs Avram and Joel Glazer dialing in via video link.



It could mean Carrick takes training when United’s players report back on Tuesday morning following a standard day off after a match.

As things stand, Carrick expects to lead training to begin preparations for their next game at Chelsea on Saturday, unless he is dragged in before then.



Carrick spent three hours at United’s Carrington training base on Monday afternoon to watch the reserves draw 2-2 against Hull City in a behind-closed-doors friendly.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Bayern and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann are among the options should Carrick be sacked.

United’s top brass are well aware of the embarrassment of appointing a third manager this year after six defeats in 12 matches, and a fourth since Ratcliffe took charge of football operations in February 2024.

Sunday’s shameful 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the club just a point above the drop and the Amazon documentary could find themselves covering a relegation scrap this season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It emerged on Monday that United would have to pay a few million in compensation to land Howe under the terms of his exit from Newcastle in July.

The 48-year-old had several years left on his contract at St James’ Park when he stepped down in the summer.

The Toon brought in a degree of protection in the event that he ended up at a rival in the months that followed.

Unai Emery and Fabian Hurzeler have admirers at Old Trafford but it would be expensive to prise them away from Aston Villa and Brighton, respectively

Former Chelsea and Spurs manager Antonio Conte is open to returning to football after leaving Napoli in June.



Carrick signed a two-year contract after guiding the club back into the Champions League in May.

The Stretford End hurled a tirade of abuse at the Glazers, Ratcliffe and board between spells of singing Carrick’s chant loudly and booing the players.

The bookies have suspended the betting on Carrick.

He is also at loggerheads with club captain Bruno Fernandes after dropping the reigning player of the year and refusing to bring him on against Bournemouth.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fernandes seemed to respond with a veiled dig at Carrick on Sunday night when he liked a cryptic Instagram post that read: “Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care”.



Fernandes was also at Carrington on Monday for treatment along with Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte.

Sports.title: Arsenal stars back 4-year-old cancer patient’s £339k appeal for life-saving treatment
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL football aces have boosted a four-year-old cancer patient’s push to raise £339,000 for life-saving treatment.

Gunners fan Zach Fleming was just two when diagnosed with rare stage 4 neuroblastoma.



To boost his fundraising drive, the Premier League champions invited Zach to Saturday’s 2-0 win against Everton at the Emirates Stadium.

He and brother Alex, 11, met players Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze, plus boss Mikel Arteta and club great Ian Wright.



Zach was given a signed shirt which will be auctioned as part of his appeal.

Mum Edwina, 40, of Hackney, North London, told The Sun: “The support that me and my family have received in regards to Zach’s diagnosis has been amazing.

“I can’t put into words the experience that Zach and his brother received on Saturday.

“They couldn’t do enough to assist us and make sure we had one of the most magical days that my kids could ever imagine. I’d like to say a massive, massive thank you to the Arsenal fans for all their support and heartfelt messages.”

Stage 4 neuroblastoma affects about 100 UK children each year.

It occurs when cells from the tumour spread to distant parts of the body.



Zach had 18 months of extensive treatment at Great Ormond Street Hospital but has relapsed, forcing him to pull out of school.

His parents hope that the CAR T-cell therapy offered in Italy’s capital Rome will help him see off the cancer and give him back his life as a happy, active child.

So far, Zach’s family has raised about £100,000 through a JustGiving page.



The campaign is supported by Solving Kids’ Cancer UK.

The family wrote: “Before he became ill, Zach was an active little boy who loved running around and playing with his brother. Through it all, he has never stopped being Zach.”

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or audience groan at Kate Scott as star-studded crowd endure lengthy delay before Harry Kane crowned winner
Sports.content:
Next

KATE SCOTT was met with groans from the star-studded Ballon d’Or audience during Monday night’s ceremony.

The popular presenter was hosting the prestigious awards alongside former Arsenal legend Thierry Henry at London’s Palladium.



The ceremony was badly delayed, with many in the packed auditorium having been forced to sit and wait patiently for the event to get going.

So when Scott revealed proceedings would be interrupted by a commercial break, they let their feelings be known.



The announcement went down like a lead balloon, with an audible groan sweeping across the auditorium as some of football’s biggest names were forced to wait even longer.

Scott was forced to announce another break later in proceedings which was also met with audible frustration.

The reaction to the ad breaks was just one of many incidents on a chaotic evening, with the ceremony delayed by 45 minutes after heavy traffic and huge crowds outside the venue disrupted arrivals.

Fans watching from home were equally unimpressed, with one writing on social media: “Not the entire room groaning at an ad break lol.”



Another sarcastically complained: “There’s some random awards in my commercials can they fix this”, while a third joked: “Damn this whole event could have been an email.”

The interruptions came as football’s biggest stars gathered for the 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or, being held in London for the first time to commemorate Sir Stanley Matthews winning the inaugural award in 1956.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Barcelona wonderkid Lamine Yamal was among the early winners, collecting the men’s young talent award for the third consecutive year.

His Barcelona team-mate Vicky Lopez scooped the women’s equivalent for the second year running.

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente was crowned men’s coach of the year after guiding his country to World Cup glory, while Barcelona manager Pere Romeu claimed the women’s award.



Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon and Barcelona’s Cata Coll were also recognised for their performances between the sticks.

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka received the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work, while Barcelona were named women’s club of the year and Paris Saint-Germain took the men’s prize.

And the winner of the biggest prize of the evening was Harry Kane, who won the Ballon d’Or.

He is the first English winner since Michael Owen won the award in 2001.

Sports.title: Who is Harry Kane’s wife Katie and how many children do couple have?
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY Kane won this year’s Ballon d’Or, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to football’s biggest individual prize.

His wife and childhood sweetheart Kate has been by his side for some of the biggest moments of his career.



Who is Harry Kane’s wife Kate?

Kate Kane (nee Goodland) was born on January 21, 1993, and grew up in Walthamstow, London.

A sports science graduate and professional fitness coach, she’s also a social media star boasting an impressive Instagram following of almost 382k as of October 26, 2026.



Harry proposed during a holiday in the Bahamas in 2017, and they tied the knot in the summer of 2019.

He celebrated the joyous occasion by posting a photo of their big day on Instagram along with the caption: “Finally got to marry my Best Friend! I love you.”

How many kids do Harry Kane and Katie Goodland have?

Kate and Harry share four kids together – daughters Ivy and Vivienne, and sons Louis and Henry.

In January 2017, they announced the arrival of firstborn Ivy with a moving social media post.

They shared a sweet snap of themselves both kissing Ivy’s head, which was captioned: “Our beautiful baby girl Ivy.”

She later shared more details with her Insta followers, saying: “Our beautiful hypnobirthed [sic] baby girl Ivy.



“Being a first-time mum, I was very scared about labour and was recommended to try hypnobirthing [sic].

“We had an amazing water birth with no pain relief or gas and air and Harry was an incredible birthing partner.”

In August 2018, Kate and Harry revealed the birth of Vivienne on X, captioning the post: “Our beautiful addition to the family! Vivienne Jane Kane.

“So proud of @KateGoodlandx for having the most amazing water birth with no pain relief at all.”

Sons Louis and Henry followed in December 2020 and August 2023 respectively.



Following the birth of his youngest, the England captain posted on Insta: “Welcome to the world Henry Edward Kane. 20/8/2023. Love you baby boy!”

The couple also have two dogs, Brady and Wilson, named after NFL quarterbacks Tom Brady and Russell Wilson.

The family relocated to Germany following Harry’s move from Spurs to Bayern Munich.

It was a family affair for the England captain when he finally celebrated getting his hands on some silverware.



Katie, their three older kids, Harry’s brother and mum and dad were all on the Allianz Arena pitch as he lifted the Bundesliga Meisterschale on Saturday, May 10, 2025.

Speaking to Esquire, Harry said of Katie: “She’s seen my whole career. Of course, she’s finding it a little crazy.

“I think she’s even been in the papers a couple of times walking the dogs.”

How did Harry Kane and Katie Goodland meet?

Katie and Harry attended the same schools in east London: Larkswood Primary and Chingford Foundation School – the latter also famously attended by David Beckham.

They started dating as teenagers after attending their school prom together.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Harry told the Standard: “If I were single now and meeting people, you’d never know if they were with you for the right reasons.

“Is it the money? You’d never really know. So, I’m lucky that I’ve got a childhood sweetheart.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or as emotional star’s voice cracks as he becomes first England ace to bag award in 25 YEARS
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE has been named as the winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

The Bayern Munich star had an incredible year for club and country last season, scoring 61 times in 51 appearances for the German giants alone.



And the star striker got incredibly emotional as he accepted the prestigious honour with his voice cracking as he delivered a powerful speech paying tribute to his Bayern and England team-mates.

Kane said: “I’m almost speechless, luckily I have this list. First of all thank you to French football, the Ballon d’Or this amazing event being in London as well looked a good omen for me so thank you very much.



“Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year, [with] some of the incredible players I was up against – some of my team-mates [and] world class players in the room tonight.

“Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees, an impressive showing of what hard work and determination can achieve, so well done. My Bayern Munich team-mates – I’ve got a few here tonight, without you it wouldn’t have been possible.

“The way you guys have pushed me, the way we compete, against Upa [Dayot Upamecano] in training every week, it just makes me want to improve.

“Vincent [Kompany], I know he’s at home, still in the hospital so wishing him very well. Hope this has given you a bit of energy and all the staff, the way we train, the way you push us you’re a credit to yourself.



“Since I’ve been with you I’ve improved as a player and improved as a person, as a leader, through your leadership. To the Bayern Munich chairman, presidents, I know some of you couldn’t be here tonight but it’s an honour to play for Bayern Munich. To represent you is a real privilege so I’m glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich for sure.

“To all of my England team-mates, Bukayo [Saka]’s here representing England and, again just saying, we had a special year. It wasn’t a perfect year but we had a lot of good moments, built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness in the way we trained and the way we played.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“The togetherness in the hotel and the World Cup. Yeah it was truly an honour to captain you, it makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us. To Thomas Tuchel and the staff, again – the leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired. To represent the England badge the way you do.”



Kane didn’t forget Tottenham, where he burst onto the scene in 2013 and went on to carve up a glittering ten-year stint that saw him becoming the club’s record goalscorer.

The Spurs legend added: “I wanna say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur as well. I wouldn’t be where I am today without Tottenham for sure. I was here from 11 years old.

“All the guidance, all the coaches. You allow me to live my dream so, for sure, without all those moments together, all the ups and downs along the way from that journey has led me to that journey here today so just want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur.

“To all the fans – Bayern Munich fans, England fans, Spurs fans – and all my fans around the world, a lot of you in this room tonight, the support you give me in the stadiums, around the place, wherever it may be, on social media, I appreciate it all.

“I remember being a fan years ago, what it means to be a footballer. It’s been a dream of mine so any time I can give back to you guys it’s a real honour and a privilege to do so.”



Kane’s wholesome speech didn’t leave anyone out as he named the people that helped him reach the top of the world.

The England great said: “I wanna give a shout out to some of my coaches who have helped me along the way.

“Bradley Allen, Chris Ramsey, Tim Sherwood, Ryan Mason is here tonight, one of my best friends, Kenny Jackett, Russell Slade, Harry Redknapp, Mauricio Pochettino, Jose Mourinho and Antonio Conte and then Roy Hodgson, Gareth Southgate and of course my two manages, Vinny [Kompany] and now Thomas.



“All of you played a big role in my development, all at different stages in my life and without each and every one of you I wouldn’t be sat here today.

“For sure I learnt lots and found myself with the best people and with the best coaches it only improves you as a person and as a player so thank you very much.”

Kane topped an incredible Top 10 in the Ballon d’Or rankings that saw Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe finish second, while Barcelona star Lamine Yamal came third.

Rodri and eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Lionel Messi completed the top five.

Paris Saint-Germain pair Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Ousmane Dembele followed as sixth and seventh respectively.



The Top 10 was completed by Manchester City superstar Erling Haaland, Kane’s Bayern team-mate Michael Olise and Fabian Ruiz, who won the Champions League with PSG and World Cup with Spain.

Kane’s incredible achievements in front of goal were recognised, as he became the first Englishman to secure the award in 25 YEARS.

Liverpool star Michael Owen was the last to seal the title in 2001, becoming the second-youngest player ever to do so at the age of 22 years and four days.

Owen beat competition from Raul, Oliver Kahn and David Beckham to take the glory after helping Liverpool to their historic domestic treble in the 2000/01 season.

But Kane was up against potentially even stiffer competition, with LaLiga superstars Yamal and Mbappe hot on his heels going into the event at the London Palladium on Monday night.



Yamal especially had quite the claim, helping his Barcelona side to the Spanish title while featuring heavily in Spain‘s triumphant World Cup campaign in July.

However, the Barcelona superstar didn’t leave the capital empty handed as he won the Men’s Young Talent of the Year award for a third consecutive year.

Yamal wasn’t the only Barca star to snatch gold as the club’s women’s manager Pere Romeu won Women’s Coach of the Year and his star players Vicky Lopez and Cata Coll won Women’s Young Talent of the Year and Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year respectively.



And the winger’s Spain manager Luis de la Fuente won Men’s Coach of the Year as he led the Furia Roja to their second World Cup, just two years after beating England in the Euro 2024 final.

Athletic Bilbao star Unai Simon was part of De la Fuente’s world champions and that is why he won Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year.

And the big day for Spain was capped off with London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas being named Women’s Ballon d’Or winner.

But Kane’s CV was hardly shabby, being the main man in a Bayern side that completed the domestic treble this season under Vincent Kompany.

He followed that up by joining up with his England team-mates in the US to captain Thomas Tuchel‘s side in the US.



His leadership – and his six goals in seven games – helped the Three Lions reach the semi-final before going out in heartbreaking fashion to Lionel Messi‘s Argentina.

England has a special relationship with the Ballon d’Or, which was first presented in 1956 by French outlet France Football.

The award is voted on by one member of the press from each of the top 100-ranked Fifa member nations.

The inaugural winner of the award (then called the European footballer of the year) was English Blackpool star Stanley Matthews, who beat Real Madrid legend Alfredo di Stefano to the accolade.

It was in his honour that Monday’s event, marking 70 years since his triumph, was held in London for the first time – having been held at the Theatre du Chatelet in Paris since 2019.



Kevin Keegan is the other England star to have won the award, and the only one to have won twice after taking back-to-back honours in 1978 and 1979.

Sports.title: Thunder's Williams requires surgery for broken leg and dislocated ankle
Sports.content:
Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jalen Williams suffered a significant injury during their victory on Sunday

Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams will need surgery to repair a broken left fibula and dislocated left ankle after being stretchered off during their 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.

Williams - a shooting guard who entered Sunday having averaged 18 points per game in his first 250 NBA contests - has been an All-Star and an All-NBA player already in his career and was a huge part of the Thunder team that won the 2024-25 NBA title.

He injured his lower left leg and saw his ankle turn at an unnatural angle in a drive with 1:14 remaining, with Williams immediately treated by medical personnel after going down underneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end.

"Dub, as everybody knows, is as tough as they come," Thunder GM Sam Presti said at a news conference in Oklahoma City.

"He's an elite competitor. Even last night, just miraculous in terms of his outlook and the way he's looking forward to attacking this. We're going to be with him the entire way."

Williams' ankle was draped with towels before a stretcher was brought out, with players left visibly shaken by the incident and the game stopped for around five minutes before the Thunder completed their victory.

Williams looked emotional after seeing his injury before going off to a standing ovation

"Just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said in a post-match interview, fighting back tears as he spoke. "Nothing more than that."

Williams, seated up on the stretcher, saluted the cheering fans with two thumbs-up signals as he was wheeled off the court.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

It was a double gut punch for the Thunder on Monday, with the team also revealing that forward Cason Wallace will need surgery to repair a left labral tear after suffering an injury in the same game.

The timetable for Wallace's return will also be set after surgery, but such procedures typically require several months of rehabilitation. Williams was an All-Defensive team selection in 2024-25; Wallace was picked to that team last season.

"Tough night last night," Presti said. "There's no way to paint that differently. We say within our walls all the time there's a difference between being positive and being optimistic.

"Not going to sit up here and say this is exactly where we want to be or this is how we'd like to have it, but at the same time, we're extremely optimistic about the recovery for both the players. Most importantly, things could have been a lot worse."

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The Thunder have experienced major injury-related challenges in recent years, including Chet Holmgren missing the entirety of what would have been his rookie season with a foot issue.

The team's 2024 first-round pick, Nikola Topic, missed all but 10 games in the previous two seasons - first because of a torn ACL, then with testicular cancer. And Williams missed 49 regular-season games a year ago with an array of issues, mostly wrist and hamstring problems.

"We've had some tough, uniquely tough, circumstances over the last few years," Presti said. "One of the things I tried to say to the staff this morning when I talked to them was we can't get to the point where we feel like this is a common situation. But that being said, it's our situation."

"But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections.

"There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham."

England boss Tuchel and Prince William send congratulations

Image: Kane became just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or

England head coach Thomas Tuchel led the tributes to Kane, who became the first Bayern player to win the award in 45 years.

"Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon d'Or!" said Tuchel.

"I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

"To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.

"I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best - scoring goals and winning football matches.'

Prince William, patron of the Football Association, also sent his congratulations.

"What a fantastic achievement and so deserved," the Prince of Wales wrote on Instagram.

"A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments."

Chaos before Kane was announced as winner

Before Kane's win was announced, the Ballon d'Or website had published three separate articles naming Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as the winner of the 2026 men's award just hours before the ceremony.

The apparent leaks confirmed the top three for the award as chaos descended when a link emerged announcing England captain Kane had received the honour.

"A record-breaking welter of league and cup goals in 2025/26 has propelled Harry Kane to Ballon d'Or success," read the story on the official website of the prestigious France Football prize.

However, further links were subsequently found to articles hailing Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as victors.

All three versions were then taken down before Kane was confirmed to be the winner.

Sports.title: Man Utd players set to return to training with Carrick's future still uncertain
Sports.content:
Manchester United's players are set to return to training at Carrington on Tuesday - but it is still uncertain whether Michael Carrick will be in charge.

United head coach Carrick was at Carrington on Monday to watch the club's U21s take on Hull in a behind-closed-doors game.

The first-team players had a scheduled day off but Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, director of football, also met at the training base, with their talks focused on next steps following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

It remains to be seen what the United hierarchy, which includes Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the part-owner, will decide.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why the problems at Manchester United run deeper than just the manager

United's defeat to Bournemouth saw Carrick drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench after he questioned his tactics following the 4-1 Champions League loss to Como. It extended United's winless run to eight games across all competitions.

Carrick has overseen United's worst start to a Premier League season. They are 16th in the table, with seven points from their seven games, and just one point adrift of the relegation zone.

Carrick was initially appointed as United boss in January 2026 on a contract until the end of the season, following Ruben Amorim's sacking earlier in that campaign. He delivered a brilliant run of results, winning 12 of 17 matches to earn a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

Carrick was nominated for Premier League Manager of the Season and, in May, signed a new contract running to 2028.

How a 'strange day' at Carrington unfolded

Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan:

"It's been quite a bizarre, strange day at Carrington. This morning, we saw director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada arrive quite early. A few players were in receiving treatment on injuries. Captain Bruno Fernandes, Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko were all in.

"Michael Carrick arrived just before 2pm. From what we understand, he was here to watch the U21s take on Hull City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dave Reed looks at the potential replacements for Michael Carrick if he leaves Manchester United

"It paints quite an awkward picture. On one end of the car park at Carrington you have the academy building, where Carrick would have been watching the U21s' game, while on the other side you would have had Wilcox and Berrada discussing his future as well as what is the future of Man Utd, what are the next steps potentially in the head coach position.

"As far as we know, no talks between Carrick and Wilcox happened. It's quite tough when you look at the timeline because the game will have finished around 4pm.

"We saw Wilcox leave Carrington around 4.30pm. We understand Carrick left around 4.45pm. Would they have had talks today? It remains to be seen.

"Carrick's future remains in huge doubt and there's no further clarity on whether he will continue or not."

Why there hasn't been swift action on Carrick's future

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following their humiliating home loss to Bournemouth, Gary Neville unleashed on Manchester United's players for their recent performances

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"I thought this would happen pretty quickly. The fact it hasn't happened makes me think one of two things are going on.

"Probably the most likely is Man Utd's bosses are taking their time to consider who they want as a replacement. The worst-case scenario for Man Utd would be if they sacked Michael Carrick and the person they went for didn't want the job, or they couldn't agree a deal with them and they were left in limbo for days, possibly weeks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick was applauded off the Old Trafford pitch following defeat to Bournemouth - but the same could not be said about the Manchester United players

"We know it happens in football all the time - clubs try to set up a replacement before they get rid of the incumbent.

"The second thing is they are very conscious - and it was made clear to them at Old Trafford - just how popular Michael Carrick is among the Man Utd support.

"The same thing happened with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021 - he gave the most incredible departure video, despite being sacked by Man Utd.

"The club wanted to make sure it ended amicably. I think Man Utd bosses are thinking the same thing here. There might not be an exit video from Carrick but they want this done humanely and respectfully.

"If they don't, the backlash from supporters could be even stronger."

Sports.title: From forgettable EFL loans to Ballon d'Or winner - Kane's 'Cinderella story'
Sports.content:
From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale.

"This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports.

"He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking, 'Are we talking about the same kid?'

"There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further.

"I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest."

The Bayern Munich striker has become the first English Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years and just the fifth in its history.

The last English winner, Michael Owen, had a simpler route to the top, winning it aged 22 in 2001, just four years after his senior debut at Liverpool.

Kane's win has come at the age of 33, some 15 years after his senior debut on loan at Leyton Orient in League One.

"I think we have to highlight his journey," says Sherwood, who Kane thanked on stage when collecting the Ballon d'Or.

Image: Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or at a ceremony in London

"Even when we go back to Michael (Owen), he was a superstar as a kid, and he got the opportunities at a very young age at Liverpool, which is a giant football club.

"Kane came through the hard way, really. He was a player who wasn't universally loved.

"He's not like a Max Dowman, for instance, who is a superstar at 16 years of age.

"He (Kane) struggled to get some game time and to get a manager to really, really buy into what he had."

Kane even mentioned his tough path to the top in his Ballon d'Or acceptance speech.

He said: "My journey wasn't straightforward; I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now."

For Sherwood, it was those low-key loan spells at Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester that have turned Kane into the world's top player.

"I hear a lot of people talking about failed loans," he says, "but we never felt like that because we felt that him playing in U21 football was a waste of time.

"They were really good loans, and those loans were the reason why we've got a player like that."

Kane's 'sliding doors' moment

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at all of Harry Kane's Bundesliga goals for Bayern Munich last season

Kane was out in the cold at Spurs until Andre Villas-Boas' sacking, when Sherwood's subsequent arrival opened the door.

He handed Kane his first-ever Premier League start - and the then-20-year-old took his chance as he scored the opener in a 5-1 home win over Sunderland in April 2014.

"He wasn't getting anywhere unfortunately," Sherwood says. "He wasn't around the first-team squad, so I suppose it's a sliding doors moment that I managed to take over until the end of the season and I managed to give him a stage where he could perform."

And perform he has.

Kane has hit nearly 550 goals for club and country to become Tottenham's record scorer, England's all-time scorer, England's leading World Cup scorer and the top English scorer in Champions League history.

His incredible goalscoring feats hit new heights last season as he plundered 73 goals in all competitions.

Sixty-one of those came for Bayern in all competitions, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues last season. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.

For Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher, Kane's £100m move from Spurs to Bayern in the summer of 2023 has allowed him global recognition and respect.

"It's a move he needed to make," Carragher tells Sky Sports.

"I thought he might be obsessed with the Premier League goalscoring record, but he's obsessed with goalscoring records, not just that one.

"But it also gives him a great chance of winning the Champions League and being involved in Ballon d'Or selections.

"There's no way Harry Kane could've won the Ballon d'Or if he was playing for Tottenham."

'Kane is an example to all young kids'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Kane's best 'clutch' moments for Tottenham and Bayern

The Bayern move has delivered the trophies Kane so desperately craved.

Despite winning three Premier League Golden Boots at Spurs and becoming their all-time top scorer, personal honours were never the aim of the game for Kane, according to Sherwood.

His trophyless career at N17 is what drove Kane to join Bayern, where he has won back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a German Cup.

"The boy loves Tottenham," Sherwood says. "He wanted to win there, but he was winning individual accolades at Spurs, and it wasn't enough for him.

"When we all grow up, we all want to be footballers, and we don't want to be footballers because we want to be rich. There are possibly some players like that now, but that certainly wasn't his motivation.

"He wanted to go to a team that could win, and he picked Bayern, and we have to say it's been a good choice."

Sherwood adds: "He's a 100 per cent team man. If I told you he would rather win the Champions League and the Bundesliga title than the Ballon d'Or for himself, that would be the truth.

"Not every player would say that, but I genuinely believe that that is the measure of the man and that's what you're talking about, and that's why he's such a dream to manage.

"The work rate and the example he shows to any young kids coming through, and to genuinely go around the houses to try and make it, and he certainly made it."

Is Kane England's greatest-ever player?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett debates whether or not Kane is the greatest England player of all time

Kane continues to break record after record in Germany.

He is the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, has the most goals in his first 100 Bundesliga appearances and is the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goal contributions.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Kane score his 150th Bundesliga goal for Bayern Munich

It is that last stat where Kane has proven he is more than just a goal scorer. His excellent vision, awareness and superb passing range make him an exquisite playmaker.

This was on show recently in Bayern's 2-2 Champions League home draw against Arsenal as Kane, who spent much of the game dropping deep, sumptuously set up Alphonso Davies for an equaliser with a pinpoint ball from inside the centre circle.

His assist ability has been on display for years, where at Spurs he claimed the Premier League Playmaker of the Season award in the 2020/21 campaign.

So, does his all-round game combined with his records and this Ballon d'Or prize make him England's greatest-ever player? Not for Carragher, who puts a fellow English Ballon d'Or winner ahead of him.

"I would still always put Bobby Charlton as the greatest England player ever," he says.

"He's won the World Cup. He's won the Champions League with Manchester United. As a midfield player, he was the leading goalscorer for a very long time for both United and England.

"I'd still always say Bobby Charlton, because right now this England team, even though it's been a golden period for us, Harry Kane and the others still haven't got their hands on a trophy, and that's what Bobby Charlton did."

Could Kane return to Spurs?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kane has previously revealed he no longer feels the need to return to the Premier League

Kane, who needs just one cap to become England's most-capped player, and although there are plenty of trophies to be won, Sherwood believes there is a longer-term goal in Kane's thinking.

"I believe he will come back for that individual accolade to be the Premier League top scorer in the future, maybe in a couple of years' time," the ex-Premier League-winning captain says.

Kane is 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's all-time Premier League record of 260 goals.

"He will only come back to a team he believes can win," says Sherwood. "At the moment you're looking at Man City with the troubles they've got, so Liverpool possibly, that could be a chance for him.

"Tottenham could be in the frame if they start progressing. Manchester United could be in the frame, but they've got a long way to go to prove that they can win anything as well.

"I'm not sure it's ever going to be Chelsea or Arsenal because of the Tottenham connection.

"So, it's on a positive note for Tottenham fans if they can start progressing and you can prove to him that he can come back and he can possibly have a good chance of winning at your club as he will have at Liverpool, Man Utd and Man City - but we don't know what's going to happen with them - then there's an opportunity he might come back and see out his career where he started it."

It seems a fitting final chapter in Kane's Cinderella story.

Sports.title: Fearnley retires injured to give Fery victory at Vienna Open
Sports.content:
Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury after losing 5-1 in the first set against Arthur Fery to give his fellow countryman a place in the second round at the Vienna Open.

Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss.

Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz and Arthur Fery reflect on winning the Laver Cup with Team Europe

Fery will face the winner of No 6 seed Francis Tiafoe and Lorenzo Musetti - the latter of whom he lost against in straight sets at the US Open - in the second round.

Dart extends winning run in Guangzhou Open

Image: Harriet Dart continued her winning streak

Harriet Dart maintained her winning form at the Guangzhou Open in China as she beat Russian qualifier Tatiana Prozorova 6-4 2-6 6-2 to reach the second round.

Dart, who also came through two qualifiers, will next face Uzbekistan's Polina Kudermetova or Indonesia's Janice Tjen in the last 16 after winning a see-saw battle against world number 123 Prozorova.

Both players struggled to hold serve, but the British number five broke three times in the decider to open up a 5-2 lead and served out to seal victory in two hours and 15 minutes.

Stojsavljevic, 17, who won the girls' US Open singles title at the 2024 US Open, was broken twice in both sets by the world number 19 after being given a wildcard into the WTA 500 tournament.

Sports.title: Careers on the line for Australia in deciding South Africa Test?
Sports.content:
Australia are about to play a Test match in Cape Town for the first time since the ball-tampering scandal back in 2018 that paused a number of their cricketers' careers.

Should they lose to South Africa this week in the series decider, live on Sky Sports Cricket, a number of careers could be ended.

Having been humbled by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha last time out, a game in which they were torpedoed for 99 in the first innings, the Baggy Greens need a response.

If that does not come, the reaction from the Australian media could be more abrasive than the piece of sandpaper Cameron Bancroft aimed to conceal down his trousers eight years ago.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In 2018 footage emerged of Australia opener Cameron Bancroft using a foreign object to alter the condition of the ball against South Africa

The batting has been creaking for a while.

In the 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, it was held together by Travis Head, Steve Smith and Alex Carey as others toiled, while in South Africa so far the tourists have managed only three individual fifty-plus scores - one for Head and two for Matt Renshaw.

Without Head in Durban, things would have been even grislier. His second-innings 121 was 81 more runs than the next highest score by an Aussie in the game.

Even the great Smith - who received a ban for the role he played as skipper in 'Sandpapergate' in 2018, along with Bancroft and David Warner - has stuttered: three innings' in the 20s and a knock of three.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Smith was dismissed by Marco Jansen in the first Test at Durban after being rapped on the gloves

He was hampered by a neck problem in Gqeberha and faces a late fitness Test ahead of the winner-takes-all Cape Town finale.

If he fails that, it could aid Marnus Labuschagne's hopes of staying in the side.

Labuschagne and selector Bailey under big pressure?

Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting had branded Labuschagne's spot as "untenable" after a lean return at home to Bangladesh left him without a Test century in 43 innings, stretching back to the 2023 Ashes in England. That has now extended to 47 innings.

Labuschagne has had no trouble starting in South Africa, the country of his birth - reaching the 30s in three of his four outings. But he has not kicked on.

Image: Australia's Marnus Labuschagne has not scored a Test century in over three years

Pinned lbw. Sliced loosely to cover. Brilliantly caught by Simon Harmer at gully. And then a criminal dismissal as he inexplicably holed out to long-on in the second innings of the second Test, a game Australia were trying to save.

If he misses out this week, it could be curtains. If he plays and fails, it could be a similar story. If Australia fail as a team, perhaps pressure will mount on head selector George Bailey?

Former skipper Steve Waugh said before the Ashes that Bailey has previously shown a lack of "appetite" to make the big calls, while the selection of the now-jettisoned Nic Maddinson for the South Africa tour was panned at the time by Matthew Hayden.

Maddinson ditching after recall highlights Australia's issues

Maddinson, 34, had not played a first-class game since March 2025 due to a testicular cancer diagnosis and averaged 6.75 from his first three Tests back in 2016.

Hayden accused selectors of "disrespecting first-class cricket" and "promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we've seen in a generation of cricket."

Image: The selection of Nic Maddinson was criticised and the 34-year old has now been dropped from the Australia squad after failing to score big runs in South Africa

Maddinson has not been as good as mediocre in this series, with his average a paltry 14 after amassing only 56 runs from four knocks - 48 of which came in one innings to punctuate a 33-ball duck, a four-ball duck and a 10-ball eight.

He has since been released from the squad, with Renshaw poised to open alongside Head in Cape Town.

Considering what he went through health-wise, people were rooting for Maddinson to perform but he hasn't. It raises the question over whether a younger player should have been given a go instead.

Ollie Davies, Sam Konstas and Campbell Kellaway were options. Nathan McSweeney, too.

The problem Australia have is that unlike in previous eras when they had players averaging north of 40 and banging out domestic runs - often in English county cricket as well as at home - waiting in the wings, they don't now.

All of the prospects mentioned above average mid-30s or lower in first-class cricket.

Will Bavuma extend excellent record as captain?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Africa captain Temba Bavuma scored a superb 179 from 334 balls in the second Test

South Africa, by contrast, have a pretty much guaranteed source of runs in captain Temba Bavuma, whose brilliant 179 from 334 balls in Gqeberha means he is averaging 49.95 across his last 28 Tests.

His nuggety ton last time out was scored after he came in at 12-2.

He was at the other end as the Proteas slumped to 110-6 before pushing them to 425-9 and was ultimately left to celebrate a 12th win in 14 Tests as skipper.

This feels like a great chance to make that 13 from 15 unless Australia are able to pull something out of the bag in Cape Town.

Unlike in 2018, something within the rules this time.

Sports.title: Harry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winner
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first Englishman to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years.

Two hours into a lavishly excitable ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, Kane’s name emerged from the final envelope to wild cheers inside the auditorium. The women’s Ballon d’Or, awarded moments earlier, was won by Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses, a third Ballon, five years on from her first in the colours of Barcelona.

In the men’s voting, Kane finished ahead of co-favourites Lamine Yamal of Barcelona and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid, an outcome that will perhaps cause the familiar consternation among the hierarchy of those clubs, not to mention the vast online fan army attached to the superstar players in Kane’s wake.

But Kane is also a fully deserving winner of football’s ultimate gong. The L’Équipe-sponsored trophy is awarded by a vote of journalists and administrators across the footballing super-scape. For Kane, it is reward for a year during which he has won the European Golden Boot, played a major role in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title, captained England to a World Cup semi-final, and above all shown himself to be a wonderfully humble superstar player.

Quick Guide Ballon d'Or: full list of winners Show Ballon d’Or  Men Harry Kane (England and Bayern Munich) Women Alexia Putellas (Spain and London City Lionesses) Kopa Trophy (under-21) Men Lamine Yamal (Spain and Barcelona) Women Vicky López (Spain and Barcelona) Yashin Trophy (goalkeeper) Men Unai Simón (Spain and Athletic Bilbao) Women Cata Coll (Spain and Barcelona) Gerd Müller Trophy (striker) Men Harry Kane Women Charlyn Corral (Mexico and Pachuca) Johan Cruyff Trophy (coach) Men Luis de la Fuente (Spain) Women Pere Romeu (Barcelona) Club of the Year  Men Paris Saint-Germain Women Barcelona Sócrates Award (humanitarian) Bukayo Saka (England and Arsenal) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“It was really tough this year, the incredible players I was up against,” Kane said as he received the trophy, going on to congratulate everyone else nominated for anything else, and thank pretty much everyone he has ever played with.

“I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special,” he added.

View image in fullscreen The Wembley Stadium arch is lit up gold in honour of Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or win. Photograph: Harry Murphy/The FA/Getty Images

As a pure goalscorer, his numbers are astonishing this year, with 89 goals for club and country since the start of August 2025. At Bayern, Kane has also become a darling of the Bundesliga for his all-round game, creativity, intelligence and professionalism. Bayern paid a record €100m fee up front for Kane three years ago, a transfer that broke the club’s usual recruitment patterns and raised some concerns, given Kane was 30 at the time.

It is a measure of his contribution on and off the pitch that this outlay is now seen as entirely vindicated. As a Ballon d’Or winner, Kane now enters rarefied company, heir to a prize that revolved around the Messi-Ronaldo two-hander for so many years, and which promises not just a form of sporting ultimacy but a vast uplift in current and future commercial earnings.

More widely, the award is a coronational moment for Kane himself, 16 years into a professional career that has taken in loan spells at Leyton Orient and Millwall, running himself into the ground to make it in the Premier League, and now, for posterity, into the lineage of elite footballers.

Earlier this month, Kane equalled England’s all-time caps record, while nudging his international goal tally on to 91 in 125 appearances. Aged 33, he still has a home Euros two years from now in his sights as England’s captain and a final opportunity for a different kind of footballing immortality.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fate
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday afternoon as elsewhere at the ­Carrington base Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar ­Berrada, the chief executive officer, deliberated over whether to sack the head coach.

Carrick arrived at 1.50pm to watch the under-21s play a behind‑closed-doors game.

Wilcox and Berrada met at Carrington early on Monday morning after United’s 3-0 defeat against ­Bournemouth on Sunday at Old Trafford that left Carrick’s job in the balance. Wilcox departed just before 5pm and Carrick left shortly after.

The defeat made it eight games without a win for Carrick’s side, who have two victories all season. United are in 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation zone.

If the 45-year-old Carrick is removed, Eddie Howe remains ­Wilcox’s preferred candidate, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle ­manager is open to taking up the position, ­subject to negotiations.

Howe, 48, would be less expensive to recruit than Unai Emery, another admired manager, because Aston Villa would demand around £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.

Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.

Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, is another who may be in the frame.

Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth defeat for what he claimed were “pure football reasons”. This came after the 32‑year‑old criticised Carrick for his tactics in the 4-1 capitulation at Como in the ­Champions League last Wednesday. The United captain was an unused substi­tute and was booed, along with other players, by fans in the ­Stretford End at the end of the defeat against Marco Rose’s side.

On Monday Fernandes liked an ­Instagram post that said: “Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.” The post also said: “The person holding everything together is usually the one nobody thinks to check on.”

Ineos, which is owned by ­Ratcliffe, has reportedly put FC ­Lausanne‑Sport up for sale. Ineos declined to comment when contacted by the ­Guardian. ­Lausanne-Sport are bottom of the top division in Switzerland.

Sports.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation
Sports.content:
England abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1.

Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. He is believed to have alleged an opponent called him a “monkey” and raised a complaint with the coaching staff, prompting England’s head coach, Matt Thorpe, to approach the referee.

Thorpe was seen asking the referee to come over before instructing his players to leave the field. One of England’s assistant coaches subsequently told the referee: “We are reporting racism”, adding that the team did not want to continue playing.

When another official approached to discuss the next steps, the assistant coach reiterated that England’s players did not want to resume the match. He also said a player was upset by the incident. Footage later showed heated exchanges between members of the coaching teams, with representatives from each side saying they were seeking to protect their players.

“Fifa is aware of an incident at the Under-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland,” said a spokesperson for world football’s governing body. “The match was abandoned by the referee following England’s refusal to continue.”

The spokesperson said the official reports were being collected and that the matter would be referred to Fifa’s independent disciplinary committee, which would decide on any further action.

The Football Association has not commented, but is understood to be waiting for more information. It is said to be taking the matter seriously and providing support to players and staff. The Football Association of Ireland has been contacted for comment.

The inaugural Under-15 World Cup involves 189 countries and territories. Games are played in an eight-a-side format on smaller pitches, with two 20-minute halves.

England, who had won their three previous matches against Cambodia, Montenegro and Nicaragua, faced Zimbabwe later on Monday, while Ireland were due to play Cambodia. Only the group winners will progress to the top-tier competition this week, with the rest of the teams divided into separate tiers depending on where they finished.

Before the tournament, Fifa described it as “unrivalled in scale or ambition”. More than 3,000 players are taking part in 950 matches, with each team playing a minimum of nine games. Arsène Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, described it as giving “players from across the world the chance to compete, to learn and to grow”.

Sports.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager. Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it.

But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically?

It’s worth remembering where all this began. The United story has taken on the aspect of a classical tragedy and, like all good tragedies, it begins with a small, seemingly unconnected moment, amplified by pride, that ends up bringing the whole edifice crashing down.

In 1999, Mull of Kintyre, a horse owned by the Irish millionaire John Magnier, won the Gimcrack Stakes at York. Traditionally, the winning owner would give a speech at the Gimcrack Dinner, but Magnier was a shy man who hated public speaking so he asked his friend, the United manager Alex Ferguson, to give the speech on his behalf. The racing establishment, though, refused: it had to be the owner. To spite them, Magnier named Ferguson as the owner of another horse, Juniper. The following year, Juniper was narrowly beaten in the Gimcrack Stakes. Magnier, though, was determined. So the year after that, he made Ferguson the owner of Rock of Gibraltar, which had won its first three races. Rock of Gibraltar won the Gimcrack easily and Magnier, waving a metaphorical two fingers at the racing authorities, watched Ferguson give the speech.

Magnier was largely making mischief, but he was also happy to do a favor for a friend, to give Ferguson a better experience of racing, and he benefited from the association of the horse with such a famous name. In addition, Ferguson did not get on well with the United chairman, Martin Edwards, and had a sense that football clubs were becoming good investments. Accordingly Magnier and his associate JP McManus bought shares in United. (The full story is explored by the journalist David Walsh here).

It turned out, though, that Rock of Gibraltar was a much better horse than anybody had realized, winning seven Group One races in a row. The stud fees would be worth tens of millions of pounds. Ferguson believed the verbal deal was that he could choose 50% of the prize money won by Rock of Gibraltar (about £800,000) or 50% of the stud fees, which ended up being worth tens of millions. He went for the latter. Magnier’s recollection was rather different: 5% of the prize money or one stud nomination a year.

Ferguson sued and, with his name on the ownership documents, probably would have won had it gone to trial. But then rumors started to spread about some of Ferguson’s financial dealings at United. Paid actors at United’s annual general meeting raised awkward points, then Magnier and McManus sent a list of 99 questions to the United board, which mysteriously found their way into the Daily Mail. United were highly embarrassed. Fans began to demonstrate against Magnier and McManus at race meetings. A settlement was reached, with Ferguson paid £2.5m to drop the action. But the damage was done.

Magnier and McManus had decided to sell their shares in United, and another shareholder was ready and waiting: Malcolm Glazer. Ferguson backed Glazer, who launched his leveraged buyout. Magnier and McManus sold up in 2005 for £260m, a profit of a little under £100m. Had they waited for Ratcliffe, who bought a similar stake in 2024, they would have received roughly £1bn more than that. For Ferguson, a threat had been dealt with.

The problem was that Glazer and his family would prove some of the worst club owners in English history. For 20 years, United have been addled by debt and have made consistently terrible footballing decisions. Ferguson’s team was good enough, and his personality big enough, that United won five league titles and a Champions League after the takeover, but once his genius had gone, there was nothing left.
