A mismatched squad built up over seven flawed managerial appointments and a multiplicity of conflicting approaches will not readily be sorted out. Carrick is the latest victim of a crisis 21 years in the making. For the want of a horse a club was lost.

Sports.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
José Mourinho had already done the por qué?, the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists.

He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out.

“We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but none of us cried because Thibaut couldn’t play,” Mourinho said. Plenty might have felt like it, more reason to be fearful. But the coach called Andriy Lunin, the substitute goalkeeper so serious that he bought a roll of artificial turf and spent the pandemic diving round the living room of his flat, and told him this was his moment: “You train to play, not to sit on the bench, so go on.” As for the rest of them, the manager told them nothing changes: the plan remains in place. By the time they headed back to the dressing room, “Fucking get in!” echoing along the Camp Nou corridor, so it had proved.

Thirteen years later, Mourinho was back in Barcelona for a clásico and he had guided Madrid to a 2-1 win. It wasn’t supposed to be like this, or maybe it was. Barcelona, the team who had won nine in a row, banging in 4.3 goals per game, had been beaten by Madrid, the team who had lost twice already and, truth be told, were mostly just not very good. The night it could have been all over, the title race done when it’s not even in November, was instead the night it finally started. “If you leave here nine points behind, it’s very heavy psychologically; if it’s six, it’s more balanced; if it’s three, that’s different,” Mourinho said.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho returned to where it all began to continue his unbeaten streak against Barcelona. Photograph: Joan Monfort/AP

This was different, and so is the season now. Counting the clásicos all those years ago, Mourinho racked up his sixth consecutive meeting with Barcelona without defeat, and there had been no parked bus, nor many lumps kicked. They didn’t just desperately hang on, although there was a moment when Dean Huijsen saved a shot with his face. Nor had they just waited for a moment, resisting and then robbing it, even if João Cancelo did insist: “That’s Madrid; they don’t have many chances but they score them.” The final shot count said 18-10 to Barcelona, and possession was 62% Barcelona’s.

“The way we won is important: you can win luckily or by defending a lot. But we won with calmness and totally deservedly. We did it by being organised, concentrated and having the courage to come out from the back,” Mourinho said. And if that might have been pushing it a little – and, let’s face it, the analyses might be different had Lunin not made an astonishing save from Gerard Martín or Lamine Yamal’s second-half shot not faded just past the post – he had a point.

Barcelona were not at their best. They had been hurried and imprecise, Rodri telling his teammates to lower their “pulse rate” as they came out for the second half. Lamine Yamal somehow missed an extraordinary chance just before the break. And when they did tighten the screw in the second half, they couldn’t break the wall. Xavi Espart was forced off, yet another injury at the back, the failure to sign a centre-back in the spotlight again. Yet this was still a faster, more aggressive, tighter Madrid than anyone expected. Asked to define it, Lunin went for “discipline and attitude”. And if that is partly about occasion, the least you can ask for, it’s more than you sometimes get.

View image in fullscreen Andriy Lunin stepped up for Real Madrid in the absence of the ill Thibaut Courtois. Photograph: Jose Breton/AP

Besides, it was also more than that. More than Marc Cucurella getting under Lamine Yamal’s skin, although he certainly succeeded. They went for the space beyond Barcelona’s full-backs: superb in his first clásico, aged 19, Yan Diomandé – the left winger – got more touches than any Madrid player, and protected his full-back as well. But it was more than that, too. More than the wonderful winning goal, a flash of inspiration with Jude Bellingham going all Nureyev, the ball flitting between his feet and Gabriel Jesus’s legs, pirouetting to release Eduardo Camavinga. This was a team with an idea and a victory that vindicated their manager, some kind of resurrection.

Before the game, Rodri said that one of Madrid’s tricks is to convince you that they’re not that good, but insisted he wouldn’t fall into that trap. Still he felt that plan particularly. Pedri did too. Bellingham dealt with Rodri, Bernardo Silva with Pedri. Pressed and tired too, according to Hansi Flick, neither truly took control. The inclusion of Arda Güler and Silva – the surprise in the middle, starting his first league game in six weeks – underlined an intention for Madrid to keep the ball when they could. They actually had a midfield, which was new. From the back they tried to build, draw Barcelona in. And if a time came when they had to wait, to put bodies in before the ball, well, they would do that too. Six times Barcelona shots were blocked. At least twice more, shots were taken from their toes. At the other end, meanwhile, Madrid attacked with an intent and an incision that probably drew the clearer chances: the xG showed 1.19 v 1.94.

Quick Guide La Liga results Show Alaves 1-1 Malaga, Rayo Vallecano 0-3 Elche, Racing Santander 2-1 Espanyol, Valencia 1-2 Villarreal, Atlético 1-0 Deportiva A Coruna, A Bilbao 4-0 Getafe, Celta Vigo 0-0 Real Betis, Real Sociedad 2-1 Levante, Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid Monday: Sevilla v Osasuna Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Victory puts Madrid three points behind Barcelona and, Federico Valverde claimed, “will give us a kickstart”. It has taken 10 weeks but it’s game on. Hay liga, as they like to say. There is league. There is Madrid, too. Something has shifted, starting in Rome, where 70 dreadful minutes gave way to 20 pretty good ones, another inexplicable comeback actually having something of an explanation, too. The changes were impossible to ignore. Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni no longer the partnership in the middle, Valverde going to right-back instead. Güler playing. Diomandé playing. And, yes, Vinícius Júnior not playing. “I’m not stubborn; I can change,” Mourinho said. Madrid have won five in succession now; something was seen that night, a way ahead. They’ve won every game since Vinícius was suspended, facile and perhaps even cruel though that may be to say. And since Mourinho grew a beard, if you believe in that kind of thing.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé celebrates the goal that leaves Real Madrid only three points behind Barcelona in the league. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

Before the clásico, Mourinho had said it wasn’t fair to compare his team, a side in construction and a long way from the finished product, to Barcelona. He insisted that he was still getting to know his players; he hadn’t been there long, after all. After the clásico, he admitted: “We have improved, we can’t hide that.” The idea has shifted, almost like it was an epiphany: “I’ve learned something about the middle of the pitch; I have learned that a mixture is better, that it is better to have a combination of qualities than two players of similar characteristics.” In short, Tchouaméni and Valverde doesn’t work. There needs to be some football in there somewhere, and so a shift started. Sunday came as a kind of confirmation, a hope, an identity emerging.

“The best Madrid is born at the Camp Nou,” ran the headline in El País. “Madrid are here now,” AS’s cover said. “I won’t let them have their heads on the moon; if we win this and then don’t win at the Sardinero, it won’t mean much,” Mourinho said, but this was a start, not just an end in itself. At full time, Mourinho headed on to the pitch and shook Lunin’s hand as all around players embraced. High in the north-east corner, Madrid’s fans stayed and sang. Back home, Courtois was watching. He had “a horrible night” on Saturday, they said, but now he was feeling a little better. They all were.

Sports.title: Davide Ancelotti wants to make a name for himself – will he do it at Lille?
Sports.content:
In a restaurant in Rio de Janeiro, two aspiring young managers sit around a table. Their respective clubs, Flamengo and Botafogo, are fierce rivals on the pitch. The relationship between the managers of the two clubs, Filipe Luís and Davide Ancelotti, however, is significantly more cordial.

Speaking before his first meeting with Ancelotti in Ligue 1 on Sunday, the Monaco manager, Filipe Luís, described his counterpart at Lille as a “really formidable person”. The Brazilian added: “It is something special for us. It will be a pleasure to face my friend.”

There were 12 managerial appointments in Ligue 1 over the summer; Filipe Luís and Ancelotti were two of the most interesting. Filipe Luís won the Premier League with Chelsea but is probably best known in Europe for his eight years at Atlético Madrid, where he won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and two Europa League titles across two spells. He carried on that success in his first job as a manager, winning the Copa Libertadores with Flamengo. “He knows what he’s talking about and how to motivate us,” says the Monaco forward Matthis Abline. “It motivates us even more to have a manager like him behind us.”

Davide Ancelotti has had a different route into management. When your surname is Ancelotti, you can’t exactly make a name for yourself; his father, Carlo, has already seen to that. “I hope to be able to write my story, with my first name, too,” said Davide before Lille played in the Champions League earlier this season. No manager has won more titles (five) or managed as many games (218) in the competition as his father.

Bar a brief 33-game stint as manager at Botafogo, Davide has spent the last 14 years following his father from club to club and then ultimately to the Brazil national team. From the banks of the river Mersey, to Bavaria, the fervour of the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, the grandeur of the Bernabéu and the vibrancy of the Maracanã. His trip around the world was enriching but he was always in the shadows. Until now.

View image in fullscreen The former Brazil defender Filipe Luís was appointed Monaco manager in the summer. Photograph: Manon Cruz/Reuters

Ancelotti’s appointment over the summer marked a radical departure at Lille. There was a common thread linking the club’s appointments of Christophe Galtier, Jocelyn Gourvennec, Paulo Fonseca and Bruno Génésio: they were all “a safe pair of hands” and most had considerable experience in Ligue 1. Génésio left Lille in the summer after his contract expired even though he had met the club’s key objective of qualifying for this season’s Champions League. The club’s president, Olivier Létang, simply said it “was the right moment” for a parting of the ways.

Unlike the wider public, Létang was at least familiar with Davide Ancelotti thanks to their time together at Paris Saint-Germain in 2012. Carlo Ancelotti was manager at the time, Létang was the director of football and Davide was the fitness coach. Létang did, nonetheless, use Carlo as a middleman when making his approach for Davide this summer. Carlo has even observed Lille’s start to the season from the stands, attending a draw with PSG in August.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Monaco 1-1 Lille Angers 0-0 Lorient Auxerre 1-1 Le Mans Marseille 4-3 Le Havre Rennes 3-0 Strasbourg Toulouse 0-0 Troyes Brest 1-2 Nice Lens 2-1 Paris Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Lille have lost all three of their matches in the Champions League this season and sit second from bottom in the 36-team table but, after their 1-1 draw at Monaco on Sunday, they were just one point behind the Ligue 1 leaders, Rennes. The point earned at the Stade Louis II took Lille’s tally to 15 points from eight games; they have not started a domestic campaign this well since they won the title in 2020-21.

Comparisons to his father are unfair but they are inevitable; the expectations on Davide have been moulded by two decades of his father’s unprecedented success. And it will always be extremely hard, borderline impossible, to live up to them. Every game is seen as proof of hereditary genius or – as had sometimes been the case in the opening weeks – its absence.

View image in fullscreen Ethan Mbappé gives Lille the lead at the Stade Louis II on Sunday. Photograph: Philippe Magoni/AP

The game on Sunday did not offer much evidence of genius. Ethan Mbappé gave Lille the lead from the only clear chance of the first half. Thereafter, they retreated inside their shell. Even before Tanguy Nianzou was sent off for a reckless challenge on Paris Brunner, Monaco had them under the cosh. Ancelotti’s decision to take off a striker in the form of Soriba Diaoune for a defender in Isaac Cossier reflected the manager’s infectious fear.

Lille could not hold on for the win and, in the end, they nearly lost the game. Monaco equalised through Edan Diop with 15 minutes to play and had numerous efforts during a late siege. One side dominated, but the points were shared. In the absence of any clear identity, Ancelotti praised his side’s “solidarity”. For signs of who Davide is beyond the son of the most prolific manager in Europe, the wait goes on. He is out of his father’s shadow but not yet truly in the light.

Talking points

There was no “headline” fixture in France on Sunday night. The game between Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon was postponed until Monday. As was the case last year, it means that many of PSG’s nine Ballon d’Or nominees will miss the ceremony in London. Their absence last year was the result of a storm, which led to their game in Marseille being delayed by 24 hours.

Unlike in the provincial cities, the planned protest in Paris on Saturday was not banned. With a significant police presence in the capital in an attempt to prevent a recurrence of last week’s riots and looting, and an NFL game to host on Sunday afternoon, the prefecture issued the directive, later adopted by the French league, on Friday.

There was further disruption. Elsewhere in Ligue 1, Toulouse’s home game against Troyes was moved from Saturday to Sunday. In Ligue 2, Montpellier’s game against Red Star was moved from Saturday to Monday. There wasn’t the same degree of disruption in Saint-Étienne, who nonetheless delayed the kick-off of their game against Nantes by 45 minutes following a police directive.

Another year, another call for bids for Ligue 1’s broadcasting rights, the value of which has plummeted in recent seasons. Dazn pulled out after just one season in 2024, giving rise to the Ligue 1+ experiment. The league-owned broadcaster, now in its second season, has been an editorial success but not a financial one. As a result, the president of the French league, Vincent Labrune, has announced a fresh auction for Ligue 1’s broadcasting rights, which will begin next month and end in December.

The prospective deal would begin at the start of next season. Labrune spoke of a “new context” and one more conducive to bigger offers. Recent changes in legislation mean that the rights can be sold in a single “bundle”, offering the option of exclusivity to any prospective buyer. Without citing any broadcasters, Labrune also revealed “registered concrete interests from different actors”. Ligue 1 cannot afford another botched deal.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
Sports.content:
Will derby win kick-start Arsenal’s season?

The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack

Match report: Tottenham 1-2 Arsenal

Godfrey a star in the making

View image in fullscreen Freya Godfrey of London City Lionesses Photograph: Clare Overfield/SPP/Shutterstock

Is Freya Godfrey England’s future? That’s what Alexia Putellas thinks of her London City Lionesses teammate, and the Spain icon heaped praise on the 21-year-old winger after she scored in her second consecutive WSL game. Godfrey – who made her senior England debut earlier this month against Greece – capitalised on a Khiara Keating mistake to score in the 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday and her all-round display delighted Putellas, who told Sky Sports: “She can arrive where she really wants. I always tell her, she’s a star girl. She will be the future of this club. She has to keep working like she is doing now. She will be the future of England as well as the present.” TG

United show progress under Olid

Manchester United’s display in Sunday’s derby draw was night and day compared to their most recent previous home league fixture against a title challenger, when they were torn apart in a 5-0 defeat at home against Chelsea just six weeks ago. Against Manchester City on Sunday they competed toe-to-toe with the defending champions, and while it would be wrong to suggest that Eva Olid’s team are anywhere near the finished article, their improvements are striking, both with and without the ball. Olid feels that heavy defeat early in her tenure actually helped her side. “It was a hard week after Chelsea but sometimes you need a difficult moment to happen, to react and see exactly where the problems [were] or the things we had to solve as a team,” she said. “It had to happen to now be the team we are.” Tom Garry

Match report: Manchester United 1-1 Manchester City

Birmingham earn first win of WSL return

Birmingham’s first win of the WSL season came in the first encounter between league newcomers this season. Following an impressive point at the Emirates the week before,the 1-0 win over Charlton marked another key step as Amy Merricks’ side continue to settle into the top flight. The Blues were almost made to pay for their profligacy in front of goal against a familiar foe from last season in WSL2. They dominated proceedings and created 20 chances in total but registered just five on target. Océane Hurtré and Lisa Naalsund rattled the crossbar while Lily Crosthwaite missed three gilt-edged opportunities before Wilma Leidhammar struck a 68th minute-winner. “That was the most important thing today,” Merricks said. “We needed to pick up three points and we delivered that. I don’t think the performance was our finest. You could feel the caginess across the pitch and that is something we need to work on. We are in a better place, and we keep pushing.” Sophie Downey

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Depth the difference as Chelsea produce comeback

View image in fullscreen Melvine Malard displayed her class as Chelsea despatched Crystal Palace. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

For 51 minutes on Sunday afternoon, it felt like it might just be one of those days for Chelsea. Despite dominating the first half – they created 12 opportunities to Crystal Palace’s four and registered 20 touches in the opposition box – they found themselves trailing and running out of ideas. A key difference between the two sides, however, is the strength in depth available to their respective managers. In bringing on Erin Cuthbert and Sandy Baltimore at half-time, Sonia Bompastor was able to call on the services of two experienced internationals. Cuthbert added a crucial bite to the midfield that had been lacking in the first half while Baltimore set up Melvine Malard to put the Blues in front before scoring from the spot to confirm the three points. In contrast, Jo Potter made just three substitutions with the first coming in the 77th minute. It is this ability to change things from the bench that truly illustrates the gap in class between the eight-time WSL champions and the league newcomers. SD

Sørensen makes statement against former club

Brian Sørensen and his Aston Villa side came away with a 3-2 win against Everton. Sørensen, who took over from Natalia Arroyo last month, faced the Merseyside club for the first time since his Goodison Park exit in February. Villa dominated the clash and went 3-0 up within 50 minutes thanks to goals from Noelle Maritz and Amalie Vangsgaard, but they were given a scare following a late comeback push with Holly McNamara and Noémie Mouchon both scoring. Villa saw the game out to take three points – just. Nevertheless, Sørensen will be thrilled with the outcome, especially as it moved his team up to eighth. It also marked the first time since the 2024-25 campaign that Villa have won back-to-back games. “I’m happy, it was overall a good performance,” the interim head coach said. “Of course, maybe they got a bit too excited at the end but I also think we had the opportunities to kill the game off a lot sooner. But three points is three points, that’s all that matters.” Emillia Hawkins

Symonds’ stunner inspires Brighton win

Maisie Symonds’ stunning strike set Brighton on course for a 3-0 victory over West Ham. The Brighton captain broke the deadlock in the 29th minute, meeting a headed clearance with a first-time strike from distance that swerved beyond West Ham goalkeeper Constance Picaud-Inconnu and kissed the post on its way in. It was her second goal of the season, rewarding Brighton’s early dominance. Fran Kirby doubled the lead in the 63rd minute before Kiko Seike struck three minutes later. Brighton’s head coach, Arturo Ruiz, called it his side’s “most complete” performance of the season, praising their confidence and tactical adaptability. Symonds said Brighton “got control” in the second half. It was the Seagulls’ first Women’s Super League clean sheet of the campaign. Mitul Samji

Sports.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net.

Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist.

What a difference it makes to this Napoli team when their Scottish star is fit and firing. McTominay was out of action for all of September, recovering from an ablation procedure to correct an irregular heartbeat – known medically as an arrhythmia. The condition was characterised by the club as mild and benign, and the medical intervention a complete success.

Napoli had struggled in McTominay’s absence. They continued to struggle right after his return, too. His first two starts back in the side came in defeats to Villarreal and Serie A’s last-placed team, Venezia – leaving the Partenopei with five losses from their first nine games in all competitions. The latter result prompted speculation about whether Massimiliano Allegri’s job as manager could soon be at risk.

A week later, McTominay is starting to change the narrative. His two goals in midweek helped Napoli to their first Champions League win of the season, 4-3 against Bodø/Glimt. On Saturday, he broke his Serie A duck and did everything in his power to deliver another win over undefeated Roma.

McTominay’s three-strikes-in-one had made it 2-0 in the 48th minute, building on Frank Anguissa’s glorious overhead opener. Perhaps McTominay’s willingness to attempt the audacious has been rubbing off on his Napoli teammates too, though the Cameroon international was a title-winner and essential figure before the Scot arrived in 2024.

View image in fullscreen Frank Anguissa succeeds in the spectacular to give Napoli the lead in the first half. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/AP

They could have been further ahead on Saturday. Mathías Olivera had a point-blank effort hacked off the line when the score was 1-0 before half-time. Then again, Bryan Cristante hit the post for Roma moments later.

McTominay’s goal appeared to put Napoli fully in control, until Matías Soulé swapped a one-two with Donyell Malen and picked out the bottom corner brilliantly from outside the box. That was the 69th minute, and Roma were level by the 74th, their centre-back Leonardo Balerdi crashing home from a corner.

And so McTominay answered again, with a wicked finish of his own from almost 30 yards. He matched Soulé’s precision after Roma had failed to clear their lines from a Leonardo Spinazzola attempt, tucking his shot inside the near post.

Against lesser opponents, that might have been the end of it. But Roma are not easily beaten under Gian Piero Gasperini. In the 89th minute, Wesley crossed and Balerdi arrived to head home another equaliser.

It finished 3-3, a marvellously entertaining game, with so many stories to tell. On the Roma side, this felt like a big night for Soulé, the 23-year-old Argentina forward delivering one of the statement performances of his Serie A career to date in a stadium named after Diego Maradona.

Signed from Frosinone in the summer of 2024, Soulé has shown glimpses of immense potential but struggled for consistency, leading to questions about whether he can truly become more than Paulo Dybala’s understudy. But this season, and in the last month especially – which began with a first senior appearance for Argentina, then two assists in a heart-breaking Champions League defeat to Real Madrid – he is stepping ever more confidently from his compatriot’s shadow.

“He’s in his prime, he’s the driving force of this team,” said Gasperini at full-time. “[Donyell] Malen didn’t have a great game, and [Soulé] carried the team. His goal was something crazy; the foot and leg speed reminds you of something [Leo] Messi would do.”

View image in fullscreen Matías Soulé’s goal reminded his manager of ‘something Messi would do’. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/AP

And then there is Balerdi, also Argentinian, on loan from Marseille with an option to buy. Gasperini noted how one of Roma’s strategies in the transfer market had been to target players perceived as leaders for their previous clubs. He named Marten de Roon in this category, too, and it was the Dutchman, wearing the captain’s armband, who put in the cross that led to Balerdi’s first goal.

Unsurprisingly, given how the match unfolded, Gasperini seemed content with the draw. Allegri rather less so. He was sent off after Roma’s third goal and though he claimed not to know why, he was later overheard outside the changing rooms insinuating that the opposition had received favourable treatment from the referee. La Gazzetta dello Sport reported him protesting that: “Last year they handed you [Roma] the Champions League and I paid for it at Milan.”

Without relitigating a year’s worth of decisions, this was a bold line to take. Milan, who spent almost the entire campaign in the top four and much of it as the closest contender to Inter for the scudetto, contrived to miss out on the Champions League by a single point after collecting only seven from their final eight games.

Allegri cut short an interview on Dazn, saying that he was “for the first time in 25 years, not lucid enough to expand on this game”. Another claim that might raise a few eyebrows, from a man who once got halfway to undressing in frustration at the officiating of a final that his own team won.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Torino 3-2 Monza, Cagliari 0-2 Bologna, Como 2-0 Sassuolo, Napoli 3-3 Roma, Lazio 2-1 Parma, Inter 2-1 Fiorentina, Atalanta 4-4 Frosinone, Genoa 1-0 Venezia, Lecce 0-2 Juventus, Udinese 0-2 Milan Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Perhaps his ire on this occasion would have been better directed at one of his own defenders. During the buildup to Roma’s final goal, Sam Beukema collapsed to the floor after tussling with Balerdi off the ball. A generous reading of the replays would be to say that he “made the most” of some contact, which appeared to be arm-on-arm, though the Napoli player went down clutching his rib cage.

If Beukema had stayed on his feet and continued marking Balerdi, perhaps the equaliser could have been avoided. Instead, he got up too late to do anything about it and then fell back to the floor again after watching the goal go in.

An undignified end to a brilliant game. As frustrated as Napoli might feel at throwing these points away, there were lots of positives here to hang on to. Only a week ago we were asking whether Kevin De Bruyne could be persuaded to occupy the deeper role Allegri sees for him and make space for McTominay further forward. In this game, and the win over Bodø/Glimt, there were positive signs.

Putting three goals past this Roma team – who had only conceded that many in the previous seven games of this Serie A season combined – is no mean feat. Napoli with McTominay are more than capable of improving on their current 10th place in the table and at least competing for a top-four spot.

The challenge is to stay lucid, as McTominay did on his triple goal, sticking at a task until it is completed. And perhaps a little longer to make sure.

Sports.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or as he beats Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to ultimate prize
Sports.content:
Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or as he beats Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to ultimate prize

Harry Kane has won the Ballon d'Or at the award ceremony in London on Monday evening.

The Bayern Munich superstar has become the first Englishman to win the prestigious trophy in 25 years.

6 Kane is the fifth Englishman to be crowned the world's best player with Michael Owen, Kevin Keegan, Bobby Charlton and Stanley Matthews coming before him Credit: Getty

Michael Owen was the last England international to claim the award in 2001, with Kane joining him in the history books.

"I'm almost speechless. (Luckily) I have this list here," Kane said upon receiving the award. "Thank you to France Football, to the Ballon d'Or for putting on this amazing event. Being here in London has made it extra special. It looked like a good omen for me tonight so thank you very much.

“Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was really tough this year, some of the incredible players I was up against, some of my teammates, some world-class players in the room tonight."

Kane went on to thank his Bayern Munich teammates as well as manager Vincent Kompany, continuing: “The way you guys push me, the way we compete, me against (Dayot Upamecano) in training every week, it makes me a better player, makes me want to improve.

“To Vinny (Kompany), I think he's at home or still in the hospital — wishing you very well and hope this has given you a bit of energy.”

And the club where it all began for him and where he became a legend, Tottenham, also got a shoutout.

He said: “I want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur. I wouldn't be where I am today without Tottenham.

“I was there from when I was 11 and the club and all the coaches helped me to live my dreams and all of those memories and those ups and downs have led me to where I am today.”

Kane finished by saying: “It's an honour to play for Bayern Munich. To represent you is a real privilege and I'm glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich for sure.

“To all of my England teammates — Bukayo (Saka) is here tonight representing England — again the same. We had a special year. It wasn't the perfect year but we had a lot of good moments.

6 Kane scored six goals at the World Cup and has 91 goals for England overall Credit: AFP

“We built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness, the way we trained, the way we played, the togetherness in the hotel at the World Cup.

“It was truly an honour to captain you, lead you, it makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us.”

Kane's magical 2026

The 33-year-old scored a stunning 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England combined during the 2025/26 season.

He won the Bundesliga title at club level, breaking endless records as well as lifting the German Cup and German Super Cup, while also captaining the Three Lions to the World Cup semi-finals.

54 goals from his incredible tally have come in 2026 alone, along with 13 assists in all competitions for Bayern.

Mbappe and Yamal miss out

Second-placed Mbappe missed out on a career-first Ballon d'Or despite scoring 58 goals in 60 games in the 2025/26 season.

6

6

The Real Madrid superstar also won the Golden Boot at the World Cup this summer as France reached the semi-finals, becoming the tournament's all-time top scorer.

He didn't win a single trophy last term, and has been beaten by Kane at the ceremony.

At 19 years old, Yamal could have become the youngest winner of the Ballon d'Or ever after winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, although he did claim get a consolation prize in his third successive Kopa Trophy.

Yamal won the La Liga title and Spanish Super Cup with Barcelona, scoring 25 goals and providing 20 assist in 2025/26.

His success with La Roja on the international stage in the USA did not give him the edge over his competitors.

2026 Ballon d'Or awards winners

There were a series of other awards handed out during the ceremony with Alexia Putellas winning the Women's Ballon d'Or prize, this being her third crown.

6 Putellas won the Women's Ballon d'Or for the third time Credit: AFP

6 Kane's England teammate Bukayo Saka claimed the Socrates Award, a prize given to players for their humanitarian work Credit: Getty

Kane also won the Gerd Muller Trophy, the award given for the best men's striker in the game, with Mexico's Charlyn Corral winning the female equivalent.

The first award of the night was given to Yamal, who won the Men's Young Talent of the Year prize for a third year running. Fellow Spaniard and Barcelona star Vicky Lopez won Women's Young Talent of the Year.

There was more sweeping success for Spain with Unai Simon winning the Men's Goalkeeper of the Year award and compatriot Cata Coll named Women's Goalkeeper of the Year.

It was Spanish glory with the coach awards too; Spain men's boss Luis De La Fuente and Barcelona women's manager Pere Romeu emerging victorious.

Barcelona won the Women's Club of the Year but the Men's Club of the Year was given to Paris Saint-Germain having retained their European crown for a second season running.

There was another English winner in Arsenal star Bukayo Saka, who claimed the Socrates Award for his work with the BigShoe charity, which funds medical surgeries for children.

Sports.title: Man United owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe puts other club up for sale as Red Devils fans turn on INEOS
Sports.content:
Man United owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe puts other club up for sale as Red Devils fans turn on INEOS

Sir Jim Ratcliffe has put Swiss club Lausanne-Sport up for sale after nine years as owner.

INEOS, who own a minority stake in Manchester United, bought Lausanne back in November 2017.



3 Lausanne-Sport have had a mix of success and failures under INEOS Credit: Getty

Lausanne had been home to the company's headquarters between 2010 and 2016.

Ratcliffe subsequently completed a takeover of the seven-time Swiss champions nine years ago.

Having won promotion back to the top-flight as champions in their first full season as owners, Lausanne-Sport were relegated again in 2022.



However, they returned at the first time of asking and have remained in the Swiss Super League since.

Following their promotion, they have finished tenth, fifth and ninth in the division.



Lausanne-Sport also reached the knockout stage of last season's Conference League, with their league phase campaign including a win over Fiorentina.

The Blue and Whites currently sit bottom of the Swiss Super League table, though, with just one win from their opening 11 matches.



Their poor start to the season has now been followed by the news INEOS are looking to sell the club.

United fans turn on owners

It comes amid growing discontent amongst United supporters towards the club's owners.

Ratcliffe purchased a 27.7 per cent stake in the Red Devils in February 2024 to become a shareholder alongside majority owners the Glazer family.

3 Lausanne-Sport are currently bottom of the Swiss Super League Credit: Getty



However, supporter protests against the owners have become commonplace at Old Trafford in recent seasons.

Those have continued into the current campaign amid United's on-pitch woes.

Following Sunday's home defeat to Bournemouth, one fan even admitted he would not care if the club were relegated in order to get rid of the current owners during an impassioned call to talkSPORT.

The Red Devils are currently 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone, as well as winless in their last eight matches in all competitions.



INEOS' sports ownership

INEOS' decision to put Lausanne-Sport up for sale follows a similar move over their ownership of French side Nice.

The Ligue 1 outfit are also open to takeover bids, but have seen their asking price slashed to £209.5million.

3 Ratcliffe and INEOS have been minority owners of United since 2024 Credit: Getty

Ratcliffe bought Nice in 2019, with the club qualifying for Europe four times and reaching two Coupe de France finals in the seven years since.



INEOS have also exited their sponsorship deals with the New Zealand rugby union team and Tottenham Hotspur in 2025.

They are also no longer tied to Sir Ben Ainslie's America's Cup sailing team.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe told to take Man United job on one huge condition
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe told to take Man United job on one huge condition

Eddie Howe has been told to 'stay clear' of the Manchester United job unless one request is met.

The former Newcastle boss is among the contenders to succeed Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.



3 Howe has been urged to turn down United if his requests are not met Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands United are set to sack their current under-pressure manager.

Dressing room insiders expect Carrick to leave the club following Sunday's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

The setback followed a humiliating loss to Como in the Champions League last week.



talkSPORT subsequently revealed technical director Jason Wilcox was leaning towards appointing Howe if Carrick was sacked in the wake of that defeat.

Should Howe accept United job?

Gabby Agbonlahor has now urged Howe to only consider taking the job on one condition.



The talkSPORT co-host believes he should be appointed, but must only accept an offer if he is given all the power he wants.

Speaking to Andy Goldstein on Drive, Agbonlahor explained: "The problem we've got now is that he dropped Bruno Fernandes and look how bad they were still.



"I've seen Bruno Fernandes liking something on Instagram earlier where it was a little dig about loyalty.

"They know it is untenable now with Michael Carrick. He has to go, but if I'm Eddie Howe, what a position I'm in.

"You definitely have to take the job, but I'm saying I'm taking it. But you know what? I want the control that Unai Emery's got at Aston Villa. I want the whole package.

3 Howe is a leading candidate to replace Carrick at Old Trafford Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"I want promises that in January that I can buy this, this and this. These idiots that are in the squad, put them in the Under-10s, let them train with the kids.

"Give me everything I want and I'll take the job. If you don't get that Eddie Howe, stay clear of it."

Agbonlahor's comments come after Jeff Stelling urged Howe to steer clear of the job.

Meanwhile, Carrick's imminent departure comes after he dropped Bruno Fernandes for the visit of Bournemouth.



The Red Devils captain was an unused substitute against the Cherries.

It was a move which followed Fernandes' criticism of the tactics in the defeat to Como.

3 Carrick is expected to be sacked by the Red Devils Credit: Getty

As for Howe, he is currently without a club after leaving Newcastle in July.

The 48-year-old spent almost five years in charge at St. James' Park.

During that time, he twice qualified for the Champions League as well as winning the Carabao Cup.



That triumph ended the club's 70-year wait for a major domestic trophy.

Sports.title: Martin Keown and Alex Crook in heated clash live on air over Man United crisis
Sports.content:
Martin Keown and Alex Crook in heated clash live on air over Man United crisis

Manchester United's ongoing crisis prompted a fiery exchange live on talkSPORT on Monday morning.

The Red Devils' problems deepened on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

4 Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook clashed with Martin Keown live on air amid United's ongoing crisis Credit: talkSPORT

United are now winless in eight matches and talkSPORT understands dressing room insiders expect Michael Carrick to be sacked as manager.

Amid the issues facing the club, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook joined Sam Matterface, Martin Keown and Dean Ashton on air.

Crook and Keown clash amid United crisis

Having provided an update on Carrick's future, though, he quickly became embroiled in a heated back-and-forth with Keown.

The exchange stemmed from the former Arsenal defender asking Crook about his status as a United supporter.

Keown said: "Alex, not to blow your cover, but you’re a Manchester United fan, aren’t you?"

"Why are you not in the camp of the fans applauding Carrick off the pitch?"

Carrick was applauded off the pitch at Old Trafford by the home crowd, who had booed the United players at half-time and full-time on Sunday.

Crook replied: "I am. How do you know I'm not?" before Keown added: "Well, you just want change. You want him out."

In response, Crook said: "I didn't say that," only for the former England international to continue: "You implied that."

As their back-and-forth raged on, Crook reiterated: "I said my information as a journalist is there’s going to be a change, whether I think that’s the right or wrong decision, I think it’s inevitable."

4 Keown questioned Crook's stance on Carrick's United future Credit: talkSPORT

When asked what he thinks United should do next, he explained: "I don’t think Michael Carrick is the biggest issue at Manchester United.

"I don't think the manager has ever been the biggest issue at Manchester United.

"I think the Stretford End conducted themselves with great dignity yesterday, making their feelings towards a club legend, someone who clearly has put his all into this job, very clear and also voicing their disdain for a group of players who week in, week out, let them down, not just the fans, but the manager himself as well.

"He won’t say it, Michael Carrick, because he’s too much of a diplomat. He still cares too much about the football club. He will feel hurt by the performance of this season.

"How can you go from beating everybody around you last season to qualify for the Champions League to turning in the tripe that they are this season, that lack of effort, that lack of endeavor, that lack of accountability?"

Keown was not finished, though, as he responded: "So you’re separating the manager.

4 Crook accused Keown of 'putting words' in his mouth during their exchange Credit: talkSPORT

"You’re looking at the iconic player and not looking at the manager that you see before you now."

Crook then hit back, saying: "Why are you putting words into my mouth, Martin? I’m not going to say that."

The exchange then concluded with Keown adding: "But you are. That’s what it seems like.

"If we’re in the dressing room, taking you into the dressing room, it’s not an us and them situation.

"If we win, we all get the credit. If we lose, then it’s all of our fault. Everybody."

Latest on Carrick's future

As of Monday evening, Carrick has not been sacked by the Red Devils.

4 Carrick is expected to be sacked by United Credit: Getty

However, club officials expect the former United midfielder to be relieved of his duties just five months after signing a two-year deal.

His squad had a day off on Monday following their heavy defeat to the Cherries, with no training session held at Carrington.

Boardroom talks were expected to take place in the morning, with a decision not yet communicated to the manager regarding his future.

Carrick was present at the training ground, though, attending an Under-21s fixture against Hull City.

He was joined by assistant manager Steve Holland and Under-18s boss Darren Fletcher.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso committed cardinal sin against Tottenham, but calls for Chelsea sack are baffling
Sports.content:
There is a tacit agreement that every Chelsea manager, head coach or interim appointment must respect - you don't lose to Tottenham.

A London rivalry that had its first fixture in 1909, the mutual loathing really kicked off in 1967 when Spurs beat the Blues 2-1 in what was the first ever FA Cup final between two teams from the capital.

6 Chelsea lost to Spurs at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 35 seasons Credit: Getty

Eight years later, Chelsea were relegated from the First Division soon after a 2-0 loss at White Hart Lane, whose residents avoided the drop by one point.

But the power eventually shifted and the Kings of the King's Road are top of their head-to-head table with 83 wins from 182 meetings, and the Lilywhites are on 56.

Chelsea have dominated since the turn of the millennium having won 41 of 69 matches, though the most recent clash on Saturday was one to forget.

Blues lose Bridge battle

Cole Palmer was sent off at Stamford Bridge as Spurs left with three points in a 2-0 victory, which is only their second away from home in the Premier League since it began in 1992.

Overseeing a Chelsea performance lacking effort from players who seemed to be unaware of the occasion's importance was manager Xabi Alonso, who made an error with his game plan before kick-off.

Joao Pedro picked up an injury the day before and was replaced by Geovany Quenda, the 19-year-old starlet who has so much potential but struggled out wide on what was his first league start.

Morgan Rogers appeared to be the focal point in attack whilst the natural striker Danny Welbeck sat on the bench until Spurs scored their second goal, by which time it was too late to make an impact.

Chelsea had just 31.3 per cent of possession, a woeful amount of time on the ball for a team who were playing at home, and a total of seven shots that their visitors bettered by eight.

During the full-time lap of applause, Levi Colwill was met with some choice words from supporters in the West Lower and encouraged to walk away from the fury by Welbeck.

It was the club's third Premier League defeat of the season and, even though they are fifth in the table and remain in the European race during Alonso's opening weeks, some fans aren't happy with him.

6 Alonso got it wrong against their London rivals and missed an opportunity to go third in the Premier League Credit: Getty

A quick search on social media will present numerous posts calling for the Spaniard to be dismissed as manager.

Some made the demand soon after the defeat to Spurs, and others believe anything but a win against a crisis-hit Manchester United this Saturday lunchtime, live on talkSPORT, is enough for the sack.

Whilst those who follow Chelsea from afar and express their views via social media are absolutely entitled to do so, they can sometimes fall into the trap of rash discourse.

Shock defeats, poor performances and questionable decisions are all catalysts for off the cuff outpourings that may be caught in clouds of emotion shortly after a full-time whistle has blown.

This can also be the case in the stands at Stamford Bridge, with those shouting at Colwill a prime example, but Alonso will have the backing of a myriad of fans who frequent the SW6 stadium for matches.

Again, those in the 'Alonso out' camp are certainly allowed to think in this way and communicate their opinions, yet a simple question must be asked for balance - what on earth would happen next?

6 Chelsea fans were furious and Colwill (right) took some of the heat, with Alonso also facing some baffling calls for the sack Credit: Getty

Calls for Alonso sacking are purely hasty

For a club who have made five permanent appointments in the head coach or manager role since BlueCo became custodians in May 2022, another change would further damage the fan-owner relations.

Thomas Tuchel was sacked in September 2022 despite winning the Champions League a year prior, Graham Potter couldn't make the step up from Brighton and ex-Spurs boss Mauricio Pochettino did not win over the fanbase.

Whilst Enzo Maresca sabotaged the 2025/26 season by throwing his toys out the pram to eventually replace Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, his successor Liam Rosenior was out of his depth.

Having finished in the bleak position of tenth, Chelsea were able to deliver a managerial coup with the hiring of Alonso.

The World Cup winner with Spain and ex-Liverpool midfielder made waves in the Bundesliga at Bayer Leverkusen as they won the 2023/24 title unbeaten, the DFB-Pokal and DFL-Supercup.

Winning one of the top five leagues in Europe cannot be overlooked, especially when there is not a single loss and the success comes in a first full season at senior management level.

6 Alonso boasts a highly impressive win record across the three clubs he has managed, especially at Madrid

Alonso was rewarded with the job at Real Madrid, where he spent five seasons as a player but taking charge at the world's biggest club is a huge leap and he left in January, despite winning 24 of 34 matches.

A 71 per cent win record is nothing to scoff at, even if his exit came off the back of Madrid's 3-2 Supercopa de Espana defeat to their bitter rivals Barcelona.

Just two months have passed since they commenced their campaign and Alonso has developed a front three of Palmer, Rogers and Pedro into a strong attacking force with a combined 13 goals and ten assists.

Chelsea are only two points outside the top four, and will be boosted towards a Champions League spot if City are to be given a massive points deduction for financial charges following their guilty verdict.

However, let's imagine a scenario where the club did decide to send Alonso packing for whatever reason - it's difficult to argue that any realistic replacements are available.

Pep Guardiola is taking a break from management and unlikely to be a candidate after spending a decade at rivals City, and Arne Slot won the league at Liverpool but had a poor title defence.

6 Julian Nagelsmann is one of the top managers currently without a club, but has already rejected a move to Chelsea Credit: Getty

Gareth Southgate has dismissed future Premier League management after reaching two Euros finals with England, whilst ex-France boss and World Cup winner Didier Deschamps is also an implausible choice.

Julian Nagelsmann turned down the Chelsea job in 2023 and is one of a number of options for United, whose targets to potentially replace Michael Carrick would most likely not come into the Blues' thinking.

Eddie Howe won the League Cup at Newcastle but is arguably a step down from Alonso, Antonio Conte left Chelsea on bad terms in 2018 and Fabian Hurzeler would be yet another hire from Brighton.

Unai Emery has gained plaudits for his work at Aston Villa but is not likely to leave, and the same can be said for Luis Enrique at Paris Saint-Germain, Hansi Flick at Barcelona and Jose Mourinho at Madrid.

Whilst the options for Chelsea look slim given the aforementioned, yet hypothetical, names are unrealistic, various fans in the 'Alonso out' camp have pointed to Cesc Fabregas as the answer.

Fabregas reunion is a no-go

He won two Premier League titles as a midfielder for the west London club from 2014 to 2019, and the 'Fabregas is magic' chant that takes aim at his ex-side Arsenal is still sung at the Bridge today.

6 Fabregas has really impressed at Como and is likely to be linked with Chelsea in the future but, in the here and now, Alonso must be backed Credit: Getty

Now at the beginning of his managerial career, the Spaniard is eyed as one for the future thanks to immense success with Como.

Fabregas not only got them promoted to Serie A in 2024, 21 years after relegation from the Italian top flight, he masterminded their first ever qualification for the Champions League.

After three games in their competition debut, Como are ninth in the league phase with two wins - 4-1 victories over RB Leipzig and United.

Chelsea naming Fabregas as their manager is not a situation that is out of the realms of possibility, whilst his fellow former employers Arsenal and Barcelona are also potential destinations in the future.

However, the 39-year-old is still relatively inexperienced and so, if he was to return to Chelsea and have a poor tenure in the dugout, then his popular reputation amongst the fans could be tarnished.

Furthermore, the club will find themselves back at square one once again, an avoidable outcome that must also be shunned in the present day.

Yes, Chelsea manager Alonso broke the tacit agreement and lost to Spurs, but relieving him of his duties so early on in his spell would be a real drop of the ball.

Sports.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch during World Cup match after racism allegation
Sports.content:
England Under-15s walk off pitch during World Cup match after racism allegation

England's Under-15s walked off the pitch during their match against the Republic of Ireland after a player was allegedly racially abused.

The Young Lions' fixture at the FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival was abandoned on Monday.

3 England Under-15s walked off the pitch during the final minute against Ireland Credit: DAZN

Head coach Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the final minute of the match following the incident.

England player alleges racist comment

According to the Daily Mail, an England player claimed an opponent had made a racist comment towards them.

It followed an altercation which saw the England youngster push a rival in the back.

After the allegation was made, a member of the Irish coaching team reportedly shouted: "No, he didn't," prompting the England player to protest back.

An argument subsequently broke out between members of staff from both benches.

Thorpe and his coaches were then approached by the accuser, who waited on the touchline whilst his manager spoke to an official.

Before the match could restart, the England boss ordered his players off the pitch.

As a result, the clash was abandoned in the final minute with Ireland leading 4-1.

FIFA statement

FIFA have since launched an investigation into the incident.

In a statement, a FIFA spokesperson said: "FIFA is aware of an incident at the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland.

3 An England player alleged a racist comment had been made towards them Credit: DAZN

"The match was abandoned by the referee following England’s refusal to continue.

"The official reports are being gathered, and the matter will be referred to the independent Disciplinary Committee who will decide in due course."

It is yet to be confirmed whether the result from the match at the time it was abandoned will stand.

Ireland currently sit a point clear of England at the top of Group C following their meeting.

The Young Lions conclude their group stage schedule against Zimbabwe on Monday, with England winning 2-0 at the time of writing.

Thorpe's side began their campaign with a 4-0 win over Nicaragua on Saturday.

3 The inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival is taking place in Azerbaijan Credit: Getty

They subsequently beat Montenegro and Cambodia 2-1 and 10-0, respectively on Sunday.

As it stands, England will advance to Tier B of the tournament stage.

This week's tournament in Baku, Azerbaijan, marks the inaugural edition of the FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival.

The event is set to run until Friday having started on Saturday.

Matches are eight-a-side and consist of two 20-minute halves.

Sports.title: 2026 Ballon d’Or winner ‘leaks’ cause fan meltdown hours before official announcement
Sports.content:
2026 Ballon d’Or winner ‘leaks’ cause fan meltdown hours before official announcement

The winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or was announced early on the award's official website...

However, fans were left confused after France Football published that Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal had all won the prestigious gong. The posts have since been deleted.



3 Kane was announced as the Ballon d'Or winner... along with Mbappe and Yamal Credit: Getty

This year's recipient is set to be officially announced on Monday night in a ceremony at the London Palladium.

The ceremony is expected to begin at 8pm, with the winner's press conference scheduled for 10:30pm.

Kane, Mbappe and Yamal are the three leading contenders for the Ballon d'Or.



The trio are amongst 30 players nominated for their performances during the 2025/26 season.

Those nominees are being placed from 30th to fourth ahead of this evening before the top three discover their fate.



talkSPORT understands Mbappe will be named as the winner of the Ballon d'Or.

Ballon d'Or winner leaked

Prior to the awards ceremony, articles appeared on the Ballon d'Or website for each player, claiming they had 'won' the award.



An article detailing Kane's 61 goals for Bayern Munich titled 'Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or' was amongst those to appear online.

The England captain won the European Golden Shoe as he fired the German giants to a league and cup double last term.

Kane also scored six goals for the Three Lions as they finished third at the World Cup, their best performance since 1966.

3 Mbappe is nominated for the award alongside Kane and Yamal Credit: Getty



He is aiming to become the fifth Englishman to win the award and the first since Michael Owen 25 years ago.

Who are Kane's Ballon d'Or rivals?

However, Mbappe's 'consistency personified at the very highest level' saw him win the Ballon d'Or, according to another article that was published on the official website.

The Real Madrid forward won the World Cup golden boot after becoming the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 10 goals this summer.

Mbappe also finished as the top scorer in both LaLiga and the Champions League last term.



Across all competitions, the France international scored 42 goals in 44 appearances for Real Madrid.

As for Yamal, the 19-year-old became a World Cup winner with Spain as well as winning LaLiga for the third time in four seasons.

3 Yamal is aiming to become the youngest-ever winner of the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

Having finished as runner-up last year, the teenager is aiming to become the youngest ever winner of the Ballon d'Or.



The current record is held by Ronaldo, who was 21 years and 96 days old when he received the award for the first time in 1997.

Yamal has previously won the Kopa Trophy, awarded to the world's best Under-21 player, in each of the last two years and talkSPORT understands he will win it again this year.

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson is one of top three strikers in Premier League – he starts for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Nicolas Jackson is one of top three strikers in Premier League – he starts for Arsenal

Is Nicolas Jackson a top three striker in the Premier League?

talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor thinks so, with the Aston Villa frontman scoring four in his last four league games.

3 Jackson has instantly hit form for Aston Villa, scoring seven goals in his first 11 appearances since joining from Chelsea Credit: Getty

Jackson, who signed for Villa from Chelsea for a club record £65million in the summer, has hit the ground running.

In 11 appearances in all competitions for his new side, he has already scored seven goals, with four strikes coming in the top flight.

His double against Manchester City on Saturday showcased just how good he can be - and after that game, Agbonlahor made a bold claim.

He asked on talkSPORT's GameDay Phone-In: "Nicolas Jackson - give me three better centre forwards in the Premier League?"

Agbonlahor firmly put him in among the best and disregarded any inclusion of Brentford's Igor Thiago in the conversation.

The ex-striker also stated that Jackson would start for Arsenal, putting him in their side over Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz.

Is Jackson one of the best three strikers in the Premier League?

After those comments, talkSPORT Breakfast host Jeff Stelling agreed with statement, saying: "I think he [Agbonlahor] is right on current form.

"Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak yeah, but who else can you argue? It's very hard to argue the case for anybody else."

Co-host Ally McCoist then added: "He [Jackson] has got a lot more composure than he's had. He can still be doing with a little more calmness in front of goal.

"But there are not a lot of strikers that are top class that really enjoying playing the role themselves and he's perfect for it, he's been terrific. Gabby's right!"

3 Agbonlahor, Stelling and McCoist all agree that Jackson is one of the best three strikers in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Jackson has found 'a natural home'

Jackson's career in England appeared to be in doubt after struggling at Chelsea and being sent out on loan last season.

He spent last term as Harry Kane's understudy at Bayern Munich, scoring 11 goals in 34 appearances in all competitions.

The Senegal international was then sold to Villa on his return to the Premier League and he is now in impressive form.

Arsenal legend Martin Keown believes Jackson lost his way at Chelsea and that now, working under Unai Emery for the second time after his spell at Villarreal, he has found a 'natural home'.

Keown said: "He worked with him [Emery] before and I think this Villa team is now unrecognisable now from the start of the season.

"Jackson, for me, is a nightmare to play against. He's robust, dynamic and he punishes you with pace.

3 Back working under Emery, Jackson appears to be finding his best form Credit: Getty

"I think the Villa faithful are delighted he's now playing for them and maybe this is a natural home for him.

"I thought he was losing his discipline at Chelsea a little bit... he was getting sent off, getting involved in silly things, he wasn't loved.

"But he has the full love now of the manager and the club and I think it's the perfect place for him."

Sports.title: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph was vindication for a superstar brimming with quiet excellence who swerves flashy controversy, writes OLIVER HOLT - and a win for English football
Sports.content:
It is July 10 2024, a couple of hours after goals from Harry Kane and Ollie Watkins have taken England past the Netherlands in Dortmund and into the final of Euro 2024. In the Dorint Hotel, the other side of a dual carriageway from the Westfalenstadion, a group of fans, some in England shirts, are sitting in the lobby bar.

They see a couple of us sitting by ourselves at another table and invite us over. It is Kane’s wife, Katie Goodland, and her family, her sister, her parents. They talk about Kane’s life in Munich and their lives in Essex, their favourite pubs, favourite places to eat. They talk a little about some of the criticism Kane is attracting but they hold no bitterness. They are lovely people. It is two hours well spent.

I thought of them when I got around to seeing Dear England, the play written by James Graham, which won rave reviews for its portrayal of Gareth Southgate as football’s answer to Jesus Christ but whose characterisation of Kane as a dolt and a bore was so crass and crudely drawn that it spoilt the play.

I thought of them when I saw Kane criticised for making the move from Spurs to Bayern Munich and then failing to win the Bundesliga in his first season. I thought of them when people laughed that he would never win a trophy.

I thought of them a few weeks ago when I read that Lamine Yamal had dismissed Kane’s claims to winning the Ballon d’Or, the sport’s most prestigious individual honour, and had fed into the star culture that pervades the game by saying the battle for it should be between him and Kylian Mbappe.

‘I honestly believe there are two of us who are the best in the world, and this year I’d deserve it because of what I’ve won,’ Yamal said in an interview clip shared by Spanish streaming platform Movistar. As far as I’m concerned, Mbappe and I are the two best in the world. It’s clear to me, and everyone who watches the matches knows it.’

Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph is a success story for football's humble superstars

The Bayern Munich and England star is a model professional as well as a superb goal-scorer

Kane thanked his wife Kate, describing her as his 'best friend' and 'my biggest supporter'

But most of all, I thought of them late on Monday night when I sat in the audience at the London Palladium in the heart of London’s West End and watched Kane walk up to the stage to take that prize ahead of both Yamal and Mbappe and become the first Englishman for 25 years to be named the best footballer in the world.

Because that moment was Kane’s vindication. It was the moment that justified the way he has conducted himself throughout a career that started with him scrapping his way through loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he nailed down a place in the Spurs first team.

‘My journey has not been a straightforward one,’ Kane said on that stage in front of an audience of yelling kids and raucous fans. 'For any young boy wanting to achieve their dreams, and hoping to learn through resilience, determination and self-belief, I hope this can give you inspiration.'

It was a pitch-perfect speech that combined the emotion that spilled out when he thanked his parents and his wife and the care and the loyalty that came with a heartfelt thank you to Tottenham for ‘believing in me and my dreams.’

It was the moment that told him that he had been right to dedicate himself to the game completely and that all the years of being a fine role model to young players in the sport and to fans who idolised something they saw in him had been worth it.

It was the moment that said that football is capable of handing the highest honours to men like him, who have not sought the limelight or courted controversy or abused their fame or hired performers with dwarfism to decorate your 18th birthday party, as Yamal is alleged to have done, but have dedicated themselves to a career of quiet excellence.

Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise. 🏆 — Harry Kane (@HKane) October 26, 2026

He received the award from Brazil icon Ronaldo after beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe

Kane, pictured embracing Women's Ballon d'Or winnger Alexia Putellas, justified the way he has conducted himself throughout his career by winning football's top individual prize

And it was the moment that told him that scoring a remarkable 61 goals for Bayern in a single season, leading England to the brink of a World Cup final and extending his astonishing goalscoring record with his country so that he now boasts 91 goals in 125 caps counts for what it should.

It is not a win for the Premier League because Kane plies his trade in the Bundesliga now but it is a win for English players. It asks more questions about Thomas Tuchel’s attempt to pin the blame on England’s World Cup exit on the poor technique of English players. In Kane and Jude Bellingham, England have players with Rolls-Royce technique.

And it is a win for English football because Kane is the ambassador for our game in the way Sir Bobby Charlton was the ambassador for our game. He is a player admired for more than just his football. He is admired for what he stands for on and off the pitch. He is a player who plays the game with respect and dignity as well as sublime skill.

‘The Ballon d’Or,’ its rules suggest, ‘is awarded based on three criteria, in order of importance: 1. Individual performances, decisive and impressive character. 2. Collective performances and titles won. 3. Class and fair play.’ Those criteria are rich justification for Kane’s win.

The truth is that for everything he has achieved, Kane has been underrated for much of his career. Because the truth is also that he is, alongside Jimmy Greaves, the greatest goalscorer England has ever produced but also a player who proves again and again that he is far more than a goalscorer.

Kane is the complete centre forward, a man who scores and scores and scores for Bayern, but whose passing ability and brilliant technique makes him stand out amid his competitors. He and Jude Bellingham drove England on and on at the World Cup in Mexico, Canada and the US last summer.

And now he is in rare company. He is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. Only four of his compatriots, Sir Stanley Matthews(1956), Sir Bobby Charlton(1966), Kevin Keegan(1978 and 1979), and Owen, have been awarded the honour. Denis Law(1964) and George Best(1968), are the only other British players to have won.

Kane was warned when he left Spurs that the move would cost him his shot at immortality because it would end his chances of overhauling Alan Shearer’s mark of 260 goals that makes him the leading scorer in Premier League history.

The striker’s move to Bayern Munich from Tottenham in 2023 has paid off handsomely

Kane is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen (right) in 2001

Those warnings may have been right but think of what Kane has gained. Think of how much he has been rewarded for that move. Maybe the chance of the league record has gone but Kane’s name is now written in football history alongside Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Franz Beckenbauer, Johan Cruyff and Zinedine Zidane.

Kane’s victory is a victory for a player who has done things the right way, a player who is not a raging narcissist like Ronaldo, a player who is understated and unassuming, a player who is the ultimate professional, who has done everything to maximise his talents and devote himself to the game and who is now reaping the rewards.

It is a victory for Spurs, it is a victory for English football, which created and nurtured him. And it is a victory for his family, whose pride in their husband, son, father and brother is something we can all share.

Sports.title: Chaotic scenes at London Palladium's glitzy Ballon d'Or ceremony as huge crowds of fans try to gain access to red carpet event to catch a glimpse of Harry Kane and Co - and a photographer gets into a spat with security!
Sports.content:
Police were forced to push back large crowds attempting to access the Ballon d'Or red carpet as the start of the marquee football awards ceremony was delayed in London. The ceremony had been due to start at 8pm at the London Palladium, but organisers were forced into a half-an-hour delay. The delay came with Ballon d'Or contenders Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe among those having just arrived at the event, amid chaotic scenes nearby. Footage shared on social media revealed that large crowds had gathered by the venue in Oxford Street in an attempt to catch a glimpse of leading sporting and showbiz names attending the ceremony. One clip showed police near the red carpet having to hold back fans, who appeared to be trying to push through barriers to gain access to the event sparking security fears. Daily Mail Sport has contacted organisers for comment. Footage shared on social media showed crowds being forced back by security as they attempted to gain access to the Ballon d'Or red carpet at the London Palladium (Source: TikTok: @winstonso7) Fans had been hoping to get a glimpse of stars including England captain Harry Kane on the red carpet Real Madrid and France star Kylian Mbappe was another star in attendance as he hoped to claim the Ballon d'Or for the first time A photographer was seen clashing with a security guard on the event's official broadcast after he was pulled back on the red carpet. (Source: DAZN) The awards ceremony – overseen by France Football – has been taking place in London for the first time in its 70-year history, with all previous editions having been held in France. The decision to stage the event in London was made to honour Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the first Ballon d'Or back in 1956. The security concerns outside the venue came as part of a chaotic build-up to the ceremony, which included a clash between a photographer and a security guard on the official broadcast. The photographer appeared to inadvertently walk into DAZN's red carpet broadcast, with the security guard seen trying to pull him away. After the security guard intervened to move him away again, the photographer could be heard saying 'stop grabbing me.' Ballon d'Or organisers had endured embarrassment in the build-up to the event after three articles were posted on their official website which each announced Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as the winner of this year's men's prize. Organisers, who were alerted by Daily Mail Sport, subsequently removed the articles and launched an investigation.
