Sports.title: Brian Norman Jr. Risks Another Setback Against Abel Ramos
Sports.content:
Brian Norman Jr. could face a dangerous test against Abel Ramos on the December 19 Devin Haney–Liam Paro card, with a loss threatening to undo his progress since surrendering the WBO welterweight title to Haney last November.

Boxing journalist Dan Rafael reports that Top Rank is planning Norman vs. Ramos for the card, which is expected to take place in San Francisco. The bout would be the 25-year-old Norman’s second fight since his defeat to Haney.

Rafael reports that Top Rank also plans to feature welterweights Tiger Johnson and Rohan Polanco. But Norman has the most to lose if the Ramos fight comes together: he’s a former champion trying to regain ground, and his proposed opponent has already shown this year that he can upset a younger fighter’s plans.

Ramos (29-6-3, 22 KOs) is 35 and has six losses on his record, but those numbers don’t tell the whole story. In February, he rallied to defeat previously unbeaten Tahmir Smalls by split decision. Smalls was supposed to be the rising fighter. Ramos turned the fight into a long night and left him with his first loss.

Norman is a more established fighter than Smalls, having already held a world title, but that doesn’t make Ramos a safe opponent. The veteran can pressure, take punishment, and keep working when a younger fighter expects him to fade.

For Norman, the danger is getting drawn into a fight at close range and spending too much time looking for one big punch. He has the power to hurt Ramos, but he’ll need to put his shots together and keep the veteran from setting the pace. If he lets rounds slip away while waiting for a knockout, Ramos could make the scorecards uncomfortable.

The setting would add another layer. Norman lost his WBO title to Haney by decision in Riyadh last November, and now he could return on the undercard while Haney fights Paro in a reported title unification.

That gives Norman a chance to put on a strong performance in front of an audience watching the man who beat him. It also gives him a direct comparison with his former opponent: Haney will be fighting for two belts while Norman takes on a hard veteran to keep his own title hopes moving.

A victory over Ramos would help Norman make his case for another major fight. A loss would be far more damaging, raising questions about where he fits among the leading welterweights after the Haney defeat.

Norman–Ramos remains a planned matchup, according to Rafael, rather than an officially announced fight. If it happens, Norman will have to get past an opponent who has already ruined one prospect’s unbeaten record this year.

Sports.title: Frazer Clarke Agrees To Joseph Parker Fight On Fury vs Joshua Undercard
Sports.content:
Joseph Parker could make his ring return against Frazer Clarke on the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard on December 11 in Cardiff, risking his remaining standing among the heavyweight elite after a lengthy layoff.

Clarke confirmed he agreed to the matchup, though communication has quieted recently and organizers have not officially announced the bout.

Parker has remained inactive since Fabio Wardley stopped him in October 2025. Facing Clarke provides immediate visibility on a massive stage, yet it offers zero margin to shed ring rust.

That defeat to Wardley halted an impressive career resurgence. Parker had forced his way back into title contention through disciplined, mobile performances against Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, frustrating both power punchers over the distance.

Those past achievements offer little protection here. Clarke possesses the size to impose himself physically, alongside an extensive amateur foundation to punish any hesitation if Parker starts slowly.

The central uncertainty centers on Parker’s sharpness. His previous run required sustained concentration across twelve grueling rounds. Following a stoppage defeat and over a year outside the ropes, replicating that form against an ambitious opponent represents a serious hurdle.

Their history stretches back to 2010, when Parker defeated Clarke in the amateur ranks in India. Clarke aims to avenge that loss, calling Parker a huge name and a great fighter in an interview with The Sun.

Clarke recently snapped a two-fight skid with an August stoppage of Lamah Griggs. Upsetting Parker would instantly elevate his profile and secure invitations to major events.

Parker’s time away also involved outside complications, including a backdated three-month suspension following a failed test for a cocaine metabolite. UK Anti-Doping subsequently cleared him for competition.

Fighting in Cardiff delivers the ultimate platform for Parker to re-establish momentum. That spotlight carries severe consequences, because a sluggish showing or another defeat under the eyes of the boxing world could permanently close the door on future world championship opportunities.

Sports.title: Vasily Lomachenko Targets Charly Suarez for Ring Return at 130.
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko is eyeing Charly Suarez for his return at super featherweight, yet defeating the Filipino contender will not settle the core mystery surrounding his comeback: How much elite ability remains after a prolonged absence at age 38?

Suarez is under consideration for his ring return. Lomachenko intends to test his reflexes under real fire prior to chasing premier targets.

“My next step, it will be a fight with a guy, maybe with a guy from the Philippines, Suarez,” Lomachenko said to Fight Hub TV. “It will be my first fight after rest, and after that, we’ll see how I feel.”

Lomachenko has remained inactive since halting George Kambosos Jr. in May 2024. He has not stepped inside the ropes at 130 pounds since 2017, introducing another variable after more than two years on the shelf.

Sharing the ring with Suarez guarantees rounds against an established contender, though any verdict requires scrutiny. Suarez is also 38 years old. Outpointing him offers limited insight into how Lomachenko handles younger, sharper champions across a full championship distance.

Lomachenko built his legendary status on dazzling footwork, spatial control, and split-second precision. He famously pivoted into blind spots, unloading clean punches before opponents could reset. If his reflexes have eroded or his legs can no longer maintain that tempo, fighters who once swung at air might suddenly connect with ease.

Taking on someone like O’Shaquie Foster represents a far steeper hazard. Foster’s slick mobility and sharp counterpunches would force Lomachenko to spend considerable energy establishing range. Looking sharp against Suarez is positive, yet it does not guarantee Lomachenko can cut the ring on Foster or match his pace over 36 minutes.

Lomachenko clearly recognizes the reality in front of him. When questioned regarding matchups with Gervonta Davis or Naoya Inoue, he urged the interviewer to pump the brakes.

“I want to do slowly, slowly, slowly,” Lomachenko noted. “I need to check my body in the real fight.”

Hitting 130 pounds again presents its own physical hurdle. After spending several years up at lightweight, dropping back to a weight class he exited almost ten years ago takes a heavier toll on an older fighter. How comfortably he makes the scale could tell us just as much as his performance under the lights.

The veteran southpaw admitted the ticking clock motivated him to lace up the gloves again instead of letting time slip away.

“One day I wake up and thinking, hey, now I’m 38 years old, and we need to try one more time,” Lomachenko said. “If it will be after two more or three years, then I will be 40, 41 years old. It will be too late.”

His team is scheduled to sit down with Bob Arum to map out the business side of the ring return. Neither a date nor an opponent has been made official.

Suarez offers a workable starting point, though Lomachenko must deliver more than just a victory to prove he still belongs among the division elite. Hand speed, foot mobility, and gas tank over the championship stretch will tell the real story.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Faces Liam Paro In San Francisco
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s new DAZN deal is getting a favorable launch: a welterweight unification against Liam Paro in San Francisco, with the Australian traveling to Haney’s home region for the opening fight of that agreement.

Mike Coppinger of The Ring reports that the WBO and IBF titleholders will meet December 19 at Chase Center. The fight has yet to receive an official announcement.

It is a legitimate unification. It also puts Haney in the more comfortable position before either man throws a punch. DAZN gets to introduce its newly signed fighter to a Bay Area audience, while Paro arrives with a belt that could make that investment look better by the end of the night.

Paro’s job is to wreck the launch.

He has done something similar before. In June 2024, he traveled to Puerto Rico and beat Subriel Matias by unanimous decision for the IBF light welterweight title. The champion’s reputation and home support failed to intimidate him.

But using that victory as proof he can beat Haney would overlook the harder comparison. Matias came forward and gave Paro opportunities to land while moving. Haney can force him to become the pursuer, making the Australian create openings rather than wait for an opponent to supply them.

That is where this fight could become frustrating for Paro. Following Haney around the perimeter would allow the American to jab, move and make relatively quiet rounds look like his rounds.

Paro needs to attack the body when Haney moves, work when they get close and avoid letting every clinch become a break from the pressure. He cannot afford to spend the first half studying a target that keeps leaving.

Haney has an obligation here, too. A new broadcast deal and two belts will generate promotion, but they cannot substitute for a performance that makes people want his next fight.

Winning narrowly while limiting the action would collect another title. Taking command against a fellow champion would give DAZN something stronger to sell.

The homecoming is arranged around Haney. Whether the night belongs to him depends on how much fighting Paro forces him to do.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Rematch Is The Only Move That Makes Sense For Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith kept his WBC light welterweight strap in Sheffield, but his reputation took a beating against Alberto Puello.

Eddie Hearn is already talking up a stadium blockbuster against Shakur Stevenson. That talk conveniently skips past the reality left inside the ring: Smith did not convince viewers he solved the man in front of him.

Domestic rival Adam Azim quickly called out the verdict, backing fans who saw the split decision as generous. Two judges handed Smith 115-113 cards, while the third had Puello cruising 116-112.

“Puello won by one round, in my opinion,” Azim told RS Boxing TV, pointing directly to Smith’s lack of urgency.

The deeper issue was how Smith faded down the stretch. Once Puello timed him, Smith went into a shell. His output cratered because every attack opened him up to clean counters.

Instead of building on early rounds, Smith spent the championship rounds fighting in a safety-first manner. He was getting outboxed right when a champion needs to close the show.

Normally, that kind of performance demands an immediate rematch. Matchroom is instead trying to fast-track Smith straight into a massive event with Shakur. The commercial angle makes sense while Smith still holds the belt, but a stadium fight cannot answer the tactical problems Puello exposed.

If Puello made Smith freeze, Shakur’s precision and defensive discipline would make every mistake punishing. Saturday showed zero evidence Smith is ready for that jump. Winning a controversial decision was not the performance Smith needed for Hearn to campaign for a fight with Shakur.

A rematch with Puello is the fight that makes sense. It offers Smith a chance to adjust, keep his work rate up, and earn an undisputed result.

Hearn can sell the official victory, but the ring tells the truth. The belt stayed in Sheffield, while the performance wrecked the case for throwing Smith in with Shakur.

Sports.title: Hearn Bets On A 49-Year-Old Floyd To Strip Ryan Garcia Of His Belt
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn picking Floyd Mayweather to defeat Ryan Garcia says far more about Garcia than Mayweather. A world titleholder at 147 pounds should never be vulnerable against a retiree closing in on 50, yet Hearn genuinely envisions Mayweather stepping off the couch to capture the strap.

“I think Floyd can beat Ryan Garcia. Maybe he’s just too old and maybe he can’t,” said Hearn last Saturday night at a press conference.

The logic assumes Floyd’s timing and defensive muscle memory can outsmart Ryan’s hand speed, even while Floyd’s reflexes and legs are knocking on fifty. That is Hearn basically declaring Ryan has no depth to his game beyond a fast left hook.

Hearn tried legitimizing the spectacle by calling it “almost like a welterweight George Foreman coming back.”

That parallel flatters the concept far too much. Foreman spent years rebuilding, stacking contenders and proving his durability before regaining heavyweight gold. A Mayweather return relies purely on nostalgia, cashing in on past greatness rather than recent proof.

The real problem is the financing of the Mayweather-Garcia fight. Domestic US promoters and traditional networks like DAZN or Amazon Prime Video cannot realistically underwrite this on pay-per-view receipts alone.

Mayweather will demand a guaranteed nine figures, and Garcia will want tens of millions. Traditional pay-per-view models are fractured, and no domestic promoter can guarantee a $150 million purse pot without bleeding cash.

The only entities capable of financing a spectacle of this scale are deep-pocketed sovereign wealth funds or a global streaming giant treating it as a loss leader. If Riyadh Season or a streaming player like Netflix decides the cultural noise is worth lighting tens of millions on fire, the checks clear overnight.

Outside of foreign state funding or a massive corporate subscription grab, traditional American boxing economics simply cannot absorb the guarantees.

Interestingly, Ryan doesn’t seem to care about the social media criticism he’s getting for pursuing a Mayweather fight. As long as millions of people tune in to complain about it, the negative perception simply feeds his bottom line.

If he knocks out an aging Mayweather, he takes credit for ending the most famous undefeated record in modern boxing history. If he loses, he lost to the consensus greatest fighter of this generation.

Sports.title: Canelo Arrives in Riyadh for Mbilli Fight: Start Time, Ring Walks and DAZN PPV
Sports.content:
Canelo returns on October 31 to challenge for the WBC super middleweight belt, live on DAZN PPV and included with DAZN Ultimate.

Canelo Alvarez arrived in Riyadh on Monday morning ahead of his October 31 fight against WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli. The Mexican challenges for a belt he previously held when they meet over 12 rounds at The Venue in Riyadh.

Mbilli had already reached Saudi Arabia. Canelo was welcomed by Faisal Bafarat, chief executive of the General Entertainment Authority, with Jaime Munguia and Rafael Espinoza among the fighters arriving alongside him.

Saturday ends Canelo’s 13-month absence from the ring. The 36-year-old has not fought since Terence Crawford outpointed him in September 2025, stripping him of his undisputed super middleweight championship.

Canelo enters at 63-3-2 with 39 knockouts, seeking to regain a title at 168 pounds. He has won championships in four divisions and twice collected all four major belts at super middleweight.

Mbilli makes his first defence of the full WBC title. The Cameroon-born, Montreal-based champion holds a 29-0-1 record with 24 knockouts, having stopped Maciej Sulecki in the opening round to capture the interim belt in June 2025.

His last fight ended in a split draw against Lester Martinez. He now faces Canelo with his championship and clean loss column at stake.

Canelo vs Mbilli Start Time and Ring Walks

The advertised running order lists preliminary coverage from 10:15 a.m. ET / 7:15 a.m. PT / 2:15 p.m. GMT on Saturday, October 31.

The PPV card begins at 2 p.m. ET / 11 a.m. PT / 6 p.m. GMT.

Canelo and Mbilli’s ring walks are listed for approximately 6 p.m. ET / 3 p.m. PT / 10 p.m. GMT, followed by the opening bell around 6:15 p.m. ET / 3:15 p.m. PT / 10:15 p.m. GMT.

The main event will not begin before 6 p.m. ET / 10 p.m. GMT under that timetable. Individual fight times remain estimates, particularly following changes to the undercard.

How to Watch on DAZN

DAZN PPV costs $79.99 in the United States. The event is also included with DAZN Ultimate, allowing subscribers to that tier to watch without a separate PPV purchase.

Undercard Changes Ahead of Saturday

Jaime Munguia faces Nikita Zon in a scheduled 12-round WBA super middleweight title bout. Their advertised slot is 5 p.m. ET / 9 p.m. GMT.

Rafael Espinoza now faces Ricardo Blandon, replacing Lorenzo Parra for the WBO featherweight title fight. The WBO approved Blandon as the substitute challenger; Espinoza’s original slot was 4 p.m. ET / 8 p.m. GMT.

Raymundo Rojas Garcia meets Reito Tsutsumi over 10 rounds at super featherweight, listed to open the PPV portion at 2 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. GMT.

Lindolfo Delgado’s planned IBF super lightweight title fight against Arthur Biyarslanov is off the card, according to reporter Lance Pugmire. Its previously advertised 2:55 p.m. ET slot should therefore no longer be treated as a confirmed bout time.

Sports.title: Hearn And Warren Let The Wolf In, Says Lou DiBella
Sports.content:
Lou DiBella isn’t buying the victory lap from boxing’s old guard over Zuffa’s early struggles, pointing out that rival promoters helped clear the path for TKO to muscle into the sport to begin with.

Shakur Stevenson walking out the door gave rival outfits an easy talking point, but grabbing free publicity does not suddenly balance a promotion’s checkbook, pack an arena, or supply the massive purse Stevenson expects.

DiBella cut through the noise to ask what these traditional promotional companies are actually gaining from the chaos.

“Is Eddie all of a sudden thriving? Does he have no worries? Is Oscar and Golden Boy great? Is Top Rank’s business getting better? Is anything changing?” said DiBella to Total Boxing.

Taking a victory lap looks hollow when signing an elite free agent immediately turns into a costly headache. Any promoter chasing Stevenson must still lock in an opponent, secure a broadcast budget, and generate enough public interest to justify the deal. Cheering because a fighter hits the open market costs nothing; financing his next outing is another matter entirely.

DiBella also turned the spotlight directly onto Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren for ushering Saudi influence into boxing.

“Who’s most responsible for letting the wolf into the hen house of boxing promotion? It’s Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren.”

Relying on external money delivered massive blockbusters, yet it built an independent power structure capable of pursuing fighters and television rights without needing the old establishment. Whining about an aggressive rival rings hollow after rolling out the red carpet for them.

Even as Zuffa hits growing pains, DiBella believes TKO still holds an edge in sheer muscle, deep political ties, and premier North American broadcast real estate.

“They still have better political and business connections. They still have the best TV deals in North America.”

Those advantages might not guarantee creative matchmaking or commercial success on their own, but deep pockets and broadcast reach give an enterprise plenty of room to absorb early stumbles.

DiBella admitted that everyone inside the sport shares blame for its fragmented condition. Still, his message lands with a thud: taking cheap shots at Dana White brings easy attention, but building a sustainable, busy boxing calendar takes real execution that no competitor can manufacture off another brand’s bad headlines.

Ghana News.title: Ghana not adequately prepared for Ebola threat — Dr Kingsley Agyemang
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament (MP) for Abuakwa South, Dr Kingsley Agyemang, has raised concerns about Ghana’s preparedness to contain a possible Ebola outbreak, warning that inadequate border health surveillance and limited public education could leave the country vulnerable.

He says the country should be doing more to strengthen its health systems and prepare communities, particularly along major entry points, as concerns grow over the spread of Ebola in parts of Africa.

Dr Agyemang, a member of Parliament’s Health Committee, said Ghana’s extensive trade and travel links with Nigeria made the threat one that could not be treated lightly.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26, he questioned the level of preparedness since he first raised concerns about the issue earlier in the year.

“Preparing for a cross-border infection is something that we all have to be very much concerned about. From where I sit, as I hinted on your network somewhere in March this year, our preparedness towards the Ebola issue has not been that rigorous, and I expect to see more. You should be worried, because you see there's a lot of cross-border trade between Ghana and Nigeria,” he stated.

Concerns over border surveillance

Dr Agyemang said the movement of people and goods between Ghana and Nigeria, including commercial transport and haulage operations, required stronger surveillance and a coordinated public health response.

He warned that frequent travel between the two countries could create opportunities for an infectious disease to cross borders, making early detection and prompt intervention critical.

“We have a lot of Ghanaians that go to Nigeria every now and then. There's a huge haulage of transactional trade between Ghana and Nigeria, and it means that we have to be on the lookout for it, and we have to prepare adequately towards that, but from what I see, I do not see that being done properly.”

The MP said Ghana should have been better positioned to respond to emerging infectious disease threats, drawing lessons from the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

“We should have been very much ahead of the game, given the ravaging effect that the COVID-19 had on our healthcare. We have a lot of learning to have learned from.”

He argued that the experience of COVID-19 should have prompted sustained investment in disease surveillance, emergency preparedness and the capacity of health facilities to respond to outbreaks.

Border communities need attention

Dr Agyemang also expressed concern about what he described as inadequate strengthening of health systems at key land entry points.

He cited Aflao, Akanu, Paga, Nkwanta and Hamile among the locations where he believed greater attention was needed to improve the country's readiness to detect and respond to a possible cross-border infection.

“This cross-border infection, I mean, if you look at our land travel, I do not see it. For instance, if you take a place like Aflao, Akanu, Paga, Nkwanta, Hamile, and others, I do not see much strengthening of the healthcare system.”

He repeated his concern about the lack of visible improvements in preparedness at the borders, saying the country needed to ensure that its health facilities and surveillance arrangements could respond effectively to a potential outbreak.

“I do not see much strengthening of the healthcare system.”

His concerns highlight the importance of disease surveillance at land borders, where health authorities need to identify suspected cases quickly, assess travellers when indicated and ensure that referral and response systems are in place.

However, the MP's assessment was based on his observations. An official assessment from the relevant health authorities would be needed to establish the current level of preparedness at the named entry points.

Public education gap

Beyond border surveillance and health infrastructure, Dr Agyemang questioned the apparent lack of public education on Ebola, arguing that people needed clear information on the disease and how to respond to a possible threat.

He challenged media organisations and health authorities to intensify awareness campaigns, saying public communication should form part of the country's preparedness strategy.

“I believe that your network is among the 1% networks in Ghana. Have you played any commercial or any health promotion on Ebola? Have you seen anything run? Not yet. All the municipal and district health directories, there does not seem to be any activation or promotion of Ebola.”

He said the apparent absence of sustained public education was worrying, given the potential consequences of an outbreak and the importance of helping people recognise symptoms, seek medical care promptly and follow public health guidance.

“There has not been much promotion, and it is very concerning. If the whole multimedia has not played a commercial that seeks to promote Ebola or how we should behave, then it is really troubling.”

Dr Agyemang's remarks place the spotlight on the need for timely, accurate public information alongside preparedness measures at ports of entry and health facilities.

Public education on Ebola should be based on guidance from health authorities, with clear information on symptoms, transmission, when to seek medical attention and how suspected cases should be managed.

Ghana News.title: Ballon d’or 2026: Harry Kane wins ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal; first Englishman in 25 years
Ghana News.content:
Harry Kane has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the award in London on Monday.

Kane scored 73 goals in a breathtaking 2025-26 season across all competitions for Bayern Munich and England, enough to earn him the European Golden Shoe award.

In Germany last season, Kane inspired Bayern to a Bundesliga and DFB Pokal double. His 14 goals in the Champions League last season -- where Bayern fell at the semifinal stage to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain -- was bettered only by Kylian Mbappe of Real Madrid(15).

He captained England at the World Cup where they finished third, their best result since winning it in 1966, scoring six goals along the way including two late strikes to rescue his side against DR Congo and a strike against Mexico at the Azteca in the round of 16.

This season, Kane equalled a record held by Peter Shilton since 1990 for the most England caps after a 125th appearance. Already his country's leading scorer, he has extended that tally to 91 goals.

Ghana News.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Harry Kane wins 2026 Men’s Striker of the Year award
Ghana News.content:
Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has won the 2026 Men’s Striker of the Year award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London after an outstanding goalscoring campaign for club and country.

The England captain received the honour on Monday, recognising his prolific performances during the 2025/26 season. Kane entered the ceremony as one of the leading contenders for the men’s Ballon d’Or after establishing himself as one of the most productive forwards in world football.

Kane scored 73 goals and made 8 assists for club and country in 65 appearances in the 2025/26 season.

The 33-year-old has continued to lead Bayern Munich’s attack since joining the German champions from Tottenham Hotspur in August 2023. His arrival in the Bundesliga marked a new chapter in his career after spending nearly two decades in English football, including his rise to become Tottenham’s all-time leading goalscorer.

Kane has also maintained his importance to England, where he serves as captain and remains a central figure in the national team's pursuit of major international honours.

His latest individual recognition comes as he challenges for the biggest prize of the evening, the men’s Ballon d’Or. Kane emerged as a leading candidate following a season in which his goalscoring record and influence for Bayern made him one of the favourites for the award.

The striker’s achievement adds another milestone to a career defined by remarkable consistency, intelligent movement and clinical finishing.

Ghana News.title: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
Ghana News.content:
Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.

Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting.

Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy".

Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election.

Bolsonaro's rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same.

But a challenge appears unlikely to succeed.

Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours. Some Bolsonaro fans are pointing out that Zanin was once Lula's lawyer and alleging bias.

But both teams had requested an extension to voting times - Lula's had argued that voters in São Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling stations because of a lack of buses, while Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in some areas in the south of the country and in São Paulo as their reason.

Both knew every vote would count and did not want their side to miss out.

The president of the Supreme Electoral Court Kássio Nunes Marques – appointed by Jair Bolsonaro – confirmed Lula's victory and said that the voter extension did not change the outcome of the race.

The sheer gap between the two candidates' tallies - 4.4 million votes - makes the result more difficult to challenge.The result came as a surprise after Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October with 47% of votes ahead of Lula's 45%.

But Lula's camp gained momentum ahead of election day, focusing on boosting voter turnout after 33 million people did not vote in round one.

Sunday saw the largest drop in abstention between the two rounds of a presidential election since 1989.

Bolsonaro had been poised to give a victory speech and said the result should be annulled, calling it "inexplicable".

As his disconsolate supporters left the house in Brasília where their candidate had been watching the result, Lula took to the streets in São Paulo to celebrate.

"This, my fourth term, will be the best of any president in the history of this country," the former metal worker told supporters. "It will be the one in which I listen most to the Brazilian people."

After pulling off this victory, Lula faces big hurdles: a divided country, an opponent that won't recognise the result, and a hostile Congress packed full of Bolsonaro allies.

Markets reacted negatively to the unexpected outcome. The Sao Paolo stock exchange opened 15% down, sparking a brief suspension before recovering slightly. Interest rate futures rose as investors scrutinised Lula's fiscal plans.

Reacting to the result, US President Donald Trump suggested the election had been stolen.

"I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election," he told reporters on Monday, without providing evidence or more details. "It looked very bad to me."

Other world leaders from across the political spectrum have congratulated Lula. Mexico's left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum said in a post on X: "The people of Brazil won."

Peru's right-wing President Keiko Fujimori praised Brazil's "democratic day". Similar messages were shared by the presidents of Chile and Ecuador.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted that their two countries had already "flourished under our partnership".

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said "democracy and multilateralism" had won. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez - also a left-wing leader - called it a "great victory".

French President Emmanuel Macron said the two nations should work "in service of a more just world".

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa called Lula's victory one for the "global south and progressive forces throughout the world".

In a video posted on Instagram later on Monday, Flávio Bolsonaro said police had told him to hand over his passports and had been banned from leaving the country.

Trump has previously shown support for Bolsonaro's father Jair, who is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence after being convicted of a coup attempt after losing the 2022 elections to Lula. Flávio Bolsonaro met Trump at the White House earlier this year to bid for his support.

Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, has already been president for three non-consecutive terms, serving two terms between January 2003 to December 2010, and again from January 2023.

His win makes him the first in Brazilian history to secure a fourth term, which will last until 2030.

But this has been a bitterly fought campaign and the new term - set to start on 5 January - comes amid significant constraints at home and abroad, including animosity from the US president.

Referring to what Trump has called the "Donroe Doctrine" - which seeks to establish US dominance in the Western Hemisphere - Lula used his victory speech to insist that Brazil "will not accept being anyone's backyard".

Lula has also bucked a wider trend in Latin America, where voters in countries such as Argentina, Chile and Colombia have put right-wing candidates and parties in power.

Ghana News.title: Anthropic warns of ‘catastrophic risk’ to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
Ghana News.content:
Anthropic has warned artificial intelligence (AI) could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the US.

The firm's valuation is expected to exceed SpaceX's, the biggest-ever listing, which was valued at about $1.8 trillion in the summer.

Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be released, the price range, or a listing date.

The Claude chatbot developer reported $16.3bn (£12.2bn) of revenue in the first half of the year, with losses of more than $80.7bn.

Anthropic, which said it will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology.

In a filing ahead of its listing, Anthropic said policymakers, regulators, researchers, and people within its organisation had raised concerns that AI systems posed a significant risk to humanity.

'Bold but sane'

In Anthropic's new documents, it reiterated promises it has made in the past to develop AI in a way that is beneficial to people, while at the same time warning investors of its dangers.

Anthropic detailed losses in its financial filings that exceeded its revenue for the first half of the year, but said it would often make forward investments "that may seem irresponsibly large at first glance".

"In general, we will aim to be bold but sane, and to win trust with a track record of successful bets," the tech giant said.

Its success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, Anthropic said, adding, "any failure to do so could adversely affect our business".

Across about 90 pages detailing possible risk factors, Anthropic set out the potential threats to its ability to safely and competitively develop AI.

Anthropic warned it relies on a cluster of cloud computing providers, Taiwanese chipmakers already facing huge demand and data centres concentrated in the US.

It also warned of "regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models"- citing concerns over AI being used by children or individuals at risk of suicide - and uncertainty about where and how it might be held liable for actions taken by its systems.

However, Anthropic also used the filing to laud the potential benefits of the tech itself, envisioning it unlocking "millions of virtual agents with the ability to revolutionise every area of human endeavour" across a range of fields.

"We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history," the firm said.

Anthropic said AI would also "profoundly accelerate the rate of progress in biology and medicine", potentially finding cures to diseases including cancer and Alzheimer's.

The firm added it could also establish "sustained acceleration in economic growth" by boosting productivity.

'Significant milestone'

Matt Orton, chief market strategist at investment management firm Raymond James Investment, said investors expected to see rapid growth as well as rapid financial losses in Anthropic's finances, so Monday's filing would not come as a surprise.

"Getting the details from this filing, I think will help provide the market with more visibility, because we need to know where its revenue growth is coming from," he told the BBC.

Peter Andersen, founder of Andersen Capital Management, told Reuters that Anthropic's plans to list was "a significant milestone in the development of artificial intelligence".

He added that the outcome of its stock market debut would be "fairly indicative of the sentiment" among investors to continue ploughing cash into AI development.

It said advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy".

Anthropic was founded five years ago by chief executive Dario Amodei, his sister Daniela Amodei and five others, and announced its intention to go public in June.

Its main rival, OpenAI, quickly followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year, according to a person familiar with OpenAI's plans.

Those announcements were followed by a wave of cyber-security and other technological breaches involving their AI agents - bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously.

Current and former staff of both companies also warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI tools.

As Anthropic revealed its stock debut plans on Monday, the owners of the rights to Elvis Presley's music sued the AI firm accusing it of using hundreds of the rock-and-roll star's songs to train its chatbot Claude.

Ghana News.title: Labourer fined GH¢120,000 for possessing and selling cannabis and tramadol
Ghana News.content:
A 20-year-old labourer, Kojo Sah Nkrumah, has been fined GH¢120,000 by the Tarkwa Circuit Court for possessing and selling cannabis and tramadol without lawful authority.

Nkrumah, who pleaded guilty to two counts of possession and selling of narcotic drugs without lawful authority, will serve three years in prison in default of payment.

The court, presided over by Ms Bernice Mensimah Ackon, convicted and sentenced him on his own plea.

Prosecuting, Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Samuel Ahiabor told the court that the complainants were police officers stationed at the Western Central Regional Formed Police Unit (RFPU) Base in Tarkwa.

He said Nkrumah, a resident of Tarkwa Railway Station, was arrested at about 0130 hours on January 21, 2025, during a routine night patrol by a police team, led by Chief Inspector Issahaque Yahaya.

The prosecution said the officers extended their patrol to the Tarkwa Railway Station, where they found Nkrumah seated under a shed selling substances suspected to be narcotic drugs.

A search of a takeaway bag in his possession uncovered 81 pieces of wrapped dried leaves suspected to be cannabis, seven sachets of tramadol and GH¢240 in cash, believed to be proceeds from the sale of the substances.

The prosecution said officers subsequently escorted Nkrumah to the Tarkwa Police Station with the exhibits.

On April 25, 2025, the exhibits were sent to the Forensic Crime Laboratory in Accra for examination.

A report received on May 13, 2025, showed that the plant material tested positive for delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the principal psychoactive compound in cannabis, with a gross weight of 139.61 grammes.

Ghana News.title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack
Ghana News.content:
Chris Brown has had hits with tracks like Freaky Friday and Turn Up the Music

US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub.

The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members' club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023.

Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months. Both men, who had pleaded guilty to affray, were also ordered to pay £1,500 in costs.

Judge Tony Baumgartner said Brown's use of the glass bottle to hit the victim twice over the head "was plainly dangerous", adding that the violence of the attack was "intense".

The sentence means Brown will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the 12-month period of suspension.

The court heard Brown's attack on music producer Abraham 'Abe' Diaw left the victim in need of hospital treatment for his injuries.

In sentencing, Judge Baumgartner said: "The repeated use of a glass bottle in that way, especially aimed at the head, was plainly dangerous, it carried the risk of delivering a more serious injury than was ultimately sustained."

CCTV footage was shown where Brown struck Diaw four times with the bottle, connecting twice with his head, and then hitting his shoulder.

Sentencing Brown, Judge Baumgartner said: "This was not planned violence. It was nevertheless serious violence by two people in a crowded nightclub."

Chris Brown (left) and Omololu Akinlolu were sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Monday

The judge told Brown: "Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious, it creates an obvious risk, not only to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others nearby."

He added that Brown's conduct was "particularly dangerous" and that he had to be "physically pulled away" from the attack.

The judge said Brown's fame, commercial success and professional standing "do not entitle you to special treatment - the law applies equally to everyone".

But judge Baumgartner also said he had noted Brown's guilty plea, compliance with bail conditions, and the impact a custodial sentence would have on Brown's children, and said the singer's "risk of further offending is low".

Brown and Akinlolu pleaded guilty to a charge of affray at Southwark Crown Court in July.

The singer was due to face a trial on more serious charges, which he denied and which were later dropped.

These were assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm, and having an offensive weapon.

Following Brown and Akinlolu's guilty pleas, the CPS released a statement outlining that Brown had approached Diaw on the dance floor, hitting him over the head with a glass bottle twice, before Akinlolu then punched Diaw in the head.

"They continued their assault whilst the victim attempted to flee through the club," the CPS said. "The victim was kicked while he was seated defenceless on the floor."

Judge Baumgartner told the pair that while he had concluded they had both crossed the threshold for jail, this year's changes to sentencing laws meant he had to put off doing so unless there were exceptional reasons.

"I have considered whether the seriousness of the offending, taken together with the need for punishment and deterrence, amounts to exceptional circumstances requiring immediate imprisonment. I have concluded, in relation to each of you, that it does not," he said.

"These were serious offences deserving of custodial sentences, but the circumstances do not justify displacing the [new legal] requirement that those sentences be suspended."

Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, also previously pleaded guilty to affray

On Monday, the court was shown three pieces of CCTV footage from inside Tape nightclub on the night of the attack.

The attack lasted no more than 20 seconds, but Brown could be seen hitting the victim four times with a tequila bottle, twice to the head.

Prosecutor, Heidi Stonecliffe KC, described the weapon as a "heavy square-shaped tequila bottle" and said Diaw was approached by Brown at around 03:00.

The footage showed that the nightclub was very small and packed at the time.

The defence described Chris Brown as a "dedicated and loving father of four children," someone who is "positive and present".

The singer is described as having lived "a good and law-abiding life" since his last conviction in 2013.

The defence described the events at Tape nightclub as a "short and deeply regretted incident".

Brown's defence lawyer told the court that he apologises to all those present at the club at the time of the attack.

"This is an ugly and unattractive incident," Sallie Bennett-Jenkins KC said.

"It is, however, an incident which was very short-lived, lasting something more than 17 seconds but no more than 20.

"It is something which undoubtedly would have caused distress to those who are present and for which Mr Brown... offers a profound apology to all those present."

The court heard Akinlolu "genuinely believed" that Brown was "under attack" when he joined the attack, punching Diaw.

Brown was described as being like a "brother" to Akinlolu, his lawyer Laurie-Anne Power KC told the court.

She added: "He genuinely believed him to be under attack and became involved, and thereafter accepts his initial involvement very quickly evolved into the events he has pleaded guilty to."

Diaw was taken to St Mary's Hospital in London after the attack. Ms Stonecliffe KC said he was discharged with "pain relief and a diagnosis of head injury and superficial injury of the knee".

An MRI scan taken in early March showed a "high grade injury to a ligament on the inner side of the left knee", the court heard.

Defending Brown, Ms Bennett-Jenkins KC said there was a "relatively low level of force" and disputed how significant the injuries were.

The defence argued that the attack left no fractures or broken skin and there was an absence of serious injuries.

Diaw, the victim, was "not supportive of the prosecution" and "withdrew" his support some time after the incident, the court heard.

Chris Brown is one of R&B's most successful singers, with hits including Yeah 3x and Forever

Brown and Akinlolu stood, faced each other, and clasped hands after the judge finished his sentencing remarks before walking out of the glass dock.

Loud cheers rang out outside the court as Chris Brown left the building and appeared to stop to sign an autograph.

After the sentencing, Brown shared a video from inside his car on his Instagram story, showing him looking out the window before turning to the camera and giving a thumbs-up.

Affray is an offence under the Public Order Act, and a person is deemed guilty in law if they use or threaten "unlawful violence towards another" with their behaviour, leading someone to fear for their personal safety.

Brown, 37, is considered one of the biggest stars in R&B, with a string of hit songs including Turn Up The Music, Ayo, Freaky Friday, Run It, Forever, Yeah 3x and Don't Wake Me Up.

Ghana News.title: Ballon d’or 2026: De la Fuente wins coach of the Year Award after Spain’s World Cup triumph
Ghana News.content:
Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has been named the 2026 Men’s Coach of the Year at the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, capping a remarkable year in which he led the national team to FIFA World Cup glory.

The 65-year-old claimed the Johan Cruyff Trophy on Monday, October 26, after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final on July 19, securing the country’s second men’s world title.



De la Fuente’s latest achievement adds another major honour to a coaching career that has flourished since he took charge of Spain’s senior national team in December 2022.



His World Cup success has also placed him among the most accomplished coaches in Spanish football, following the country’s victories at the 2023 UEFA Nations League and Euro 2024.



De la Fuente beats coaching heavyweights

The Spanish tactician emerged ahead of an impressive shortlist featuring Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique, Aston Villa boss Unai Emery and Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany.



The award recognises De la Fuente’s work in guiding Spain through a successful international campaign, culminating in victory over Argentina in a dramatic final that was decided in extra time.



Spain secured the trophy through Ferran Torres’ 106th-minute strike after Argentina had held them goalless during normal time.



The victory also made De la Fuente the oldest coach to win the men’s FIFA World Cup, at 65 years and 28 days, surpassing the previous record held by compatriot Vicente del Bosque, who led Spain to the 2010 title.

Spain’s historic World Cup campaign



Spain’s triumph was built on a disciplined and largely dominant tournament performance.



De la Fuente’s side went unbeaten throughout their eight matches at the expanded 2026 World Cup, conceding just one goal during the competition.



Goalkeeper Unai Simón also recorded seven clean sheets, setting a tournament record for the most shutouts by a goalkeeper in a single men’s World Cup edition.

Spain’s victory over Argentina further strengthened the country’s position among international football’s leading forces, adding the world title to its recent continental and international successes.



The achievement also made Spain the first country to hold the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cup titles simultaneously, following the women’s team’s triumph in 2023.



A new milestone for Spain’s coach



The Johan Cruyff Trophy gives De la Fuente individual recognition for the success he has overseen with Spain, following years of development work within the country’s national-team system.

Before taking charge of the senior side, he worked with Spain’s youth teams, helping develop players who have since become central to the national team’s success.



His senior-team achievements include the 2023 Nations League, Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, a run of major honours that has established his reputation among Europe’s leading international coaches.



The 2026 award also places a national-team manager at the top of a category whose previous winners came from the club game, marking a significant moment for international coaching.



For De la Fuente, the recognition completes an extraordinary year in which Spain returned to the summit of world football and his work on the touchline earned one of the sport’s most prestigious individual coaching honours.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Romania says Russia-run sabotage network set fire near weapons factory
World.content:
Authorities say the fire in Brasov in September is part of a broader Russian campaign against European countries that support Ukraine.

Romanian authorities say they have uncovered a network “coordinated” by Russia that they believe was responsible for a fire at an industrial site near a state-owned weapons factory in September.

Romania’s Intelligence Service said on Monday that the blaze in the central city of Brasov on September 14 was “part of a wider campaign of sabotage operations coordinated” by Russia amid its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The agency said the operations were aimed at arms manufacturers and “other targets of military and industrial interest”.

“These actions are intended to intimidate, undermine defence capabilities and weaken the contribution of the targeted states to European and regional security,” it said in a statement.

There was no immediate comment from Russia on Romania’s claim. Moscow has previously repeatedly denied such accusations.

Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism, known as DIICOT, said three people had been involved in the Brasov fire – two Belarusians and a Ukrainian, all living in European Union countries.

Two were “tracked down and remanded in custody in Germany while they were preparing to commit similar offenses”, the directorate said.

The third remains at large in Poland.

According to Romania’s Intelligence Service, recruits for such networks are often found on social media and are first offered money “for a seemingly harmless task”, such as “observing or photographing certain targets”.

Over time, “the tasks become increasingly serious, potentially involving acts of vandalism, arson or even murder”, it said.



‘Hybrid’ war

Romania, a member of the EU and NATO, shares a border of more than 600km with Ukraine.

Its centrist president, Nicusor Dan, has said the country is a target of a hybrid war that Russia is waging to destabilise nations backing Kyiv, citing drone incursions into Romanian airspace, cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns and sabotage.

Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said the fire in Brasov was “part of a broader campaign of sabotage across Europe” targeting military production.

“Hybrid attacks will not hold us back from strengthening our resilience and defense,” he wrote on X.

The accusation follows a string of incidents at defence sites across Europe in recent weeks.

In September, explosions and a fire erupted at an ammunition storage site in Bulgaria, weeks after a blaze at another munitions facility in the country. Both sites are operated by the Bulgarian arms maker EMCO, whose munitions are used in Ukraine.

That same month, firebombs were thrown near the offices of a defence company in Munich, and Romanian authorities said they had detained a Russian citizen accused of filming and photographing military sites in preparation for sabotage.

In August, a blast struck an ammunition factory near Rome in Italy operated by the arms maker KNDS.

At sea, at least eight cargo ships have been hit off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria over the past three weeks, and about 34 sailors have been reported dead or missing.

Dan, the Romanian president, has called the attacks on ships in Romanian waters “a new example of the tragic consequences of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine”.

A year ago, Poland and Romania also detained eight people suspected of taking part in a Russian plot to send exploding parcels to Ukraine.

World.title: Jordan strikes Syria after church attack, killing at least seven people
World.content:
Syria closes border crossings with Jordan after air strikes kill seven people in Deraa and Suweyda, including children.

Share Jordan strikes Syria after church attack, killing at least seven people on social media

Jordan has carried out air strikes in Syria in retaliation for last week’s deadly church attack, with Syrian authorities saying the raids killed at least seven people, including three children and a woman.

The attacks on Monday prompted Syria to close its main crossing with Jordan.

Jordan’s Armed Forces said in a statement that it targeted “hideouts” of armed groups in southeastern Syria in “retaliation” for the gun attack at a church in its Karak governorate on Friday. At least nine people were killed and dozens more wounded in the shootings.

The Jordanian military said the strikes on Syria were launched “in coordination with the Syrian government”.

It said the raids “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”.

Syria, however, denied any coordination with Jordan.

In a statement, the Syrian government said “the military operation was conducted without prior coordination or notification” and said it has launched an investigation into the attacks.

Syria’s Civil Defence service said at least four sites in rural Deraa and Suweyda provinces were hit on Monday evening, and that its crews had recovered the bodies of seven people: three men, a woman and three children.

Five of the dead – a man, a woman and three children – were members of one family killed in a strike on a tent in the village of Al-Tai in Deraa Province, the service said. Three other family members, including a child, were wounded.

A second strike hit Al Shayyah, also in Deraa, killing an 80-year-old man. A third hit a residential building in Muzayrib, in the Ain al-Basal area of Deraa, causing no casualties.



A fourth struck a residential building in the town of Shahba in Suweyda province, killing a 60-year-old man.

After the strikes, Syria’s border authority closed the Nassib crossing, suspending traffic in both directions. Nassib is the only crossing for passengers and commercial goods between Jordan and Syria.

A Syrian Foreign Ministry official called the strikes a “treacherous attack” and told Al Jazeera that the ministry would try to manage the fallout in a way that preserved Syrian sovereignty.

Earlier on Monday, Jordanian security forces arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law on suspicion of involvement in the church attack. The arrests took place in the village of Al-Jadeeda, after a shootout with authorities.

A Jordanian government source told Al Jazeera that the suspects sustained serious injuries during the confrontation, which lasted for about three hours.

The arrests and air strikes in Syria come after Jordan’s King Abdullah II pledged a stern response to the church attack. During the attack, three gunmen opened fire on mourners at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 90km south of the capital, Amman.

The king said those responsible would face the “harshest penalties” and ordered a review of the country’s security procedures.

Karak is home to a minority Christian population, which makes up about 300,000 of Jordan’s 11.5 million people.
