World.title: NDC opens new Abuja base, targets 2027 electoral victory
World.content:
Sen. Seriake Dickson, National leader of the NDC.

…As Dickson hails new national secretariat as Noah’s Ark 2

By Henry Umoru

The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has inaugurated its newly acquired national secretariat in Abuja as part of efforts to strengthen its operations ahead of the 2027 general election.

The facility, located in the Jabi area of the Federal Capital Territory, was unveiled shortly after an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), as it marks a significant step in the party’s efforts to strengthen its organisational structure and establish a permanent administrative base as preparations for the forthcoming elections gather momentum.

The new secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative centre and headquarters for its presidential campaign as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, just as the development marks a step in the NDC’s efforts to establish a permanent national base for coordinating its activities and managing its expanding political structure.

It is a strategic centre for coordinating its activities, strengthening communication among state chapters and mobilising supporters across the country and is also expected to play a central role in organising the party’s presidential campaign and coordinating other electoral activities ahead of the 2027 general elections

In his remarks, the National Leader of the party, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the facility as its new “Noah’s Ark” ahead of the 2027 general elections as he congratulated members and supporters on the acquisition, describing the new secretariat as a unifying centre that would provide a befitting home for the party’s growing membership.

He referred to the facility as the NDC’s newly acquired “Noah’s Ark,” a description underscoring its importance as a rallying point for members and supporters as the party pursues its political ambitions.

The inauguration attracted the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas; National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson; and Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly.

Also present was the party’s Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, alongside other party leaders and members.

With this, the NDC has positioned itself as an alternative political platform for Nigerians seeking a change from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

With the new facility, the party is expected to strengthen coordination between its national leadership, state chapters and other structures as election preparations continue.

World.title: NIMASA, ITF Endorse MOU on Seafarer Well-being
World.content:
The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) and the International Transport Workers’ Federation (ITF) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at promoting the mental health and wellbeing of Nigerian seafarers and cadets through training, awareness and capacity building.

This was the high point of a three-day Seafarers’ and Cadets’ Wellbeing Awareness and Train the Trainers Programme with the theme, “Stress: Understanding, Early Management and Coping,” organised by NIMASA in collaboration with the ITF.

Speaking at the event, the Director General of NIMASA, Dr. Dayo Mobereola disclosed that the partnership would support capacity building and the integration of the wellbeing module into maritime training curricula, with plans to make seafarer wellbeing a permanent component of preparations for life at sea.

Represented by the Executive Director, Maritime Labour and Cabotage Services, Mr Jibril Abba, he said “seafarers’ wellbeing is essential to safe shipping and NIMASA is committed to protecting maritime workers’ welfare. This programme would equip maritime training institutions, Agency officers and union partners with the skills to identify and manage stress and provide psychological first aid when necessary”.

He emphasised the importance of addressing the psychological challenges associated with life at sea, including stress, anxiety, depression and burnout. Citing a 2019 study commissioned by the ITF in collaboration with Yale University, he noted that one in four seafarers surveyed showed signs of depression, while approximately one in six exhibited signs of anxiety.

Also speaking, the ITF Africa Regional Secretary, Mr Safiyanu Dauda Mohammed, who signed the MoU on behalf of ITF noted that this MoU was the first of its kind that the ITF was going into with any country in Africa.

According to him, “it is very exciting for me because it is the first in Africa, and we are starting with Nigeria. Seafarers are very critical workers in the maritime sector. So it is very important to prioritise their wellbeing and welfare, to mitigate their anxiety and depression”.

In his remarks, the President-General of the Maritime Workers Union of Nigeria, Comrade Francis Bunu applauded the development saying “we need seafarers to be mentally sound while doing their job and that is why today is a very significant day for the seafarer in Nigeria”.

World.title: UBA Launches Climate Action to Advance Green Finance,  Sustainability
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has launched a Group-wide Climate Action Week to deepen climate awareness, promote responsible environmental practices and advance sustainable finance across its African and international operations.

The five-day campaign is with themed, “Banking on Africa’s Climate Future” and reflects the Bank’s commitment to integrating environmental responsibility into its operations, customer engagement and financing solutions.

The initiative commenced with the deployment of waste segregation bins across UBA offices and measures to reduce the use of single-use plastics at the Bank’s head offices. These activities underscore UBA’s commitment to translating sustainability principles into practical actions within its workplace and across its wider ecosystem.

UBA’s Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Oliver Alawuba, emphasised the importance of collective responsibility in addressing the growing impact of climate change.

“Climate change is no longer a distant environmental concern; it is increasingly shaping everyday life across Africa. We see its effects in rising food costs, increased energy demand and flooding that disrupts homes, businesses and livelihoods.

“At UBA, we believe that building a sustainable future requires collective action, beginning with the choices we make at work, at home and in our communities. Through this Climate Action Week, we are encouraging every member of the UBA Tribe, alongside our customers and other stakeholders, to embrace practical, sustainable habits and inspire others to do the same,” Alawuba said.

Alawuba, noted that climate considerations were increasingly important to business resilience, risk management and long-term economic growth.

“Climate change presents significant risks to businesses, communities and economies. These risks can affect business continuity, operating costs and financial performance, making sustainability an increasingly important consideration for both businesses and the financial institutions that support them.

“Through UBA Green Finance, we seek to support eligible businesses investing in cleaner technologies and more sustainable operations. By helping customers explore financing solutions aligned with their needs, we can contribute to a more resilient private sector while unlocking opportunities for sustainable economic growth across Africa,” Alawuba further said.

World.title: Firm Drives Financing of Oil Palm Industry to Boost National Output
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor

Reftop Holdings has continued to expand its footprint in driving innovative financing models of Nigeria’s agricultural financing model through allotment of 2,700 acres of land to subscribers under its PalmCrest Agro-Real Estate Project to boost national oil palm output by 5 percent in 2031.

This for the company marks a significant milestone in its drive to combine real estate investment with oil-palm plantation development.

This is also as the company has set a target of five-years plan to build its own oil palm refinery that would be capable of meeting 5 per cent Nigeria’s national output and thereby pushing the country to top 2 in world production.

Speaking in Lagos, recently the Managing Director of Reftop Holdings, Dr. David Assogba, said the project was designed to create opportunities for investors to participate in land ownership while supporting the development of productive agricultural assets.

He said that PalmCrest is Reftop’s flagship agro-real-estate initiative, built around the ownership of agricultural land, oil-palm cultivation and professionally managed plantation operations.

He explained that its first two project phases cover 5,200 acres and have attracted approximately 2,100 subscribers, reflecting growing participation in its agro-real estate investment model noting agriculture remains the next frontier.

“The model combines land ownership with the development and management of productive oil-palm farms. The concept connects land acquisition with productive farming, particularly oil-palm cultivation, allowing subscribers to participate in agriculture without having to personally manage the day-to-day activities of a plantation,” he said.

Presenting a technical report, the Chief Operating Officer, Reftop Homes Limited, Emmanuel Oluwatosin,said that so far 2700 acres has been allocated to subscribers, while 150,000 seedlings are ready for transplanting and 40,000 oil-palm seedlings are being nursed.

World.title: Kane Ends England’s 25-year Wait, Wins Ballon d’Or
World.content:
*Saka wins Sócrates Award, Yamal awarded the Young Talent for the Third year

Duro Ikhazuagbewith agency report

England’s Three Lions Captain, Harry Kane, on Monday night became the first English player to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world’s best player at a ceremony at the London Palladium.

Bukayo Saka, Arsenal forward with Nigerian ancestry, was also amongst the winners last night as he won the Socrates Award.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker Kane is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others.

Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland’s George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom.

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals – plus eight assists – in 65 matches.

Only one player at a club in Europe’s top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season.

But he wins it despite not lifting either of football’s biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals.

Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d’Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981.

BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies.

Kane’s Record-breaking 2025-26 Season

In term of trophies, Kane may have ‘only’ lifted the German double last season.

But that more than doubled his career trophy total – having also won the Bundesliga the season before.

But in terms of individual output Kane – whose previous best Ballon d’Or finish was 10th – was unmatched last season.

His 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern was 19 more than any other player in Europe’s top five leagues managed.

In fact it was the most anyone has recorded since Cristiano Ronaldo also notched 61 for Real Madrid 11 years ago.

He was the Bundesliga’s top scorer with 36 goals – 17 clear of anyone else. In the Champions League he scored 14 for the beaten semi-finalists.

In the German Cup he scored 10 goals, including a hat-trick in the 3-0 win over Stuttgart in the final, and he also netted once in the German Super Cup.

No player has ever scored so many goals in a season for Bayern, a club who have had legendary goalscorers like Gerd Muller, Rummenigge and more recently Robert Lewandowski in their ranks.

Kane’s 12 goals for England last season – including six at the World Cup – take him up a total of 73.

Only one player in history from Europe’s top leagues has scored more in a season, Lionel Messi’s 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Next on the list are Muller (72 in 1972-73), Cristiano Ronaldo (66 in both 2011-12 and 2014-15), former Brazil striker Ronaldo (66 in 1996-97), Erling Haaland (64 in 2022-23) and Luis Suarez (64 in 2015-16).

Former England striker Alan Shearer recently told BBC Sport: “The winner of the Ballon d’Or should be Harry Kane.

“His numbers for the last 12 to 18 months have been absolutely sensational for Bayern and for England. For that reason, he should get it.”

Another ex-Three Lions player Danny Murphy added: “His goalscoring has been relentless, brilliant. He’s had one of the best seasons of his career and it’ll be a great reward for him if he gets the trophy.

“He’s been brilliant at Bayern Munich since he’s been there, adapted really well and he’s been the best centre forward in the world for the last 12 months.”

OTHER CATEGORIES WINNERS

World.title: Cricket: Nigeria’s YellowGreens in First-ever T20i Dramatic Win over Uganda
World.content:
*Seal spot in T20 World Cup Africa sub-regional qualifiers

Nigeria’s stocks in the game of cricket has continued to rise following the country’s senior men’s team, YellowGreens’ defeat of Uganda by one run in a last-ball thriller, ending a long wait for a maiden men’s T20I victory over their East African rivals.

YellowGreens’ Isaac Danladi and Selim Salau were selected for tournament honours.

The YellowGreens, have recorded a historic milestone in Nigerian cricket, securing their first-ever men’s Twenty20 International (T20I) victory over Uganda with a dramatic one-run win at the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Africa Sub-Regional Qualifier C in Abuja last Sunday.

In a contest that went down to the final delivery at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium cricket venue, Nigeria successfully defended a target of 149 to defeat one of Africa’s established cricketing sides and conclude their qualifying campaign on a memorable note.

Beyond the victory, the result represented a significant breakthrough in the historical rivalry between the two nations. Uganda had traditionally dominated their men’s T20I encounters, winning the overwhelming majority of their previous meetings. Nigeria’s narrow triumph therefore marked not only a crucial tournament result but also a landmark achievement for the YellowGreens.

With both teams already assured of qualification for the 2027 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier, the encounter offered an opportunity to establish supremacy between two of the competition’s strongest sides. Nigeria seized that opportunity in unforgettable fashion.

After winning the toss and electing to bat, Nigeria made an aggressive start, with openers Isaac Danladi and Selim Salau immediately putting Uganda’s bowling attack under pressure.

The pair combined for an opening partnership of 68 runs from just 7.2 overs, giving the YellowGreens early momentum and laying the foundation for a competitive total.

Danladi was particularly impressive, scoring 47 runs from 28 deliveries, including three fours and four sixes. His attacking innings earned him the Player of the Match award and proved crucial in a contest ultimately decided by the narrowest of margins.

Salau contributed 30 runs from 24 balls, striking four boundaries and a six before falling to Uganda’s Joseph Baguma.

Baguma emerged as Uganda’s most effective bowler, finishing with figures of four wickets for 21 runs in four overs and preventing Nigeria from building an even larger total.

Ali Rahmon also made a valuable contribution, scoring 35 runs from 23 deliveries, including three fours and two sixes.

Despite Uganda’s efforts to restrict the scoring in the closing stages, Nigeria were eventually bowled out for 148 in 19.4 overs, setting their opponents a target of 149.

Uganda’s chase suffered an early setback as Nigeria’s bowlers struck in the opening overs, dismissing Raghav Dhawan and Robinson Obuya to put the visitors under immediate pressure.

Abdullahi Ismail claimed both early wickets, giving Nigeria the breakthrough they needed to defend their total.

Uganda captain Riazat Ali Shah, however, responded with a remarkable counterattack that brought his side back into contention.

Shah scored 60 runs from 35 deliveries, striking five sixes and three fours to keep Uganda firmly in the contest. His aggressive innings shifted the pressure back onto the Nigerian bowlers and raised the possibility of an Ugandan victory.

The victory over Uganda brought their sub-regional campaign to a fitting conclusion: an unbeaten run, qualification secured, individual awards earned and a historic breakthrough against one of their toughest continental rivals.

Nigeria now turn their attention to the 2027 Africa Qualifier, carrying the confidence of a team that has shown it can compete, endure pressure and make history.

The YellowGreens have conquered the sub-regional stage and broken new ground against Uganda. The road to the 2028 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup continues.

World.title: Ikpeme Motivates Flamingos ahead Mexico Clash on Thursday
World.content:
The Acting General Secretary of Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, has commended Nigeria’s U17 girls, Flamingos for their impressive 3-1 victory over two-time winners Korea DPR on Friday, which secured their place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

During a visit to the team’s training session on Monday morning, Ikpeme urged the players to carry the same determination into their knockout match against Mexico on Thursday, October 29. He encouraged the team to take each game as it comes and remain focused on reaching the quarter-finals.

The NFF scribe also promised to be present at the Round of 16 match to support the Flamingos as they continue their World Cup campaign.

Nigeria have scored a total of six goals in their three matches so far at the tournament, with Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Oluebube Umejiaku accounting for two each. Precious Oscar scored the second goal against Puerto Rico while Rodiat Kanyinsola Yusuf netted from a free-kick against Korea DPR.

Thursday’s encounter is a clash of former FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup bronze medallists. Nigeria picked up the bronze medals after a dramatic penalty-shootout win over Germany in the third-place match in India four years ago, while Mexico defeated Brazil 3-1 on penalties after a 1-1 draw to win bronze medals at last year’s tournament also staged by Morocco.

In India, the Flamingos led Germany 3-0 after 63 minutes, but Germany drew level before the final whistle.

However, Nigeria won the shootout 3-2 at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai to attain the podium for the first time in the history of the competition.

World.title: Super 4 Race Intensifies at Nat Idowu U16 Football League
World.content:
The race for a place in the Super 4 of the Nathaniel Idowu Under-16 Football League 2026 has reached a thrilling climax following a dramatic Week 8, setting the stage for a blockbuster final round of fixtures on Saturday, 31 October 2026.

Unbeaten Young 11 FA have already secured their place in the Super 4, but three spots remain up for grabs with five teams still firmly in contention heading into Week 9.

At the New Maracana Sports Complex, Tolu, Ajegunle United SC kept their qualification hopes alive with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over St. Petersburg FA. Goals from Adogha Peter in the 13th minute and Onyeabuchi Okoli in the 50th minute proved decisive as Ajegunle claimed a vital three points.

Atico FA also breathed new life into their campaign with a thrilling 4-3 win over Moore Wins Foundation FA. Haruna Usman, Korede Olabiyi, Ayomide Oyebanji and Opeyemi Ajiboye all found the net in an entertaining seven-goal encounter.

Bright Stars SA produced one of the biggest surprises of the weekend, defeating SC Heritage 2-1 away from home. Feranmi Akinwale scored twice in the 20th and 48th minutes to overturn Norbert Theodore’s opener and propel Bright Stars back into Super 4 contention.

At the Nathaniel Idowu Football Pitch, Oregie, Divinely Blessed FA recorded a comfortable 3-0 victory over bottom-placed Seraphic FA, while league leaders Young 11 FA once again demonstrated their resilience by coming from behind twice to earn a 2-2 draw against second-placed Fortune FA.

Bamidele Waris and Adebayo Lateef were on target for Fortune FA, but Daniel Hameed and Quadri Azeez responded for Young 11 to preserve their unbeaten record.

With qualification still hanging in the balance, all roads now lead to Tolu and Oregie for a decisive final day where every goal and every point could make the difference.

World.title: Orania residents to ‘refugees’ – Leader calls on Afrikaners to stay behind
World.content:
Orania Movement leader Joost Strydom has appealed to Afrikaners to remain behind in South Africa . Images via Facebook: Orania

More residents of Orania are choosing to leave the Afrikaner-only town to take up refugee status in the US.

The programme is open to South Africans of minority race groups – predominantly white – who are “victims of racial persecution”.

ORANIA RESIDENTS TAKING UP REFUGEE STATUS – HERE’S WHY

According to a new report, a small percentage of residents in Orania have been granted refugee status in the US.



Orania Movement leader Joost Strydom predicts this to be around 5% of the 2 900 population he believes have left the Afrikaner-only town to pursue bigger and better opportunities in America

Strydom stated that families were interested in applying to the refugee resettlement programme, as the US boasted a “powerful economy” compared to Orania.

He added in a Facebook post: “America has a lot to offer. This is the most powerful economy in the world. There are definitely many safe places in the USA, and there are welfare services for Africans who arrive there. Housing, food, and medical care are paid for by the U.S. government for a number of months, and there are other benefits.

He continued: “There are many places out there with better service delivery and obviously without an ANC government. Orania can’t compete with all those economic benefits. Orania is still small and is still very strong under the ANC government’s influence”.

Strydom added that many Afrikaner families saw Orania as a “stepping stone” to other opportunities.

We are also saddened by each of these individuals who had to seek greener pastures beyond their native land. The reality is that with every person who leaves, fewer and fewer Afrikaners remain in South Africa.



CALL TO STAY AND ‘BUILD’

Joost Strydom appealed to those considering leaving from Orania or elsewhere in South Africa on the refugee programme, or of their own accord, to consider staying behind.

He shared: “We cannot give you anything; we ask that you come and help build. Come and help build for those who choose to live in South Africa. Come help build for Afrikaners who believe that we belong here on this continent.

“Yes, we are sad about everyone leaving…they made a choice. If we want to survive as Africans in Africa, we must choose to build on something where our people can have opportunities again, where our children can go to school and study in Afrikaans, and where we can protect our culture”.

Strydom listed attractions such as Orania’s high-quality education, training facilities, and booming tourism sector.

He added, “All these things contribute to us being able to build a bigger and stronger economy. We choose to stay here and build a future for our people. What is your choice?”.

WHAT RACIAL PERSECUTION DO THEY FACE?

Orania is located in the Northern Cape, with a population of around 3000 individuals.

The Afrikaner-only town was built on private property in 1963. It is self-sufficient, with its own businesses, schools, hospitals, and even currency.

So, how do residents qualify to enter the refugee programme?

Like other applicants, those from Orania must meet the following criteria…

Be South African

Be of Afrikaner ethnicity or be a member of a racial minority in South Africa

Must be able to articulate an experience of persecution or fear of future persecution.

In line with US President Donald Trump’s claims of “racial discrimination”, South Africans interested in the refugee resettlement programme must prove that they have been “persecuted” in their applications.

In the Statement of Interest form, applicants are required to specify if the “persecution” was based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, membership of a social group, or a fear of “future harm”.

Other questions included when the prospective “refugee” would like to travel to the US, how many family members they would like to bring, and if interested parties have a valid passport.

World.title: The best time of year to see animals in Kruger National Park
World.content:
From dry winter months to lush summer landscapes, here’s what each season means for wildlife viewing in Kruger. Image: canva

If seeing as many animals as possible is your main goal during a trip to the Kruger National Park, the time of year you visit can make a big difference.

While wildlife can be seen throughout the year, the dry winter months from roughly April to September are traditionally considered the best period for game viewing.

According to SANParks, the reduced vegetation and limited availability of natural water during winter make animals easier to find and see.



That doesn’t mean summer is a bad time to visit. In fact, each season offers something different.

April to September at Kruger National Park

For visitors primarily interested in wildlife sightings, the dry season is the safest bet.

Kruger’s winter months are generally dry, with warm days and colder nights. As the vegetation becomes less dense and water sources become more limited, animals tend to concentrate around rivers, dams and waterholes.



This can make them easier to spot from the park’s roads.

SANParks specifically notes that winter traditionally provides the best game viewing, while its visitor guidance also says early mornings and evenings are usually the most productive periods for sightings.

The late dry season can be particularly rewarding because vegetation is at its sparsest.



What animals can you see?

The dry season can be a good time to look for Kruger’s famous Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo, as well as giraffe, zebra, hippo, antelope and numerous smaller species.

Predators can also be easier to spot when there is less vegetation providing cover. There are no guarantees, however. Wildlife is free-roaming, and sightings can vary from one day to the next.

October to March at Kruger National Park

Kruger National Park’s rainy season generally runs from October to March.



The summer rains transform the park, bringing fresh vegetation, flowing water and a dramatic change in the landscape. The downside for wildlife viewing is that there is much more vegetation, which can make animals harder to see.

SANParks says animals are also more widely distributed during the wet season because there are more natural water sources available.

That means you may have to work a little harder for sightings compared with the dry winter months. But there are some major advantages, as the green season can offer a completely different safari experience.



The landscape is greener and more vibrant, while summer is also an excellent period for birdwatching. SANParks notes, for example, that the Orpen area has particularly strong raptor sightings during the summer months.

Summer can also bring opportunities to see young animals, depending on species and conditions.

And while the thicker vegetation can make some mammals harder to spot, the abundance of water means wildlife is not as dependent on the limited waterholes and rivers used during the dry season.



Which months are best for a first safari?

For a first-time visitor whose main priority is seeing lots of animals, the cooler and drier period is generally the better choice.

Period Game viewing What to expect April–May Very good Vegetation starts drying out; generally pleasant conditions June–August Excellent Dry vegetation and limited water improve visibility September Excellent Very dry conditions can concentrate wildlife around water October Good Hotter weather; rains may begin, and vegetation starts changing November–March Good Green landscapes, more water and excellent birding, but thicker vegetation

It’s also good to remember that choosing the right season is only part of the equation: time of day matters too.

Early morning and late afternoon are among the best times to look for wildlife, according to SANParks.



SANParks’ guided morning drives leave before official gate-opening times, while sunset and night drives offer opportunities to see animals becoming active as temperatures cool and darkness approaches.

For self-drive visitors, getting out early can therefore be just as important as choosing the right month.

Ultimately, there is no bad time to visit Kruger National Park. The park changes dramatically throughout the year, and that’s part of what makes returning for another safari so rewarding.

World.title: Tuesday tide times: What to expect after the full moon

Spring tide conditions continue along South Africa’s coastline on Tuesday, following Monday’s full moon. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

Spring tides continue along South Africa’s coast after full moon

Spring tide conditions continue along South Africa’s coastline on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, following Monday’s full moon.



According to the South African Weather Service, spring tides bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.

The sea may reach further up beaches during high tide, while low tide could expose more rocks and sections of the shoreline.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. Beachgoers, anglers and other coastal visitors should check tide times, waves and sea conditions before heading out.

Check the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs expected starting XI against TS Galaxy
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will face TS Galaxy in the Carling Knockout Cup on Tuesday evening as they look to bounce back from their CAF Confederation Cup exit at the hands of Red Arrows.

Head coach Fernando da Cruz is under pressure, and a victory could ease the growing concerns surrounding his position at the club. Another defeat would increase the pressure on the Frenchman and could put his future in doubt.

With the Soweto Derby against Orlando Pirates coming up this weekend, Da Cruz could buy himself more time with a positive result against TS Galaxy and a strong performance against their arch-rivals.



Here is how Kaizer Chiefs can lineup against TS Galaxy

Brandon Petersen could return to the starting lineup if he is fit, particularly with the Soweto Derby looming. The goalkeeper could be given an opportunity to feature ahead of the crucial clash against Pirates.

However, Da Cruz could also opt to retain Bruce Bvuma between the posts, although Petersen’s potential return cannot be ruled out.

In defence, Miguel Inacio and Thabo Moloisane are expected to form the centre-back partnership, with Reeve Frosler and Bradley Cross occupying the full-back positions.

Sibongiseni Mthethwa and Lebohang Maboe could anchor the midfield as Chiefs look to establish control and provide a solid platform for their attacking players.

In terms of attack, Kaizer Chiefs could experiment with a combination of Mduduzi Shabalala and Mfundo Vilakazi as they look to put TS Galaxy to sword.

Asanele Velebayi is another player who could feature on the wing, while Flavio Silva is expected to lead the line.



Chiefs will be eager to respond after their continental disappointment, knowing that a place in the next round of the Carling Knockout Cup would provide a timely boost ahead of the Soweto Derby.

Kaizer Chiefs’ predicted lineup against TS Galaxy: Brandon Petersen; Reeve Frosler, Miguel Inacio, Thabo Moloisane, Bradley Cross; Sibongiseni Mthethwa, Lebohang Maboe; Asanele Velebayi, Mduduzi Shabalala, Mfundo Vilakazi; Flavio Silva.

World.title: Kruger’s popular Skukuza gate to close from next week
World.content:
Kruger visitors will face a temporary change to access at Skukuza. Image: wikimedia commons

Visitors heading to Skukuza Rest Camp in the Kruger National Park are being warned of a temporary change to the camp’s entrance from next month.

The Skukuza Rest Camp Main Gate will close from Monday, 2 November 2026, to allow essential maintenance and repairs to the gate’s roof structure.

According to SANParks, the closure is expected to remain in place until early December, subject to weather conditions and any unforeseen circumstances.



Where will visitors enter Skukuza?

While the main gate is closed, visitors will use a temporary camp entrance from Hippo Circle Street.

This is the road leading towards the Skukuza Medical Doctor/Surgery. The temporary entrance will be accessed through AM Spa and Skukuza Safari Lodge.

Visitors heading to Skukuza during this period are advised to follow the directional signage and instructions from SANParks staff.



This will help ensure the safe and efficient movement of both vehicles and pedestrians around the temporary access point.

Why is the gate closing?

SANParks said the planned work forms part of its ongoing infrastructure management programme in the Kruger National Park.

The maintenance is intended to improve the safety, functionality and longevity of park facilities.



The work is therefore not expected to affect access to Skukuza for the entire period, with visitors instead being directed to the temporary entrance.

The maintenance project is expected to be completed by 4 December 2026. SANParks has cautioned, however, that the completion date is subject to weather conditions and other unforeseen circumstances.

Visitors should therefore check for any updates before travelling to Skukuza during the maintenance period.

World.title: Wicknell Chivayo’s unpaid car bills: Uebert Angel steps in
World.content:
Zimbabwean self-proclaimed prophet Uebert Angel has pledged to pay up to US$2 million (R33.2 million) towards verified debts left by businessman Wicknell Chivayo, following reports that three car dealerships are owed millions of dollars for vehicles supplied to the late businessman.

Angel made the announcement while addressing his congregation on Sunday, 25 October, saying he was prepared to help settle legitimate claims because his family had also benefited from Chivayo’s generosity.

According to reports by Tuko and My Zimbabwe News, Angel’s offer is subject to strict conditions, with claimants required to provide documentary evidence proving that Chivayo owed them money.



Angel sets conditions for paying Chivayo’s debts

Angel reportedly said he would consider claims from a limited number of creditors, with his commitment capped at US$2 million.

He urged those seeking assistance to provide proof of their claims, indicating that he would not simply pay every person who alleged that Chivayo owed them money.

The self-proclaimed prophet also reportedly said he had arranged meetings with people seeking payment and that the businessman’s estate still needed to be assessed to establish its overall financial position.

Angel’s offer comes as questions emerge over the outstanding obligations of Chivayo’s estate following the businessman’s death in a helicopter crash near Marondera on 30 September 2026.

Chivayo died alongside his wife, Lucy Muteke, and four other people.

Car dealerships reportedly owed US$5.1 million

Reports have linked three Harare dealerships to outstanding payments totalling approximately US$5.1 million for vehicles supplied to Chivayo.



Enterprise Car Sales has reportedly been linked to a claim of US$1.3 million (R21.58 million), while Exquisite Cars and Faramatsi Motors have been associated with reported balances of US$1.4 million (R23.24 million) and US$2.4 million (R39.84 million), respectively.

However, the claims have not all been accepted by the businesses involved.

Reports indicate that the circumstances and amounts surrounding some transactions remain disputed.

The reported debts have drawn attention because Chivayo was widely known for gifting luxury vehicles to musicians, footballers, religious leaders and other public figures.

Some of the vehicles were reportedly supplied under arrangements that allowed payment at a later date, leaving questions about outstanding balances after his death.

Angel’s family benefited from Chivayo’s generosity

Angel’s pledge also comes against the backdrop of his close relationship with Chivayo, who reportedly gifted the preacher’s family luxury items, including a Rolls-Royce Ghost.

The prophet has described Chivayo as a close friend and family member following his death.

His offer has prompted mixed reactions on social media, with some users questioning why the announcement was made publicly during a church service rather than handled privately.

It remains to be seen how many claims will meet Angel’s requirements and whether the proposed US$2 million will be used to settle any of the reported dealership debts.

The administration of Chivayo’s estate will also be central to determining his outstanding liabilities and how legitimate claims are ultimately resolve

World.title: New report: Kaizer Chiefs in talks with top local coach
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are said to be exploring the idea of appointing Manqoba Mngqithi. Amakhosi previously made contact with the 55-year-old before deciding to hire Fernando Da Cruz in July.

According to the leading Amakhosi insider Innocent Mkhabela on X, talks are underway with Mngqithi resisting the idea of working with the current techincal team at Naturena.

KAIZER CHIEFS TALKS WITH MANQOBA MNGQITHI

“Amakhosi are back to MANQOBA MNQITHI. Based on what im hearing now is that talks are already taking place behind the scenes but Manqoba doesn’t want current technical team,” Mkhabela said on X.



These developments follow after Kaizer Chiefs crashed out of the CAF Confederation Cup at the hands of Red Arrows last weekend.

Coach Da Cruz is yet to taste defeat in the league. But the Glamour Boys’ performances under the Frenchman have left him with an uncertain future.

Meanwhile, Mngqtihi is currently a free agent after parting with Tanzanian giants Young Africans last weekend. The Umzimkhulu-born coach previously confirmed he held advanced talks with Amakhosi before the start of the season.



MOVE TO AMAKHOSI WAS BLOCKED

“Kaizer Chiefs did have interest in me. But someone blocked the move and I know who it is,” said Mngqithi.

“I have had very cordial talks with Chiefs, even with Kaizer Motaung Sn. It is not a lie. But it never reached any fruition because there are people who block these moves.” “I’m fortunate to know that the person who blocked it I am not even worried about. But it’s true there was interest recently,” he continued.  “Kaizer Chiefs even wanted me before I joined Sundowns. I’ve had very cordial talks with senior Kaizer Motaung. I know they have always shown interest in me. But for whatever reason it never happened.”

World.title: Number of the Day | 31.9% | 26 October 2026
World.content:
The Hidden Cost of Saving South Africa's Supermarkets

When a retailer begins recovering financially, the consequences for workers and communities can be far more complicated than the balance sheet suggests.

A struggling supermarket has two very different balance sheets. One records revenue, expenses, profits and losses. The other is harder to quantify: the livelihoods supported by its stores, the communities that depend on them and the economic security of the people who keep its shelves stocked.

South Africa's grocery industry is confronting the tension between these two measures of success. Pick n Pay's latest financial results provide a revealing example. The retailer's parent group reduced its headline loss by 31.9%, from R439 million to R299 million for the 26 weeks ended 30 August 2026. That represents measurable improvement, but the group remains loss-making.

The more consequential question is what must change for the business to become sustainable, and who carries the cost of those changes.

When efficiency reaches the shop floor

Supermarkets operate in a competitive environment where labour scheduling, stock management, distribution costs and operating hours affect profitability. Decisions that improve efficiency can also influence the economic security of employees.

For workers, operational efficiency is not an abstract financial objective. It can determine the predictability of working hours, income and family routines.

Pick n Pay reached an agreement with SACCAWU, its primary labour partner, and withdrew the Section 189A consultation process initiated in May 2026. The company says the agreement introduces a more flexible store labour model, supporting improved scheduling and cost management.

The withdrawal of the consultation process is significant, but it does not establish that every employee's existing working arrangements will remain unchanged.

For example, fewer guaranteed hours could leave an employee financially worse off even if their job is retained. That is a potential consequence of changes to working arrangements, not a verified outcome for every Pick n Pay employee.

The challenge is finding a balance between commercial sustainability and the financial stability of workers.

The community cost of closing an unprofitable store

Store closures present a similar dilemma. From a retailer's perspective, withdrawing from an underperforming location can prevent ongoing losses and free resources for stronger operations.

For a community, the calculation is different. A supermarket can anchor a shopping centre, provide entry-level employment and attract customers to neighbouring businesses.

Its closure may therefore affect more than the employees directly attached to the branch. Nearby traders could lose foot traffic, while shoppers may need to travel further to access familiar products and services. The scale of these consequences depends on the location and the alternatives available.

This does not mean struggling retailers should maintain every loss-making store indefinitely. It means that financial savings and their wider consequences deserve to be examined together.

A smaller, more productive retail footprint may strengthen a company. Whether it strengthens the wider economy is a separate question.

The digital transformation complicates the picture

Online grocery shopping introduces another challenge. As delivery services become more important, supermarkets must manage physical stores alongside digital ordering, fulfilment and distribution.

Pick n Pay reported 35.4% growth in online turnover, an encouraging development in a difficult trading environment. But growth from an individual channel does not automatically compensate for weakness elsewhere in the business.

Competition from services such as Checkers Sixty60 is also changing how retailers organise their operations. The need to deliver groceries quickly and reliably places greater importance on inventory accuracy, logistics and coordination between digital platforms and stores.

This transformation may create opportunities in technology, delivery and fulfilment while changing the skills and working arrangements required in traditional retail operations.

The broader employment outcome will depend on how businesses implement these changes and whether workers can access opportunities within the evolving retail model.

A recovery that must work beyond the boardroom

Pick n Pay continues to pursue its FY29 break-even objective. Its latest results show progress, although its core supermarket business remains under pressure.

For South Africans, the stakes extend beyond whether one familiar retailer survives. A competitive grocery sector matters for consumer choice, affordable access to essential goods and employment opportunities.

A successful turnaround should therefore be assessed through more than falling losses and improved margins. It should also be assessed through the quality of the jobs that survive, the competitiveness of the stores that remain and the value delivered to customers.

A healthier company is an important achievement. A healthier company that continues contributing meaningfully to the economy is a considerably bigger one.

References

· Pick n Pay Stores Limited. Condensed Consolidated Interim Financial Results for H1 FY27, 26 October 2026.

· Pick n Pay Stores Limited. Trading Statement and Conclusion of Store Labour Agreement, 22 October 2026.

· eNCA. Number of the Day, 26 October 2026.

· MyBroadband. Pick n Pay Reports 35.4% Growth in Online Turnover, October 2026.

World.title: Pick n Pay says turnaround efforts are taking hold
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Retailer Pick n Pay is still making a loss but there are some encouraging signs.

Pick n Pay group includes Pick n Pay stores and the profitable discounter Boxer.

It reports that headline losses fell by 31.9% to reach R299 million in the half-year that ended in August.

Focusing on Pick n Pay alone, it managed to reduce its trading loss by R105 million to half a billion rand.

READ | Pick n Pay reports modest sales growth

Revenue from Pick n Pay stores was fractionally lower and the company says this is partly because six stores were closed down in the six months and 12 over a full year.

Still, Pick n Pay says the loss underscores the scale of work that still needs to be done.

Price inflation was 1.5%, with the retailer saying this reflects its commitment to deliver low prices to consumers.

The group aims to break even in 2029.

World.title: Multi-party government rule is here to stay - Roelf Meyer
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa is unlikely to return to a government that is led by a single party.

This is according to South Africa's ambassador to the United States, Roelf Meyer.

Meyer, who was speaking at the launch of his political memoirs on Monday, said multi-party government rule is here to stay.

The book details Meyer's political journey from the National Party to the transition to a democratic South Africa.

READ | LIVESTREAM | Eugene de Kock testifies before TRC inquiry

Meyer attributed the success of this transition to the ability of ‘keeping the middle ground together’.

This transition, he said, was made possible by former presidents Nelson Mandela and FW de Klerk, among others.

“That success was part of the ultimate sobering effect that led us to make that transition in a peaceful way.”

World.title: Tshwane water woes | Govt launches Gauteng treatment plant audit
World.content:
PRETORIA - Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina is launching an audit of Gauteng’s water treatment plants.

It comes amid reports of water contamination and unreliable supply.

Majodina says the audit will identify infrastructure problems.

"We're focussing on Gauteng because of the high population of Gauteng, but also there's unreliability of water supply. There's a lot of contamination that gets reported time and again in Gauteng… “Unless we do the audit, we might not be able to know exactly what the state of these water treatment works is, because to us that is very much important,” she said.

The minister also called on the private sector to help bankrupt municipalities fund urgent repairs.

“We need nothing less than R400 billion to fix the entire system with the money that the country does not have. That is why we have made a call that the private sector must also partner with municipalities. Most of our municipalities, they don't have a revenue collection.”

Previously, Rand Water warned that a major water supply crisis could be looming as excessive consumption places its entire network under severe pressure.

The pressure comes as several municipal customers have reached what the water utility described as 'exceptionally high levels'.

Among those areas ranking high included City of Johannesburg, City of Tshwane, City of Ekurhuleni.

Other municipalities on the list include Mogale City, Emfuleni, Madibeng, Merafong and Lesedi.

READ | Rand Water flags areas consuming more water than allocated

World.title: Katiso Molefe, co-accused's case postponed to July 2027
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The case against alleged Big 5 cartel member Katiso 'KT' Molefe and his co-accused has been postponed to 19 July 2027.

This is to allow for a partial head trial involving two of the accused to be finalised.

Molefe, Michael Pule Tau, Tiego Floyd Mabisela and Musa Kekana appeared in the High Court in Johannesburg on Monday.

READ | WATCH: KT Molefe rocks bulletproof vest to court with armed guards

They face 35 charges linked to the 2022 murder of Oupa Sefoka, popularly known as DJ Sumbody.

Molefe's bail has been extended while his co-accused remain in custody.

The National Prosecuting Authority says it remains trial-ready and committed to ensuring that the matter proceeds once outstanding proceedings are concluded.

World.title: ‘Only the person you killed can forgive you' - De Kock
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former Vlakplaas Commander Eugene De Kock says he does not believe in forgiveness, insisting that only the person killed could forgive him.

He was speaking on the sidelines of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) Cases Inquiry on Monday.

The man nicknamed ‘Prime Evil’ reflected on his role in some of the crimes committed during apartheid.

READ | LIVESTREAM | Eugene de Kock testifies before TRC inquiry

De Kock was sentenced to two life terms and 212 years in prison for six murders.

Asked whether he had apologised to families of those he killed, he said he had apologised but never asked for forgiveness.

“I don't believe in forgiveness at all. Even if they grant it, I won't accept it. Only the person that you killed can forgive you,” he said.

He admitted that he killed ‘a few’ people and that his unit targeted the militant opponents of the National Party rather than civilians.

During his testimony at the inquiry, De Kock outlined further his part in some of the gruesome crimes committed at the time.

READ | De Kock says activists were not seen as terrorists

He claims he was willing to give evidence just as he did in the 1989 Motherwell car bombing in which three police officers and an informer were killed, but was not called as a witness to do so.

World.title: Closing ranks: Opposition unity talks intensify as Gachagua hosts Kalonzo, Wamalwa
World.content:
Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka with DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua at his Wamunyoro residence in Nyeri on October 26, 2026. [Boniface Okendo, Standard]

The Opposition unity is now taking shape following intense political discussions between Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) leader Kalonzo Musyoka.

Moments after Kalonzo and his delegation left Wamunyoro, Democratic Action Party leader Eugene Wamalwa and a section of the Luhya council of elders were ushered in for talks about when to announce the Opposition’s Presidential flagbearer, strict timelines of the electoral process, and internal affairs of the Opposition taking centre stage in the separate talks.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Serbia’s leader concedes defeat to student-led movement in seismic political shift
World.content:
Belgrade, Serbia AP —

The long-serving strongman leader of Serbia, Aleksandar Vucic, conceded defeat on Sunday in an election that pitted him and his right-wing party against a diverse student-led opposition movement that spent two years protesting his government.

It was a seismic political shift in the Balkan country where Vucic, who had been endorsed by Russian President Vladimir Putin and who denounced the student movement as a foreign-led attempt to unseat him, led for 14 years.

High turnout and gathering tensions marked the highly contested parliamentary election that was a showdown between Vucic and his right-wing Serbian Progressive Party and university students who, accusing the government of corruption and dismantling democracy, had built a popular following across the country.

Serbia’s 6.4 million voters were electing lawmakers to the 250-member Parliament. In conceding the election, Vucic said his party projects that his opponents, the youth-backed Students’ List, will take between 135 and 140 seats while his SNS party will have around 105.

“The Students’ List has won,” Vucic told supporters at his party’s election-night event, though he blamed Serbia’s independent media as well as alleged interference by unnamed European countries and an “American deep state” for the loss.

Belgrade erupts in celebration

Vucic said that his SNS party won around 1.7 million votes compared to the Students’ List, which he said took around 2.2 million.

Supporters of the Students’ List immediately flooded onto the streets of Belgrade and other cities, honking horns, shouting and chanting: “Aleksandar is gone,” referring to Vucic.

The outcome, which Vucic announced only around an hour and a half after polls closed, came after tensions had built as voting progressed during the day.

Police in anti-riot gear cordoned off an area in central Belgrade around the election commission headquarters. Special police vehicles could be seen near a Belgrade park where Vucic’s loyalists have been camping for over a year, and large groups of black-clad men had congregated at various points throughout the city.

Protests over corruption lead to Vucic’s fall

Vucic was seeking to become Serbia’s prime minister after serving two near-full terms as president. He resigned the presidency last month to lead the campaign.

Support for the populist had eroded since 16 people were killed in 2024 when a concrete canopy collapsed at a train station in Novi Sad. That set off a wave of youth protests that blamed the collapse on high-level corruption, cronyism and rampant graft during renovation work at the station.

Despite the protests, Vucic retained considerable support among many of Serbia’s voters. Admirers viewed him as a capable leader who can steer the nation through global uncertainties — the image that was carefully crafted by the mainstream media.

Student movement

While the increasingly authoritarian Vucic has routinely outplayed Serbia’s fractured opposition in the past, the leaderless youth movement proved to be a tough opponent that rattled his firm grip on power in Serbia like no one else in the 14 years since his party took office.

The newly formed Students’ List movement was shaped by university students but none actually appeared on the election list. Instead, its candidates are little-known experts, athletes, farmers and artists.

This approach was meant to counter Vucic’s one-man rule and restore a sense of community and solidarity. The students’ message during the campaign focused on a non-partisan effort to rebuild Serbia’s economy and restore its democracy.

Candidates and supporters at the Students’ List headquarters in Belgrade celebrate victory at the news that Serbia’s ruling party, the Serbian Progressive Party, has conceded defeat in the parliamentary elections on October 25. ( Andrej Isakovic/AFP/Getty Images

The students have used youthful energy to attract voters who are disillusioned with local politicians. Vilified by pro-government media, they cycled and walked through the country to reach voters in rural areas — Vucic’s traditional strongholds.

The student victory echoed the recent electoral defeat of a Vucic ally in Hungary, where youth participation helped oust the autocratic Viktor Orbán after 16 years and bring in a new pro-European government. It was likely to resonate beyond Serbia as countries across Europe have faced angry youth and student protests.

The vote was closely watched in the EU

Monitors predicted that total turnout in the election could reach around 70%, unseen in Serbia since 2000. During the day, long queues formed at polling stations in Serbia and in cities around the world.
