PUERTO VALLARTA — This guide is for people who live here or are staying for weeks, not for a one-weekend tourist. It lists the things to do in puerto vallarta november 2026 that are worth crossing the city for, with dates, venues and practical notes.

The first week centres on Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead) and the monumental Catrinas on the Malecón, the seafront promenade. The busiest stretch is 11 to 15 November, when concerts, Gourmet International and the half marathon overlap.

Every date, venue and price below comes from the organiser, the venue or the Puerto Vallarta tourism board. Prices converted at about MXN 18.65 per US$.

31 October to 8 November: Day of the Dead and HEAT Week

Now, through the Festival de las Almas Monumental Catrina exhibition Malecón seafront promenade, Centro · Price not published Monumental Catrinas, the skeletal figures of Día de Muertos, line the seafront for the Festival de las Almas, the Jalisco Day of the Dead programme. Walk it more than once.

Saturday 31 October to Thursday 5 November HEAT Latin Music Awards 2026 and HEAT Week Puerto Vallarta International Convention Center, Marina Vallarta · Price not published HEAT is a Latin music awards show, and its gala is on Thursday 5 November. The tourism board lists no ticket prices, so check the awards’ own channels before planning.

Friday 6 to Saturday 7 November Torneo de Pesca Playa Los Muertos 2026 Los Muertos Beach Pier, Zona Romántica · Registration fee not published The 19th annual sport-fishing contest uses the pier as the starting point for the boats. Registration opens the day before at the Deportes Gutiérrez Rizo store, so ask there if you want to enter.

Saturday 7 to Sunday 8 November The Grill Festival 2026 Puerto Vallarta International Convention Center, Marina Vallarta · Tickets MX$300 to MX$400 (about US$16 to US$21), sold on thegrillfestival.com A barbecue and fire-cooking festival with cooking competitions, live demonstrations, workshops and a kids’ zone. Saturday features the Mixólogo de Fuego contest and Sunday the Maestro del Asador contest.

11 to 15 November: Gourmet International, Concerts and the Half Marathon

Thursday 12 to Sunday 22 November 31º Festival Gourmet International 30 participating restaurants, Puerto Vallarta area · Menu prices not published The festival brings more than 60 guest chefs and over 15 special dining events, with more than 20 wineries taking part. Book directly with the restaurant you choose, because the tourism board lists no central ticket platform.

Thursday 12 November, 8:00 p.m. Maroon 5, VidantaWorld Concert Series VidantaWorld Esplanade, Vallarta-Nuevo Nayarit · Price not published Maroon 5 play the VidantaWorld Concert Series at the Vidanta World Esplanade in Nuevo Nayarit, the resort district just north of the city. Check the resort’s official site for ticket details.

Thursday 12 November Michael is Back: The Michael Jackson Experience Teatro Vallarta · Price not published A Michael Jackson tribute show at Teatro Vallarta, the city’s theatre and cultural centre. Tickets are sold through the theatre’s website, which links to Red Access, a Mexican online ticket seller.

Saturday 14 to Sunday 15 November PVR Asian Festival 2026 ASIPONA Pier 2 (the port authority’s dock) · Tickets from MXN 120 (about US$6.43) The festival offers Asian food, K-pop, anime, cosplay, gaming and cultural activities. Buy tickets on festivalespvr.com, where service fees are added to the base price.

Saturday 14 November, 7:00 p.m. Edna Rendón: Voz sin límites Teatro Vallarta · Price not published Mexican soprano Edna Rendón sings opera, bolero and international repertoire. Tickets are sold at the Teatro Vallarta box office and on its website.

Saturday 14 November, from 7:30 a.m. Cruce Vallarta 2026 open-water swim Holi Beach, Hotel Zone, and Hotel Rosita Beach, start of the Malecón · Registration fee not published The 4.5K and 3.1K routes start at 7:30 a.m. from Holi Beach, the 1.5K route at 9:30 a.m. from Hotel Rosita Beach, and the youth 1K at noon. Registration is through the organisers’ Facebook page, Cruce Vallarta.

Sunday 15 November XXII Medio Maratón Puerto Vallarta 2026 Start and finish at the Agustín Flores Contreras sports complex (El Estadio) · MX$450 (about US$24) and up The 21K starts at 6:30 a.m. and the 5K at 6:40 a.m. at the Agustín Flores Contreras sports complex. Registration starts at MX$450 (about US$24) and rises later, through Trotime, a Mexican race-registration platform.

Weekly and Seasonal Events

Saturdays 7, 14, 21 and 28 November Olas Altas Farmers Market Lázaro Cárdenas Park, Zona Romántica · Price not published The market opens its 2026-27 season on 7 November and runs every Saturday, with produce, prepared food, jewellery, textiles and art. Zona Romántica is the old-town beachfront district.

Thursdays from 12 November Movie Picnic 2026-27 season Jardín de Luna garden, Puerto de Luna Hotel, North Hotel Zone · MXN 50 (about US$2.68) This is the 12th season of a “petate cinema”, where you watch films on a mat on the grass. Screenings run on Thursday evenings, and details are on the Movie Picnic Facebook page.

Planning Your Puerto Vallarta in November

Revolution Day, which marks the 20 November anniversary, is observed on Monday 16 November 2026 under Mexico’s Federal Labour Law. That is a statutory day of rest for workers, so 14 to 16 November is a long weekend.

Work out your journey home before evening shows at the Convention Center or VidantaWorld.The official Puerto Vallarta tourism calendar at visitpuertovallarta.com lists most dates but often publishes venues and prices late.

For tickets, follow the links on each organiser’s own page.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the biggest events in Puerto Vallarta in November 2026?

The Festival de las Almas brings monumental Catrinas to the seafront, the Gourmet International festival runs from 12 to 22 November, and the city half marathon is on Sunday 15 November.

When is the Maroon 5 concert in Puerto Vallarta?

Maroon 5 play the VidantaWorld Esplanade on Thursday 12 November 2026. The concert starts at 8:00 p.m.

When is the Olas Altas Farmers Market open in November 2026?

The market runs every Saturday morning from 7 November, at Lázaro Cárdenas Park in Zona Romántica.

Is Revolution Day a public holiday in Puerto Vallarta?

Yes. Mexico observes the 20 November anniversary as a statutory day of rest on the third Monday of November, which is Monday 16 November 2026.

Where does the Puerto Vallarta half marathon start?

The XXII Medio Maratón starts and finishes at the Agustín Flores Contreras sports complex, known as El Estadio, on Sunday 15 November. Registration is on maratonvallarta.com.

World.title: What to Do in Bogotá in November 2026: Opera, Carranga and Cypress Hill
World.content:
BOGOTÁ · Culture

Ópera al Parque closes on 4 November and the first Festival Carranguero fills the weekend of 7 and 8 November. The month, day by day.

Archive photo: a colonial street in La Candelaria, the historic district where the Carranguero Festival ends on 8 November.

BOGOTÁ — This guide is for people who live in the city or are staying for weeks, not for a one-weekend tourist. It lists things to do in Bogotá in November 2026 with dates, venues, prices and ticket platforms where the official sources confirm them.

November opens with the tail of Ópera al Parque and a public holiday on 2 November that thins the traffic and closes some offices. The first full weekend brings the free Carranguero Festival, a celebration of folk music from the Boyacá highlands, and Cypress Hill plays on 5 November.

Mid-month brings Colombian rock, and the final week adds a family show and a concert celebrating women in music.

1 to 4 November: Opera Closes and a Holiday Monday

Sunday 1 to Wednesday 4 November Ópera al Parque 2026 Museo Casa Lleras and the National Museum · Free Bogotá’s free opera festival closes its 29th edition with free concerts and piano recitals. Entry is free up to venue capacity, so arrive early.

Monday 2 November All Saints’ Day observed Citywide · Public holiday Many offices and banks close for the holiday. It is a quiet day for errands but a good one for parks and neighbourhood walks. Check opening hours before visiting museums or shops.

5 to 9 November: Hip-hop, Poetry and the First Carranga Weekend

Thursday 5 November, doors 5:00 p.m. Cypress Hill Movistar Arena, Bogotá’s largest indoor arena, in Barrios Unidos · Tickets on Tuboleta, Colombia’s main ticketing platform Buy through Tuboleta, the official ticket seller, and plan your route because Barrios Unidos gets busy on arena nights. The arena is well served by TransMilenio, the city’s bus rapid transit system, but leave extra time for security checks.

Thursday 5 to Saturday 7 November Jumbo Open Bar Festival 2026 Chamorro City Hall, an events venue · Register at jumboopenbarfestival.com A three-day festival of wine, beer and cocktails. Register through the festival website, and consider a ride-hailing app for the return journey.

Saturday 7 November, from noon Primer Festival Carranguero de Bogotá – day one Parque San Andrés, Engativá · Free The first edition of this festival celebrates carranga and rural musical traditions from the Bogotá–Boyacá region. The official programme starts with Monte Violeta at noon, followed by Pulido Son, Rumbambuquiando, El Son del Frailejón and Los Fiesteros de Boyacá. It is free and outdoors, so bring layers and rainwear.

Sunday 8 November, from 1:00 p.m. Primer Festival Carranguero de Bogotá – day two Teatro al Aire Libre La Media Torta, La Candelaria · Free The festival moves to the open-air amphitheatre in La Candelaria for a full afternoon of carranga. The confirmed line-up runs from Los De la Moña at 1:00 p.m. through to Los Rolling Ruanas at 6:55 p.m. This is a rare chance to hear the genre’s leading acts for free in a historic setting.

12 to 16 November: Rock, Theatre and a Holiday Monday

Thursday 12 November Ekhymosis: El Origen Teatro Colsubsidio, a concert theatre The Colombian rock band Ekhymosis, which has returned to its original name, plays its El Origen show. Check ticket details with the venue before you go.

Monday 16 November Cartagena Independence Day observed Citywide · Public holiday A Monday holiday marking Cartagena’s independence. Banks and many offices close, and some cultural venues may run Sunday hours. Use the day for the free outdoor spaces or check venue schedules before heading out.

21 to 25 November: Family Show and Women in Music

Saturday 21 November El Show de Alejo Igoa – Bogotá Movistar Arena, Barrios Unidos A 90-minute family show at the arena. Check ticket details with the venue and arrive with time for entry procedures.

Wednesday 25 November, 7:00 p.m. Ellas Cantan Teatro Jorge Eliécer Gaitán, Carrera 7 #22-47 · Paid entry A concert celebrating women in music, with Flor de Lava, Lunalé and Pedrina, timed around the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Tickets are sold at the box office.

Planning Your Bogotá in November

November is cool and often rainy in Bogotá. Carry a compact umbrella and wear layers because sunshine and evening chill can arrive in the same day.

Two public holidays fall on Mondays this month: 2 November for All Saints’ Day and 16 November for Cartagena Independence Day. Banks and many offices close, and some venues run reduced hours, so check before you travel.

Foreign cards sometimes fail on Colombian platforms, so have a backup card or ask your bank to approve international transactions.For getting around at night, use ride-hailing apps or book a taxi through a trusted app rather than hailing on the street.

TransMilenio is efficient for major venues but check the last service times if you are staying out late.The Bogotá cultural agenda on bogota.gov.co and the website of the Secretaría de Cultura, the city culture department, are the best weekly listings sources.

Idartes, the city arts institute, also publishes free event programmes, including the Carranguero Festival schedule.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the main events in Bogotá in November 2026?

Ópera al Parque closes on 4 November and the first Festival Carranguero runs free on 7 and 8 November.

Is the Festival Carranguero free?

Yes, the official Bogotá city listing confirms free entry for both days at Parque San Andrés in Engativá and La Media Torta in La Candelaria.

Are there public holidays in Bogotá in November 2026?

Yes. Monday 2 November (All Saints’ Day) and Monday 16 November are public holidays; the latter is Cartagena Independence Day observed under Colombia’s Ley Emiliani, the law that moves some holidays to Mondays.

World.title: Spain’s Housing Costs Outrun Wages in 2026
World.content:
SPAIN · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening Spain’s Housing Price Index rose 12.2% year on year in Q2 2026, far outpacing wages, and the government is cracking down on tourist rentals.

— Why it matters The affordability squeeze is reshaping Spanish cities and the rental market that American expats and investors rely on.

— The numbers The INE Housing Price Index rose 12.2% year on year in Q2 2026; second-hand prices rose 12.9%.

— Who is who Pedro Sánchez leads the government; Pablo Bustinduy leads consumer affairs.

— What to watch The tourist-rental decree awaits convalidation by Congress.

— What it means for you American buyers face higher entry prices and new rules on short-term rentals, but the policy push may expand long-term rental supply in cities like Madrid.

Spanish home prices rose 12.2% in the year to June 2026, about three times the 4.0% rise in labour costs per worker. For American readers, the gap means a property market that is pricing out local tenants and drawing government intervention into tourist rentals.

Spain is the eurozone’s fourth-largest economy and a magnet for American retirees, remote workers and property investors. This analysis explains the official numbers behind the housing squeeze and the policy response, drawing on the Europe Intelligence Brief.

The Price-Wage Gap in Official Numbers

Spain’s National Statistics Institute, known as the INE, reported a 12.2% year-on-year rise for the second quarter of 2026. Second-hand home prices climbed 12.9%, while new-build prices rose 7.4%.

Wages did not keep up. INE’s quarterly labour-cost survey shows labour cost per worker up 4.0% year on year in the second quarter, about a third of the pace of house prices.

Archive photo: a housing protest on Calle de Alcalá in Madrid in February 2025.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Driving the Divergence

Tourist rentals have become a central political target. The government says short-term lets remove homes from the long-term rental pool and push up prices in city centres.

On 23 October 2026, the Ministry of Social Rights, Consumer Affairs and Agenda 2030 demanded that two platforms remove 8,318 listings allegedly presented as seasonal rentals while permitting stays under 31 days. The ministry identified 6,772 of those listings in the Community of Madrid, including 6,523 in Madrid city.

Royal Decree-Law 29/2026, approved on 6 October and reported as entering into force on 8 October, requires seasonal rentals to last at least 31 days. The temporary reason for the tenancy must be documented, such as study or medical treatment.

The Ministry of Consumer Affairs had previously imposed a €64 million (about US$72 million) fine on Airbnb.

The Government’s Policy Response

Spain’s Council of Ministers approved two housing royal decree-laws in September and October 2026. The government described access to housing as one of the country’s principal public concerns.

Purchases by so-called vulture funds, investors who buy distressed property in bulk, face new restrictions.

The Actors and What Each Wants

Pedro Sánchez, President of the Government of Spain, has made housing a signature issue. Pablo Bustinduy, Minister of Social Rights, Consumer Affairs and Agenda 2030, leads the enforcement push against illegal tourist listings.

His ministry demanded the removal of 8,318 s in October 2026.José Luis Escrivá has led the Bank of Spain, the central bank, since September 2024.

Business and Investment Stakes

The housing squeeze cuts across Spain’s tourism economy, construction sector and rental market. Tourist flats are a significant income source in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and the Balearic Islands.

The new rules create compliance costs for platforms and property owners. Airbnb has already faced a €64 million (about US$72 million) fine, and more enforcement is likely.

For investors, the policy direction is clear: long-term rental supply is being prioritised over short-term tourist income.

What It Means for the United States

American buyers in Spain face higher entry prices, especially for second-hand homes in established neighbourhoods. The 12.9% annual rise in second-hand prices is the steepest segment of the market.

US expats who rent long-term may benefit if tourist flats return to the long-term market. Americans who own tourist flats should review the new seasonal-rental rules carefully.

Stays under 31 days now require a documented temporary reason.Spain’s policy response is more interventionist than most US state-level approaches, so American owners and buyers should expect tighter rules than at home.

The Latin American Echo

Spain’s housing debate resonates across Latin America, where tourist rentals have also transformed city centres. Cities such as Mexico City, Buenos Aires and Medellín face similar tensions between short-term rental income and long-term housing supply.

The Spanish approach of taxing tourist flats as businesses and requiring minimum stays is a template that Latin American policymakers are watching. The echo is a policy parallel, not a measured comparison.

Spanish-speaking investors and expats move between Spain and Latin America, making the regulatory direction relevant across both markets. The push to expand public housing also mirrors debates in several Latin American capitals.

Scenarios: What Could Stabilise or Tip the Market

A stabilising scenario would see the new rental rules shift tourist flats back into long-term supply. That could slow rent growth and ease pressure on city-centre prices.

A tipping scenario would involve weak enforcement of the seasonal-rental rules. If platforms and owners find loopholes, the supply squeeze could persist.

Higher interest rates or a tourism slowdown could also shift the market.

What It Means for You

If you are an American considering a Spanish property purchase, expect higher prices and more competition for second-hand homes. The policy direction favours long-term rental supply over short-term tourist income.

If you rent in Spain, the crackdown on short lets could improve your position. Document any seasonal rental reason carefully to avoid enforcement action.

If you invest in Spanish real estate, review the tourist-flat rules before committing capital. The regulatory environment is tightening, not loosening.

What Is Not Known

A precise Spain–US affordability comparison is not possible from official series: there is no directly comparable US house-price and income dataset.

What to Watch

INE’s next quarterly Housing Price Index will show whether the 12.2% annual pace is accelerating or cooling.INE’s next quarterly labour-cost survey will give a clearer read on whether wages are catching up.

Congress’s vote on the tourist-rental decree-law will determine whether the seasonal-rental rules stand as written.Watch for further enforcement actions against platforms and property owners.

The October 2026 demand to remove 8,318 listings is unlikely to be the last.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much have Spanish home prices risen in 2026?

Spain’s INE Housing Price Index rose 12.2% year on year in the second quarter of 2026. Second-hand home prices rose 12.9%, while new-build prices rose 7.4%.

How fast are wages rising in Spain?

INE’s quarterly labour-cost survey shows labour cost per worker up 4.0% year on year in the second quarter of 2026. That is about a third of the 12.2% rise in house prices.

What is Spain doing about tourist rentals?

Royal Decree-Law 29/2026 requires seasonal rentals to last at least 31 days. The government demanded removal of 8,318 illegal listings in October 2026.

What does the new tourist-rental rule require?

Royal Decree-Law 29/2026 requires seasonal rentals to last at least 31 days, with a documented temporary reason such as study or medical treatment.

How does Spain’s housing market affect American buyers?

American buyers face higher entry prices, especially for second-hand homes, and new rules on short-term rentals. Long-term renters may benefit if tourist flats return to the long-term market.

When does INE publish new housing price data?

INE publishes the Housing Price Index quarterly. The second-quarter figures came out on 7 September 2026.

World.title: Europe’s Top Defence Powers Meet in Paris
World.content:
FRANCE · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening The E5 defence ministers of France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom met in Paris on 26 October 2026 to coordinate support for Ukraine and European defence projects.

— Why it matters The format lets Europe’s five principal military powers align on capability gaps without waiting for wider NATO or EU consensus.

— The numbers Five countries issued one joint declaration on 26 October, calling Russia the “most acute and long-term threat” to Euro-Atlantic security.

— Who is who Catherine Vautrin, France’s armed forces minister, hosted the meeting.

— What to watch A date for the next E5 meeting, and whether the Ukraine air-defence plan gets national funding.

— What it means for you US defence contractors should read E5 announcements as political demand signals, not as funded NATO or EU procurement contracts.

The E5 defence ministers are an informal coordination format bringing together France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom. For US readers, the group matters because it is Europe’s most direct answer to Washington’s demand that allies carry more of their own defence burden.

France has become a recurring venue for a compact European defence conversation that sits outside both NATO and the EU. This analysis explains what the E5 is, what it has decided and why its Paris meeting on 26 October 2026 signals where European defence demand may flow.

The related Europe Intelligence Brief places the meeting in its wider context.

What The E5 Actually Is

The E5 is not a treaty-based alliance, an EU institution or a NATO command. France’s Defence Ministry calls it the European Group of Five, an informal ministerial format for rapid coordination among five of Europe’s principal military powers.

Its members are France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom. All five belong to NATO, while four are EU members and the United Kingdom sits outside the EU after Brexit.

That composition gives the group a bridge-building role. It lets London participate in continental defence discussions while allowing Paris, Berlin, Rome and Warsaw to connect those talks to EU defence initiatives.

The format has no standing secretariat, common budget or independent command structure. It operates through meetings convened by participating defence ministries, which makes it flexible but also harder to track than a formal institution.

Poland’s Ministry of National Defence described the Kraków meeting of 20 February 2026 as the seventh E5 ministerial meeting since 2024. That frequency shows the format has become a recurring rhythm rather than a one-off summit.

File photo: the Eiffel Tower in Paris. The E5 defence ministers met in the French capital on 26 October.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Poland Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How The Format Developed

The E5 emerged from three pressures. Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine created an urgent need to coordinate military support among Europe’s largest defence powers.

European governments also recognised gaps in air defence, ammunition, drones and other capabilities exposed by the war. Finally, Washington’s repeated demand that European allies assume a larger share of the defence burden pushed governments to find faster coordination mechanisms.

The format should not be confused with other European groupings. The E5 comprises France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom, while the Weimar Triangle comprises only France, Germany and Poland.

Those distinctions matter because they define who is in the room and what decisions can be made.The group’s previous Paris meeting was on 12 March 2025, according to France’s Defence Ministry.That meeting was hosted by Sébastien Lecornu, then France’s armed forces minister.

What The E5 Has Decided

The most concrete E5 output is the Low-Cost Effectors & Autonomous Platforms initiative, known as LEAP. Launched at the Kraków meeting on 20 February 2026, LEAP aims to develop lower-cost air-defence weapons and autonomous platforms capable of protecting NATO airspace.

The British government announced LEAP as a multinational effort involving Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland. It links the programme directly to NATO air defence, but the initiative is not itself a NATO command or procurement agency.

The logic behind LEAP is economic as much as military. Expensive missile interceptors can be consumed quickly against relatively inexpensive drones and cruise missiles, creating a cost imbalance that European governments want to correct.

The Paris meeting of 26 October 2026 produced a joint declaration rather than a treaty. Reporting on it describes no new collective command and no binding troop commitment.

What Paris Produced

The joint declaration is dated 26 October 2026. It describes Russia as “the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability”.

Germany’s defence minister, Boris Pistorius, said the group is working with Ukraine on an air-defence system to supplement existing defences, including US-made Patriot missiles (a long-range US air-defence system). Winter aid packages for Ukraine were also assembled.

No new pledge amounts were reported.

The Actors And What Each Wants

Catherine Vautrin, France’s Minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs, hosted the Paris meeting. France wants the E5 to anchor European defence cooperation while keeping Paris at the centre of the conversation.

Germany brings industrial weight and budget capacity.Italy’s interest lies in Mediterranean security and ensuring that southern-flank concerns are not crowded out by the eastern focus on Ukraine.Poland is the group’s most exposed eastern member and the strongest advocate for urgent air-defence investment.The United Kingdom’s participation keeps Britain inside European defence planning despite Brexit, and it brings nuclear status and expeditionary experience.

The Economic And Business Stakes

For investors and defence contractors, the E5 is best read as a demand signal rather than a procurement pipeline. An E5 announcement may signal political support for a capability area, but it does not automatically constitute a funded programme or guaranteed order.

The capability areas most likely to benefit are those where European governments want faster and larger-scale production. Air defence, drones, autonomous systems, ammunition, sensors and related electronics sit at the top of that list.

Pooling demand among five large defence markets may help companies reach production volumes that individual national orders cannot provide. That is the industrial logic behind LEAP and similar cooperative projects.

The distinction between E5, NATO and EU matters commercially. A project launched through the E5 does not automatically qualify for EU financing through the European Defence Fund or become a NATO procurement programme.

US contractors should therefore treat E5 statements as early indicators of European intent. The gap between political announcement and funded contract can be wide, and the E5 has no common budget to close it.

What It Means For The United States And Latin America

Washington has long pushed Europe to carry more of its own defence burden. The E5 is the clearest European institutional response to that pressure, even though it remains informal and politically driven.

The group does not compete with NATO’s collective-defence system. NATO remains responsible for Article 5 (its mutual-defence clause), integrated military command, common defence planning and alliance-wide operational requirements.

The E5 operates below that level. It helps participating governments coordinate positions, launch joint capability projects and shape proposals that may later support NATO requirements.

For Latin American readers, the E5 matters as a case study in how middle powers organise defence cooperation without waiting for a superpower. Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Colombia face their own capability gaps, though their security environment differs sharply from Europe’s.

The E5 also shows how informal formats can move faster than treaty-based institutions. That lesson may resonate in regions where formal security organisations are slow or politically constrained.

The Scenarios

The stabilising scenario is that the E5 becomes a reliable pre-negotiation chamber. Five large European governments would align on Ukraine, air defence and industrial scale before taking positions into wider NATO or EU discussions.

That would make European defence cooperation faster without creating a new bureaucracy. It would also give Washington a clearer European counterpart on burden-sharing questions.

The tipping scenario is that the E5 remains a talking shop. Without a common budget, secretariat or binding procurement mechanism, its announcements could fail to translate into funded programmes.

A second risk is duplication. If E5 projects compete with EU or NATO initiatives rather than feeding them, the result could be fragmentation rather than scale.

The most likely path lies between those poles. The E5 will probably continue as a recurring political forum that occasionally produces concrete initiatives such as LEAP, while the harder work of funding and procurement stays with national governments and existing institutions.

What It Means for You

If you invest in or sell to the defence sector, track E5 statements as early indicators of European demand. The capability areas named in E5 announcements are where European governments want faster production, even if contracts lag behind.

If you follow US foreign policy, the E5 is evidence that Europe is building a more credible defence pillar within NATO. That may reduce pressure on Washington to lead every European security response.

If you do business in Europe, the E5’s informality is a feature, not a bug. It allows quick political alignment without the legal constraints of EU or NATO processes, but it also means decisions are not automatically enforceable.

What Is Not Known

Official sources say little about how the E5 began, so its origins are less documented than its recent activity.The group has no common budget, so its financial footprint cannot be quantified as of October 2026.The available statements do not establish that the E5 has created a new collective military command or made a legally binding commitment to deploy troops.

Those claims should be treated as unconfirmed unless a separate official communiqué emerges.We have not found an announced date or venue for the next E5 meeting as of 26 October 2026.

What to Watch

Watch for a confirmed date and venue for the next E5 ministerial meeting.Watch for any follow-up on LEAP.The initiative’s next milestone would be a national funding commitment or a joint procurement decision, which would signal that the E5 can move from announcement to acquisition.Watch for EU or NATO institutional responses to E5 projects.

If the European Defence Fund or NATO procurement bodies adopt E5 priorities, that would confirm the format’s bridge-building role.Watch for changes in ministerial participation.Further turnover could shift the group’s priorities.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the E5 group of defence ministers?

The E5 is an informal ministerial format bringing together the defence ministers of France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom. It coordinates on Ukraine, European defence capabilities and defence-industrial cooperation.

Is the E5 part of NATO or the EU?

No. The E5 is separate from both NATO and the EU. All five members belong to NATO, and four are EU members, but the format itself has no treaty basis, standing secretariat or common budget.

What has the E5 decided so far?

The most concrete E5 output is the LEAP initiative, launched on 20 February 2026 to develop lower-cost air-defence weapons and autonomous platforms. The group has also coordinated support for Ukraine and examined European defence projects.

Who attended the Paris E5 meeting on 26 October 2026?

France’s Catherine Vautrin hosted the defence ministers of Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, EU defence commissioner Andrius Kubilius and NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska also attended.

Why does the E5 matter for the United States?

The E5 is Europe’s most direct response to Washington’s demand that allies carry more of their own defence burden. It lets five large European powers align on capability gaps without waiting for wider NATO or EU consensus.

Does the E5 have its own budget?

No. Projects launched through the format rely on national funding and existing procurement channels.

When is the next E5 meeting?

No date has been announced as of 26 October 2026.

World.title: Yen Carry Trade Risks Before Japan’s 30 October Decision
World.content:
JAPAN · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening The Bank of Japan meets on 29–30 October 2026 with its policy rate at around 1.25%, and markets are repricing the yen carry trade before the decision.

— Why it matters A hawkish signal from Governor Kazuo Ueda could trigger yen appreciation and forced selling of US equities, Treasuries and Latin American currencies.

— The numbers Japan’s core inflation was 2.4% in September 2026, and the Bank of Japan’s policy rate is around 1.25% after a quarter-point hike agreed on 18 September and effective 24 September.

— Who is who Kazuo Ueda, the Bank of Japan’s governor, will hold a press conference after the decision.

— What to watch The policy statement on 30 October, Ueda’s press conference, the dollar–yen rate (USD/JPY) speed, peso and real reactions, and US equity volatility.

— What it means for you A portfolio that looks diversified across US stocks, emerging-market bonds and foreign currencies may share one hidden position: short yen and long global risk.

The yen carry trade is a leveraged strategy that borrows yen at low Japanese rates and invests in higher-yielding assets abroad, and it faces a critical test when the Bank of Japan meets on 30 October 2026. For US investors, the decision could trigger a rapid yen rally that forces hedge funds to sell American equities and Latin American currencies, even when those markets’ fundamentals have not changed.

Japan is the world’s third-largest creditor nation, behind Germany and China, with record net external assets of ¥561.8 trillion (about US$3.5 trillion) at the end of 2025, and is the source of some of the cheapest funding in global finance. This analysis explains how the yen carry trade works, why a Bank of Japan move can shake markets from New York to São Paulo, and what US investors should watch before the decision, drawing on the Asia Intelligence Brief.

How the Yen Carry Trade Works

The mechanics are simple in principle. An investor borrows yen at Japan’s low interest rate, sells the yen for dollars, pesos or reais, and buys higher-yielding assets in those currencies.

The return is roughly the foreign asset yield minus the yen funding cost, plus or minus the currency movement. In practice, the trade is often synthetic rather than a literal bank loan.

Hedge funds use foreign-exchange forwards, swaps, options and futures to create the same economic exposure: short yen, long a higher-yielding currency or risk asset.The Bank of Japan’s current policy rate is around 1.25% for the benchmark overnight lending rate (the uncollateralized overnight call rate), effective from 24 September 2026.

The Bank raised it by 25 basis points (0.25 percentage points) in a 7–2 vote, so it is low by global standards but well above years of near-zero or negative rates.The trade works when the yen is stable or weakening.

It unravels when the yen strengthens sharply, because repaying the yen loan requires more dollars, pesos or reais than the investor originally received.

File photo: the Tokyo skyline seen from Shibuya. The Bank of Japan decides on 30 October.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why a Bank of Japan Move Shakes Markets

The Bank of Japan does not need to raise rates to disrupt the carry trade. A hawkish statement, a change in bond-purchase guidance, or a press conference that signals further normalisation can be enough.

Higher Japanese rates reduce the interest advantage of the trade. More importantly, closing short-yen positions requires buying yen, which can create a self-reinforcing appreciation.

Losses on currency positions can force hedge funds to sell unrelated assets to meet margin calls. Volatility-targeting funds may cut exposure when currency volatility rises, and dealers may need to buy yen or sell risk assets as options move against them.

The risk is not theoretical. In August 2024, expectations of tighter Japanese policy coincided with a stronger yen and sharp selling in leveraged positions, while US and international equities suffered abrupt losses.

The key risk is not only the level of the BOJ’s rate but the speed and surprise of the adjustment. A rapid yen move is far more dangerous for leveraged portfolios than a gradual one.

Who Is Exposed

US Equities

US equities are exposed indirectly through leverage and global risk appetite. A disorderly yen rally can lead hedge funds and macro investors to sell liquid positions, including large-cap US stocks, to meet margin requirements.

The most vulnerable areas are highly valued growth stocks, semiconductor and technology shares held as liquid sources of cash, and stocks crowded into by leveraged funds. A yen-led selloff does not mean US corporate fundamentals have deteriorated.

US Treasuries

Treasuries can respond in opposite directions. A global risk-off episode may produce a safe-haven bid, pushing yields lower, while Japanese investors repatriating funds can weaken demand for US bonds.

Currency hedging costs determine whether Japanese investors want US bonds even when headline US yields are high. The initial response may be a Treasury rally during equity stress, followed later by reassessment of foreign demand.

Hedge Funds and Leveraged Investors

Hedge funds are among the clearest transmission channels. A fund can be profitable while the yen remains stable but face rapid losses when the yen rises against several funded currencies simultaneously.

Because many funds hold diversified portfolios, the yen carry trade can create selling in assets that were not part of the original currency position. Prime brokers tightening financing terms can amplify the pressure.

Mexican Peso and Brazilian Real

The Mexican peso has been a natural carry-trade destination because Mexico has historically offered substantially higher short-term interest rates than Japan. Investors borrowing yen may buy peso assets or use peso forwards to capture the rate differential.

The Brazilian real is another favoured high-yield currency. Investors may buy Brazilian local-government bonds, use derivatives or hold real exposure through funds and structured products.

Both currencies face two-sided risk. A yen rally can force investors to unwind positions, and local depreciation increases the loss for a yen-funded investor, even when country-specific fundamentals are unchanged.

The Policy Trigger on 30 October

The Bank of Japan’s next monetary-policy meeting is scheduled for 29–30 October 2026, with its policy statement due on 30 October. The current guideline keeps the overnight call rate at around 1.25%.

Governor Kazuo Ueda will hold a press conference after the decision. His tone on wages, inflation, consumption and financial conditions may matter more than the headline rate decision.

Japan’s September 2026 inflation data, released on 23 October, showed core CPI (excluding fresh food) up 2.4% year over year, slowing from 2.8% in August. The measure excluding fresh food and energy rose 2.1%, up from 2.0%.

Persistent inflation above the BOJ’s target can affect expectations for future policy. But the central bank must balance that against concerns about economic growth and the impact of a stronger yen on exporters.

A decision to hold rates can still be hawkish if the BOJ indicates that additional normalisation is likely. Conversely, a hike accompanied by concern about weak demand could limit the yen’s reaction.

What It Means for the United States and Latin America

For US investors, the carry trade is a hidden correlation risk. A portfolio that appears diversified across US stocks, emerging-market bonds and foreign currencies may contain one common position: short yen and long global risk.

A disorderly unwind would show up first in crowded technology positions and high-beta currencies. The Mexican peso and Brazilian real are liquid enough to be early sources of cash during a global deleveraging.

For Americans living in Japan or Latin America, the carry trade can affect more than financial portfolios. A stronger yen raises the dollar cost of yen expenses, while a weaker peso or real can increase the local-currency cost of imported goods and dollar-linked obligations.

The central risk is correlation, not any single market’s fundamentals. Investors should identify currency exposure, leverage, collateral requirements and the timing of cash needs before the Bank of Japan (BOJ) meeting.

Scenarios

In a stabilising scenario, the BOJ holds rates at 1.25% and Governor Ueda signals patience. The yen moves gradually, carry trades adjust without forced selling, and US equities and Latin American currencies continue to trade on their own fundamentals.

In a destabilising scenario, the BOJ hikes or signals an imminent increase, the yen rallies rapidly, and leveraged investors face margin calls. Selling spreads from crowded US technology positions to the peso and real, and correlations rise across otherwise unrelated markets.

A middle scenario involves a hawkish hold: no rate change but language that points to another hike soon. Markets would reprice gradually, but volatility would rise and the most leveraged positions would still face pressure.

What It Means for You

Check your portfolio for hidden yen exposure before 30 October. Funds that hold emerging-market bonds, high-yield currencies or leveraged macro strategies may be short yen without you knowing it.

If you hold Mexican peso or Brazilian real assets, understand that a yen rally can hit those positions even when local economic news is positive. The carry trade connects markets that appear unrelated.

For US equity investors, the first sign of a carry unwind is often a volatility spike alongside selling in crowded technology names. That is a liquidity event, not necessarily a change in corporate earnings.

What Is Not Known

The Bank of Japan has not signalled its October decision in advance. How much a carry trade earns depends on each investor’s own funding cost, so no single figure applies to everyone.

Costs for carry trades are broker- and instrument-specific, and a carry trade is not a risk-free arbitrage.

What to Watch

On 30 October 2026, watch the policy-rate decision and the statement’s forward guidance. Markets will distinguish between a one-off move and a sustained normalisation cycle.

Governor Ueda’s press conference follows the decision. His tone on wages, inflation and financial conditions may move markets more than the headline rate.

Watch USD/JPY speed, not only direction. A rapid yen move is more dangerous for leveraged portfolios than a gradual adjustment.

Monitor the Mexican peso, Brazilian real and Australian dollar for evidence of broad carry liquidation. US equity breadth and volatility will show whether selling is deleveraging rather than a narrow Japan-related move.

Treasury-market behaviour matters too. Falling yields with weaker equities indicate safe-haven demand; rising yields during equity stress suggest concern about foreign demand or forced selling.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the yen carry trade?

The yen carry trade is a leveraged strategy in which investors borrow yen at Japan’s relatively low interest rates, convert the proceeds into higher-yielding assets or currencies, and profit from the interest-rate gap, provided the yen does not strengthen sharply.

Why does a Bank of Japan move shake the yen carry trade?

A Bank of Japan rate increase, hawkish guidance, or reduced bond-market support raises yen funding costs and can trigger rapid yen appreciation, forcing investors to close short-yen positions and sell unrelated assets to meet margin calls.

When is the next Bank of Japan meeting?

The Bank of Japan’s next monetary-policy meeting is scheduled for 29–30 October 2026, with its policy statement due on 30 October 2026.

What is the Bank of Japan’s current policy rate?

The Bank of Japan’s current guideline is to keep the uncollateralized overnight call rate at around 1.25%, effective from 24 September 2026.

Which currencies are most exposed to a yen carry trade unwind?

The Mexican peso and Brazilian real have historically offered substantially higher short-term interest rates than Japan and are liquid enough to be early sources of cash during a global deleveraging.

How can US investors protect against yen carry trade risk?

US investors should identify currency exposure, leverage, collateral requirements and the timing of cash needs before the BOJ meeting, and understand that a portfolio diversified across US stocks, emerging-market bonds and foreign currencies may share one hidden position: short yen and long global risk.

World.title: Bank of Canada Rate Decision on 28 October Explained
World.content:
CANADA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening The Bank of Canada will announce its overnight-rate decision on 28 October 2026 at 09:45 ET.

— Why it matters The decision will move the Canadian dollar, borrowing costs and the price of US goods for Canadian buyers.

— The numbers The policy rate is 2.25%; September inflation was 3.1%, or 2.2% without gasoline.

— Who is who Tiff Macklem is Governor of the Bank of Canada and leads the Governing Council that sets the policy rate.

— What to watch The Monetary Policy Report (the Bank’s quarterly forecasts) released alongside the decision will show updated inflation and growth projections.

— What it means for you A stronger Canadian dollar would make US goods cheaper for Canadian buyers and support border-state retail and tourism.

The Bank of Canada interest rate announcement on 28 October 2026 is widely expected to deliver a 25-basis-point increase to 2.50%. For US exporters, border-state businesses and anyone holding Canadian dollars, the decision will reshape near-term exchange rates and cross-border purchasing power.

Canada’s central bank sets the price of money for more than 41 million people. This analysis explains what the Bank of Canada will likely decide, why inflation and weak growth have created a policy dilemma, and what the outcome means for the Canadian dollar and US-Canada trade, drawing on the US-Canada Intelligence Brief.

The Policy Dilemma Behind the Decision

The Bank of Canada enters its 28 October meeting facing two forces that pull in opposite directions. Inflation has reaccelerated above the Bank’s 2% target, while growth and employment have weakened.

Headline inflation rose to 3.1% in September from 3.0% in August, driven by gasoline prices up 27.8% on a year earlier. Without gasoline, inflation eased to 2.2% from 2.4%.

That nuance is central to the Bank’s dilemma: it must decide whether to treat the energy-driven spike as temporary or as a signal of more persistent price pressure.The labour market adds another layer of concern.

Economists who favour waiting point to softer employment and core inflation data, a weak housing market and the risk that US tariffs slow growth further.The Bank’s Governing Council, led by Governor Tiff Macklem, must weigh the risk of letting inflation expectations drift higher against the risk of tightening into an economy that is already losing momentum.

File photo: Toronto’s financial district, where the Bank of Canada’s decision will be watched.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Market Expects

Market pricing has moved materially toward a hike in the days before the decision. Before 17 October, futures priced only about a one-in-three chance of an October hike.

After Governor Tiff Macklem said the Bank’s inflation forecasts were likely to be revised higher, pricing jumped above 75%, and market reports on 26 October put it near 80%.A Reuters economist survey found that 19 of 34 economists, or 56%, expected a 25-basis-point hike.

The same poll found that a majority of respondents expect a further increase by March 2027.The market view is not unanimous.

Some analysts continue to expect the Bank to wait, arguing that weaker growth and trade uncertainty make an immediate hike unnecessarily risky.The practical interpretation is that a 25-basis-point hike to 2.50% is the base case.

A hold at 2.25% remains the main alternative, while a larger increase is not part of the current market discussion.The Bank may choose to hike while signalling that the next move is not automatic.

That would combine a modest inflation response with what the Intelligence Brief calls “strategic patience” on further tightening.

The Numbers That Matter

The current target for the overnight rate is 2.25%, with the Bank Rate (the rate the Bank charges commercial banks) at 2.50% and the deposit rate at 2.20%, unchanged since the 29 October 2025 decision.The key figures shaping the decision, as of October 2026, are:

Headline inflation: 3.1% year over year in September 2026, according to Statistics Canada, the national statistics agency.

Inflation excluding gasoline: 2.2%, down from 2.4% in August.

Gasoline prices: up 27.8% on a year earlier; all energy up 19.0%.

Policy rate: 2.25%, unchanged since 29 October 2025.

The Bank’s quarterly Monetary Policy Report, released alongside the rate decision at 09:45 Eastern Time, will provide updated projections for inflation and economic growth. Those projections are at least as important as the rate itself for markets.

The Bank of Canada sets the target for the overnight rate to influence short-term borrowing costs and broader financial conditions. The 28 October announcement is one of eight scheduled policy decisions in 2026.

The Actors and What They Want

Tiff Macklem is Governor of the Bank of Canada. He chairs the Governing Council, the policy-making body responsible for conducting monetary policy and promoting a safe financial system.

Carolyn Rogers is Senior Deputy Governor. The Governing Council comprises Governor Tiff Macklem, Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers, Deputy Governors Toni Gravelle, Marc-André Gosselin, Nicolas Vincent and Michelle Alexopoulos.

The responsible federal department is Finance Canada, headed in October 2026 by François-Philippe Champagne as Minister of Finance and National Revenue. The minister announced that Budget 2026 would be tabled on 5 November 2026, eight days after the rate decision.

The Bank’s Governing Council wants to bring inflation back to the 2% target without causing unnecessary damage to employment and growth. Finance Canada wants a stable fiscal backdrop that does not fight the central bank’s monetary policy.

The Federal Reserve is also meeting on 27-28 October, almost simultaneously with the Bank of Canada. The Canada-US rate differential may shift in either direction depending on what both central banks signal.

What It Means for the Canadian Dollar and US-Canada Trade

A hike would normally support the Canadian dollar by increasing the return on Canadian-dollar assets. But with roughly three-quarters of the market already expecting a 25-basis-point move, a hike alone may produce only a limited Canadian-dollar gain.

The currency is also sensitive to oil prices, global risk appetite and US monetary policy.The larger currency catalyst will be the Bank’s guidance.

A hawkish hike, with clear concern about persistent inflation or further increases, would likely push USD/CAD (the US dollar–Canadian dollar rate) lower, indicating a stronger Canadian dollar.A dovish hike, paired with an explicit pause signal, could produce little lasting Canadian-dollar support, especially if the Bank downgrades growth.

An unexpected hold would likely push USD/CAD higher as traders unwind hike bets.

US Exporters

US exporters selling into Canada could benefit from a rate-driven Canadian-dollar appreciation because Canadian customers would have greater purchasing power in US-dollar terms. The effect would be most relevant for industrial machinery, food and agricultural products, vehicles and parts, consumer goods, and cross-border services.

If the Bank hikes but signals that economic weakness limits further increases, the Canadian dollar may not strengthen much. US exporters should avoid treating the policy-rate decision as a guaranteed currency tailwind.

Border-State Consumers

Consumers in Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia and other regions with frequent US shopping trips would face higher or lower effective costs depending on USD/CAD. A stronger Canadian dollar reduces the Canadian-dollar price of US retail purchases, travel and services.

For US border communities, a stronger Canadian dollar can support Canadian shopping, tourism and hospitality demand. A weaker loonie can reduce that flow, particularly in discretionary retail and restaurants.

Canadian Exporters to the United States

A weaker Canadian dollar improves the price competitiveness of Canadian exports in the US market, but it also raises the cost of imported US inputs, machinery and components. Resource exporters may benefit from stronger US-dollar revenues, while manufacturers dependent on US inputs face higher costs.

Trade uncertainty complicates the usual currency logic. A weaker Canadian dollar can cushion exporters, but it cannot fully offset tariffs, border delays, regulatory barriers or a collapse in US demand.

The Scenarios

The most defensible pre-decision forecast is a 25-basis-point hike to 2.50%, followed by a cautious signal that further moves will depend on inflation persistence and the damage caused by weak growth and trade uncertainty.A hold remains plausible because September’s underlying inflation picture was softer once gasoline was excluded, and the economy faces an external shock from uncertain US-Canada trade.

A hold justified by improving inflation could limit the currency move.A hawkish hike, with clear concern about persistent inflation or further increases, would likely push USD/CAD lower and support the Canadian dollar.

A dovish hike, paired with an explicit pause signal, could produce little lasting Canadian-dollar support.The Federal Reserve’s own decision on 27-28 October could dominate the currency reaction if the two central banks send conflicting signals.

US Treasury yields may matter as much as the Bank of Canada’s own words.

What It Means for You

For US readers, the Bank of Canada interest rate announcement matters through three channels: Canadian borrowing costs, the USD/CAD exchange rate and cross-border purchasing power. A stronger Canadian dollar makes US goods cheaper for Canadian buyers and supports border-state retail and tourism.

For investors holding Canadian assets, the key is not simply whether the Bank hikes or holds. It is the combined change in the Bank’s overnight-rate path, its inflation forecast, its growth forecast, its assessment of trade uncertainty, and the Federal Reserve’s policy signal.

For US exporters, a rate-driven Canadian-dollar appreciation could improve Canadian purchasing power, but only if the Bank’s guidance supports a sustained currency move. A dovish hike may leave the exchange rate largely unchanged.

For expats and cross-border workers, the decision affects the value of Canadian-dollar earnings converted to US dollars. A stronger loonie improves the US-dollar value of Canadian salaries and savings.

What Is Not Known

The official sources available do not establish the 28 October outcome in advance. The rate, Bank Rate and deposit rate should be treated as pending until the Bank publishes its decision at 09:45 Eastern Time on that date.

It is not yet known whether the Bank will treat September’s gasoline-driven headline increase as temporary or as evidence of broader price pressure. The Monetary Policy Report will reveal the Bank’s updated inflation and GDP projections.

It is also not known how the Federal Reserve’s decision will interact with the Bank of Canada’s signal. The Canada-US rate differential may shift in either direction depending on what both central banks say.

A hold remains a live possibility.

What to Watch

The most important signals on 28 October 2026 will be the rate decision itself, the opening statement, and the Monetary Policy Report released at 09:45 Eastern Time. Watch for references to persistent inflation, inflation expectations and excess demand.

Core inflation measures will show whether the Bank views September’s gasoline-driven headline increase as temporary or as evidence of broader price pressure. Trade language will reveal any explicit assessment of US trade policy, tariffs, border frictions or export weakness.

The future-policy wording matters as much as the rate move. The Bank may say additional tightening is required, that it remains data-dependent, or that it can wait.

USD/CAD price action will show whether the Canadian dollar strengthens despite a widely expected hike, which would indicate a hawkish surprise, or weakens despite the hike, which would suggest a dovish interpretation.Budget 2026 is tabled on 5 November 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What time is the Bank of Canada interest rate announcement on 28 October 2026?

The Bank of Canada will publish its rate decision at 09:45 Eastern Time on Wednesday, 28 October 2026, alongside the quarterly Monetary Policy Report.

What does the market expect the Bank of Canada to do on 28 October?

Economists are split. A Reuters poll of 34 economists, taken on 21 to 23 October, found 19 expecting a hike; the others expect the Bank to wait.

How does the Bank of Canada decision affect the Canadian dollar?

A hawkish hike would likely push USD/CAD lower, indicating a stronger Canadian dollar, while a dovish hike or an unexpected hold could weaken the loonie.

Who is the Governor of the Bank of Canada in 2026?

Tiff Macklem is Governor of the Bank of Canada. He chairs the Governing Council that sets the policy rate.

World.title: Chile Tornado Damages 20 Homes and a School
World.content:
Breaking: Chile

Chile’s weather service has preliminarily rated the Requínoa tornado EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita scale, and the disaster agency Senapred declared a red alert.

A tornado tore through central Chile late on Monday afternoon, leaving damaged homes, a damaged school and power cuts behind. The Requínoa tornado struck at about 5:30 p.m. local time (about 20:30 GMT) on Monday 26 October 2026.

Requínoa is a commune, the Chilean word for municipality, in the agricultural O’Higgins Region. The storm struck between Requínoa and the neighbouring town of Rengo.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Chile weather Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Tornadoes are uncommon in Chile. It matters to US readers who travel to central Chile’s farming country, and who already know the EF scale from home.

Key Facts Rating. Preliminary EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita scale, with winds of 179–218 km/h (111–135 mph).

Damage. At least 20 homes and one school damaged; the figure is preliminary and under evaluation.

Alert. Red alert, the highest level, declared for Requínoa; power cuts reported; no injuries reported at the time of writing.

Status. As of 26 October 2026, 22:30 GMT

Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

What We Know

Chile’s weather service, the Dirección Meteorológica de Chile (DMC), classified the tornado preliminarily as EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita scale. The scale runs from EF-0 to EF-5, and EF-2 is rated as considerable damage.

The DMC puts the winds at 179–218 km/h (111–135 mph). Because the rating is preliminary, those figures could still be revised.

EF-2 sits in the middle of the scale, above the weakest ratings and well below the most violent. US readers will know it as the level at which roofs can be torn from homes.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Senapred, Chile’s national disaster-prevention agency, declared a red alert for Requínoa, its highest alert level. More than 7,000 customers lost power, according to the first reports.

No injuries had been reported at the time of writing. The tornado came on a day of rain and thunderstorms in central Chile.

At least 20 homes were damaged, and one school was also hit. Senapred described its damage figures as still very preliminary and under evaluation.

The main north–south highway near Rengo, a town next to Requínoa. File photo: Aeveraal / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Cover photo, main square of Requínoa: Marco Antonio Correa Flores / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.
