World.title: Croatia is at Back of EU When it Comes to Electric Car Purchases
World.content:
October the 25th, 2026 – Despite the global climb in people buying electric vehicles, Croatia ranked at the very back of the EU when it comes to electric car purchases.

The share of fully electric cars among new cars is growing around the world, and in many countries it has reached record levels. Vedran Salvia reports for Index that this is clearly shown by the latest data from the international energy organisation Ember, which analysed car sales on global markets. Croatia is significantly lagging behind the other EU countries.

croatia is at the very back of the eu

According to Ember’s analysis, which tracks the share of fully electric cars (BEVs) among newly registered cars, Croatia recorded its own record during 2026, but despite that remained in last place in the European Union. From March to August such cars accounted for around 4.3 percent of all new registrations in Croatia. The data are based on rolling six-month periods because this presentation allows clearer tracking of trends.

The research covered 56 countries, while 49 of them are shown on the interactive chart, i.e. only those that achieved record shares during 2026. The difference between Croatia and the European leaders is extremely large. In Norway, which is not a member of the European Union, the share of fully electric cars reached as much as 97.8 percent, in Denmark 79.8 percent, in Finland 49.7 percent, in the Netherlands 42.8 percent and in Sweden 40.8 percent. The European Union average was 22.5 percent, more than five times higher than in Croatia. As for the EU members that are not shown on the chart, these are Poland and Romania, which did not achieve record shares of electric cars during 2026. However, both are ahead of Croatia. From March to August the share of fully electric cars among new registrations was 4.8 percent in Poland and 7.4 percent in Romania.

why is croatia lagging so much?

One of the reasons for the weaker sales of electric cars across Croatia could be their high price, especially in relation to average local purchasing power. That Croatian buyers are largely turning to used vehicles is also shown by data from the Croatian Vehicle Centre, according to which more used cars are imported into Croatia than new ones are registered, while the average age of passenger cars is more than 13 years. The European Commission in its 2026 report on Croatia also warns of the high costs of public charging of electric vehicles, problems with different charging systems and limited possibilities for home charging, especially for citizens who live in apartment buildings.

State incentives also play an important role; they are not awarded continuously but through occasional tenders. Available funds can sometimes be used up in just a few hours. Thus in 2024 citizens reserved all 15 million euros earmarked for subsidies in only four hours, after which the Environmental Protection Fund closed the tender. Such a system makes purchase planning more difficult because citizens cannot count on the constant availability of incentives.

large market differences

There are also significant differences among the large European markets. In France the share of fully electric cars was 30.6 percent, in Germany 27.5 percent and in Italy 8.3 percent. Germany and France have in recent years been moving towards an ever higher share of electric cars, while their penetration in Italy is considerably slower. Nevertheless, the Italian market is also recording growth, especially during 2026. Looking at absolute numbers, China is by far the world’s largest market for electric cars by the number of vehicles sold and is in a category of its own. According to Ember’s data, from January to August 2026 almost 4.46 million fully electric cars were registered there, which is almost half of the total of 9.33 million registered worldwide. In the EU in the same period around 1.65 million such cars were registered.

electric cars are conquering even emerging markets

The data show that the growth in the share of electric cars is no longer limited to developed European countries and China. Among the countries with high shares, Uruguay stands out with 40.2 percent, while in Thailand the share reached 28.8 percent and in Indonesia 24.2 percent. “Strong growth outside the USA and China was key to the continued growth in electric vehicle sales. Excluding the USA and China, global BEV sales rose by an estimated 45% in the period from January to August 2026 compared with the same period of the previous year,” the research states. At the same time, electric cars in some large countries still occupy a relatively small part of the market. In India their share is 7.4 percent, in Japan 3.3 percent and in Mexico only 2.1 percent.

the usa didn’t even make it on the chart

Ember particularly highlights the example of the United States of America, which did not even make it among the 49 countries with record shares of electric cars shown on the chart. After last year’s abolition of federal support for electric vehicles, their share among new vehicles fell to only six percent in the first eight months of 2026. Looking at everything in absolute numbers of electric cars sold the USA stands considerably better. From January to August around 640 thousand such vehicles were registered there, which puts it in second place in the world, immediately behind China. However, the American car market is so large that electric cars still make up a small part of total sales. According to Ember’s analysis, as many as 49 of the 56 observed countries now have a higher share of electric cars than the USA, and during this year alone 15 countries overtook it, among them Brazil, India, Italy, Malaysia and New Zealand.

electric cars and energy security

Ember emphasises in its analysis that the spread of electric cars affects not only the car market but also the energy security of states. According to the organisation’s estimates, electric cars in oil-importing countries from March to August this year replaced oil consumption worth around 20 billion dollars.

The authors of the research conclude that the electrification of transport can reduce states’ exposure to disruptions on the oil market and sudden changes in fuel prices. “Countries that invested in electric cars before this crisis are now better protected, and their example is being followed by an increasing number of other countries. Every electric car on the road reduces exposure to volatile oil markets, and as their number grows, so does protection against future supply disruptions,” the research states.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan sign nine memoranda of understanding
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Jordan signed on Monday nine memoranda of understanding and executive programs in Amman.

The agreements were finalized during an official visit by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who met with Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan and King Abdullah II to enhance bilateral ties and economic integration.

The agreements span economic, diplomatic, educational, and cultural sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The agreements include managing competition policies and preventing market monopolies, protecting the ecosystem and biodiversity, a five-year plan to expand university research cooperation and academic partnerships, and mechanisms to safeguard consumer rights and trade standards, as well as collaboration on historical preservation, manuscripts, and national archives.

They also cover a partnership between Iraq’s Foreign Service Institute and Jordan’s Diplomatic Institute, support for small and medium-sized enterprises, an executive program for bilateral cultural exchange, and a multi-year framework establishing core educational sector cooperation.

Al-Zaidi formally proposed establishing a joint free zone to boost commercial volume and position Iraq as a regional economic hub.

The Iraqi prime minister’s trip to Jordan comes ahead of planned visits to Lebanon and Syria.

World.title: Vessel reportedly catches fire off the coast of Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) issued a warning on Monday after receiving multiple third-party reports of a vessel on fire 63 nautical miles (116.6 kilometers) southeast of al-Faw, Iraq.

The UKMTO has officially classified the incident as suspicious activity. The crew’s current status, the exact extent of the damage, and any potential environmental impacts remain unknown.

The warning issued on Monday did not identify the vessel or specify the cause of the fire.

According to UKMTO, vessels transiting the northern Arabian Gulf are advised to exercise extreme caution and report any suspicious activity to authorities.

Attacks and hostile security incidents targeting commercial vessels in the far northern Arabian Gulf near Iraq have surged drastically, turning the waters surrounding Iraq’s primary oil terminals into an active maritime conflict zone.

A few days ago, a tanker’s master claimed being hit by an unidentified missile 30 nautical miles (55.5 kilometers) southeast of al-Faw in a different incident.

World.title: Iraq proposes establishing free zone with Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi emphasized on Monday the importance of establishing a free zone between Iraq and Jordan to bolster trade exchange between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place when he and Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan co-chaired an expanded meeting between the Iraqi and Jordanian delegations in the capital, Amman.

The meeting addressed approaches to strengthen bilateral relations in different sectors, particularly energy, the economy, and investment, to serve the mutual interests of both countries, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

As it aims to enhance cooperation in the economic, commercial, industrial, and security sectors, al-Zaidi emphasized the importance of his visit to Jordan.

The meeting addressed regional developments, emphasizing the importance of the Palestinian cause.

In addition to supporting diplomatic efforts to confront obstacles, resolve crises, and lessen their negative impacts at the regional and global levels, it emphasized the significance of securing justice for the Palestinian people and restoring their full rights.

Al-Zaidi underscored Jordan’s role as a strategic partner and expressed Iraq’s eagerness to enhance cooperation with its neighboring country to tackle various challenges and further strengthen bilateral relations.

World.title: Iraqis mark 7th anniversary of 2019 Tishreen Uprising
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Thousands of Iraqis gathered on Sunday in Baghdad’s Tahrir Square and southern provinces to mark the seventh anniversary of the 2019 Tishreen (October) Uprising.

Major centers, including Baghdad, Najaf, Nasiriyah, and Basra saw a resurgence of protests, with activists bringing national and local problems back to the scene.

Activists are still calling for justice and the punishment of those who murdered more than 600 demonstrators during the initial crackdowns in 2019.

Protesters explicitly voiced their opposition to regional external influence, shouting anti-Iranian chants and demanding an end to foreign interference in Iraqi politics.

The muhasasa system, a sectarian political quota system that divides political posts and state resources among controlling parties, is still being opposed by protesters.

Protesters demanded that all weapons be restricted to state authority, targeting the power of Iranian-backed armed militias operating in the country.

Popular infrastructure failure, significant young unemployment, and widespread government corruption continue to be major sources of public frustration.

Iraqi security officials deployed forces to safeguard important squares and public areas ahead of the anniversary, putting soldiers in Baghdad on high alert to prevent possible escalations.

The 2019 Tishreen Uprising was the largest, longest-lasting, and most significant social movement in Iraq’s post-2003 history.

The nonviolent movement, which was mostly spearheaded by frustrated youth, broke out in Baghdad and southern Iraq on October 1, 2019, demanding a complete reform of the country’s political system.

World.title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
World.content:
Manchester – Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price.

The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline.

“I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said.

Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job.

The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired.

David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching.

– Sentimental choice –

Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson.

“The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports.

“But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.”

The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout.

Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts.

Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed.

Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion).

United, who for years bullied their rivals in the transfer market, lost out on the biggest names as they targeted a summer midfield rebuild, with Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes all choosing other clubs.

United instead recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — none of whom have made a strong impression — for combined fees of about £150 million.

Significant rifts have emerged in recent weeks.

Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox for not doing more to strengthen Carrick’s squad.

Last week captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 humbling by Champions League debutants Como.

Carrick is expected to take the blame, but the route back to the top for one of the world’s biggest clubs appears tougher than ever.

“It can’t just be the manager again. There has got to be consequences above that. You can’t keep letting the people pick the manager who keep getting it wrong,” said Neville.

“It’s years now without a Premier League title. That will be another five or 10 before you know it because there are other clubs set up for success and Manchester United aren’t.”

World.title: Kane tipped to beat Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d’Or glory
World.content:
London – Harry Kane is favourite to become England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years when the award is presented in London on Monday, but he faces stiff competition from La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas is the clear frontrunner to win the women’s prize for a third time, with Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign set to come to an end after an injury-hit spell.

The ceremony to decide the world’s best male and female footballers is being held in London for the first time — 70 years after England winger Stanley Matthews was presented with the inaugural award.

Bayern Munich and England forward Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and at the World Cup in the United States mean a triumph for Kane at the London Palladium is far from certain.

“I’d love to be able to achieve something like that. It would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old former Tottenham forward.

“I think my wife would prefer to know and my family… it’s very stressful for everyone,” added the England captain.

Only four players from England have won the Ballon d’Or. Michael Owen was the last to triumph in 2001, following in the footsteps of Matthews, Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany praised Kane’s focus on his team, saying: “What made Harry happy the most in recent years is that he finally won his first team trophies here.

“Now if he can crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be deserved for the way he plays for the team.”

– ‘I deserve it’ –

Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d’Or winner one day.

However, a hamstring injury ended his club season early and he failed to show his most irresistable form during Spain’s World Cup triumph, which was built on impressive teamwork.

But that has not diminished his confidence ahead of the ceremony.

“For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” Yamal said last month.

“I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won.”

Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France.

The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies.

His 10 World Cup goals in North America made him the top goalscorer in the competition’s history, on 22.

“Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” said Mbappe.

“Who am I voting for? Myself.”

The Ballon d’Or was established by the magazine France Football, with the first award given to Matthews in 1956.

One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA’s rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist.

Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player’s overall market value.

Putellas, winner of the women’s award in 2021 and 2022, was a member of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses.

Her former Barcelona team-mate, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, is Putellas’s main challenger after scoring 11 Champions League goals in Barca’s latest triumph.

World.title: Iraqi PM makes official visit to Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived on Monday in the Jordanian capital, Amman, for his first official visit to the neighboring country since taking office.

King Abdullah II received Al-Zaidi at Amman Civil Airport. Leading a high-level delegation, al-Zaidi’s visit comes in response to an invitation from the Jordanian king.

Amid ongoing tensions, the two leaders are meeting to discuss security concerns in the region, joint development initiatives, and economic cooperation.

The two countries are expected to sign several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) to advance joint economic initiatives.

Al-Zaidi and King Abdullah II are expected to discuss approaches to strengthen bilateral relations, as well as mechanisms for cooperation to address various challenges.

Furthermore, the two leaders will chair an expanded meeting between the delegations of the two countries and oversee the signing of several memoranda of understanding aimed at fostering cooperation, integration, and economic partnership, while safeguarding mutual interests.

The trip reflects a shared vision between Baghdad and Amman to expand regional dialogue and promote solutions that ensure long-term stability across the Middle East.

World.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
World.content:
Riyadh – Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.

Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday.

Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July.

Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defence alliance in Mecca in August.

Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume.

Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV.

“This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X.

“The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.”

– ‘Serious tensions’ –

On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen.

The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month.

Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.

“Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighbouring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday.

Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia”.

Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions.

“For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just… sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP.

“There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added.

“And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.”

– ‘Don’t test us’ –

Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged.

Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28.

On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power.

“We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said.

“Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials.

The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

World.title: More violence in Arunachal as anti-dam protests spread
World.content:
PASIGHAT/ITANAGAR: A 12-hour bandh against a proposed hydropower project in Arunachal Pradeshâs Upper Subansiri district turned violent Monday, with mobs damaging vehicles and NHPC equipment and wounding two security personnel as anti-dam protests spread from Siang basin to Subansiri valley, report Kangkan Kalita and Joken Ete.

The latest flashpoint was Daporijo town, 220km west of Pasighat by road. NHPC equipment, a company vehicle and two police vehicles were damaged during the bandh called by All Tagin Studentsâ Union and other organisations against Menga dam, part of the proposed 1,605MW Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project. Police conducted a flag march in Daporijo and appealed for peace.

Remove central forces, say protesters; depends on restoration of peace: Government

Constable-driver Hibu Lasha and a CRPF man were wounded. Both were shifted to Ziro for treatment,â Upper Subansiri SP Pawan Kumar Yadav said.

The bandh began at 5am over opposition to the proposed Menga dam and an alleged attempt to detain ATSU president Tadak Pakba. Backed by student unions and community groups from the Subansiri basin, the agitation grew out of fears that the project would threaten their land, livelihoods, and future.

Earlier, Pasighat recorded widespread arson, vandalism and clashes with security forces when protesters laid siege to the East Siang district headquarters from Friday night to early Saturday over the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), with its main reservoir planned near Geku village, about 35km downstream from Upper Siang district headquarters Yingkiong.





The Siang flows from Tibet into the ancestral land of the Adi community inhabiting Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts, while Upper Subansiri is home to the Tagin community. The Adi and Tagin people are closely related.

Tension continued in Upper Siang, where protesters demanded the release of people arrested for the violence and four activists placed under preventive detention. They also demanded the withdrawal of central security forces and an immediate halt to the pre-feasibility survey for the project.

World.title: Border patrols normal, let’s work for peace: China
World.content:
After India accused China of carrying out activities detrimental to peace, Beijing said Monday it is strictly abiding by relevant agreements and âconducts normal border patrol.

.. activities to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and stability in border areasâ.

âWe hope India will work with China in the same direction by jointly implementing the common understandings reached between the two sides and maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas with concrete actions,â said a Chinese foreign ministry official.

World.title: June 2025 decision to hold SIR taken unanimously, EC tells SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Election Commission Monday filed an affidavit in SC that the chief election commissioner and the two election commissioners had unanimously taken the decision on June 24, 2025 to conduct nationwide SIR of electoral rolls and that there was no difference of opinion.

The affidavit by deputy EC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu came with an unusual declaration that it was being filed with the approval of the CEC and the two ECs. âAt the very outset, I state that the present affidavit has been approved for filing before the SC by a unanimous decision of the three members of the Election Commission, that is the 2 election commissioners and the chief election commissioner,â the affidavit said.

The assertion contradicts the charge that CEC Gyanesh Kumar, at Modi governmentâs instance, unilaterally decided to conduct SIR of electoral rolls â the mainstay of the oppositionâs âvote choriâ campaign.

The affidavit was filed in response to petitions, including one filed by

and other opposition leaders, following a news report that the two ECs â S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi â had approached the cabinet secretary because of their differences with the CEC over SIR-related issues.

âAllegations based on the communication between ECs and the cabinet secretary are misconceived,â the EC said, adding that the letters by Sandhu and Joshi pertained to administrative matters.





No substance in claim that Form 6 was amended by SIR orders: EC

An office order came to be issued on July 28 by an IAS officer of the rank of additional secretary who had been posted on deputation to the commission pertaining to internal work allocation. On July 29, the two election commissioners wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary in relation to this order and the conduct of the officer. In view of the joint direction of July 30 by the two ECs, the order of July 28 was never implemented,â the commission said.

Responding to the petitions by Rahul and other INDIA bloc netas, the EC said all the petitions were based on a news article alleging that the commission had not been functioning in accordance with the procedure mandated in law, and allegations were also made questioning the integrity of the commission.

It also issued a strong denial of the allegation, another key plank of the oppositionâs offensive, that Form 6, as provided under Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was amended by the commission by the SIR orders of June 24 and Oct 27 last year and May 14 this year.

âThere is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the commission vide the SIR orders.â EC said Form 6 could be amended only by the Centre and what was changed was the introduction of a declaration to âenable the person seeking registration as a voter to dispense with the need for filing documents during the claims and objections periodâ.

The âdeclarationâ was a document provided by the SIR orders and was not a part of Form 6, which was the statutory form for inclusion in the electoral rolls, it said, adding there was no significant change in the earlier and present declaration.

The declaration that the affidavit was approved by the two ECs is significant because of the charge that the CECâs âunilateralâ calls on SIR-related issues were violative of the law, which required the poll body to take decisions unanimously or, when not possible, by majority.

The opposition has demanded removal and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar for violating the law.

Denying the charge, the affidavit said that while the CEC, the ECs and even other officers may have expressed different views during deliberations, the decisions were taken in accordance with law.

âThe views by ECs/CEC of the commission during the decision-making process on the subjects before them are considered for arriving at the decision. It is upon consideration of all the views placed before the commission that the decision is taken and the orders are issued in accordance with the process,â the EC said.

Explaining the process of decision-making in which views of all divisions concerned with the subject are considered in detail, the EC said, âIn any such decision-making process, any suggestion, observation or query by the CEC or ECs either to the ECs or CEC or to any officer of the commission does not constitute a decision of the commission under Section 18 of the CEC and ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

â

It said the statute prefers a decision by unanimity but also provides for decision-making by majority in the three-member EC. The commission said the CEC and ECs had taken a unanimous decision on June 29 that âin case any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and/or logical discrepancies, BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them in the ECINet, for decision by the EROâ.

âSuch person shall not be called for hearing to the ERO/AERO officer. Only in exceptional circumstances, as defined by the ERO/AERO, will the hearing be held, preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf,â EC said. Referring to the allegation relating to deletion of 97 voters in Goa, the commission said it had directed that no eligible voter should be left out of the rolls and pursuant to this, the BLOs conducted a house-to-house visit and found that 88 of the 97 had already filled Form 6 for inclusion of their names.

Of the remaining nine, six were out of the country and three were Portuguese passport holders.

World.title: SC to UP police: Educate officers on investigation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a severe indictment of Uttar Pradesh police for carrying out a âslipshod investigationâ that resulted in a man being in custody for six years when there was no evidence against him, Supreme Court Monday said the state cannot shirk its responsibility to protect citizens and directed it to pay a compensation of Rs 6 lakh to him.

âThis is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a personâs life and liberty,â SC noted at the outset of its verdict.

On Sept 30, in a separate matter, the top court had slammed UP police for not naming the accused in a road accident case.

Appalled at the way UP cops carried out probe: SC

It would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police works with an agenda and does cover-up jobs, court had said, noting the accused had not been named despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police.

In the present case, a bench of J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to implicate the person in a kidnapping and murder case. It noted he was never named in the FIR and police made him an accused on the basis that he was seen in CCTV footage. SC said it was âappalled at the manner in which investigation was carried outâ. âIt is unfortunate that despite no evidence against the petitioner, he was imprisoned for six years as an undertrial.





Based on a slipshod investigation, a haphazard prosecution was carried out, which resulted, fortunately, in the acquittal of the accused. We cannot but deprecate the manner in which the probe was carried out and prosecution conducted,â SC said. âState police would do well to educate their officers in the process of investigation.â

Making the state accountable for policeâs misdeed, the court said six years have been erased from the manâs life on the strength of a concocted story built on mere surmises and conjectures, and the state has to pay compensation.

âThe state cannot shirk from its responsibility to protect its citizens, especially when a person arraigned in a criminal case is presumed innocent until proven guilty. The investigation and prosecuting agencies exist not merely to, and by whatever means, bring in a conviction. They should recognise themselves to be essential stakeholders in the justice delivery system, ensuring justice, not only to the victim, the de facto complainant and the injured but also to the accused,â the SC bench said.

World.title: No action on deleted voters using Form 6: Supreme Court
World.content:
New Delhi: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, the

verbally assured electors on Monday. It allayed fears that use of Form 6, which asks applicants to declare they are fresh voters, for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration.

The statement came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL against large-scale exclusion of names from

âs draft electoral roll and as a response to senior advocate Aravind Datarâs plea that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to lying under oath.

Will grant time to genuine voters to submit papers if out from final list: SC

The bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, to be published on Nov 6, it could grant them more time to submit their documents for the purpose.

A similar concern was raised by advocate Prashant Bhushan 10 days earlier while questioning the ECâs directive that voters whose names were deleted from Delhiâs draft electoral roll during SIR exercise use Form 6 to restore them in draft rolls.

Datar said that with two crore voters excluded from Maharashtraâs draft electoral roll, including 1.22 crore on grounds of logical discrepancy, and the deadline for claims and objections ending on Oct 26, many voters who were removed on flimsy and non-existent grounds would have little chance of getting names restored.





The senior advocate requested the bench to extend the Oct-26 deadline for those seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral roll. The bench asked the EC to file its response to the PIL by Nov 5 and said it would examine on that day whether extra time would be required for those seeking inclusion of names.

Datar said, âIn Maharashtra, 33% of voters have been deleted. In Mumbai, 40% of the voters have been excluded. What is happening is people are asked to fill Form 6, which is meant for fresh voters.

There is no provision for a person who had voted in the last three or four elections to get his name restored in the voter list. If he fills Form 6, which is meant for registration of fresh voters, then he would face prosecution for false declaration.

â

However, the CJI allayed these fears and said, âNo one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists.â Datar said that since there was no imminent election in Maharashtra, the SC could direct EC not to finalise the electoral roll for the state on Nov 6 and postpone the schedule to enable genuine voters to re-enter them in voter lists. The bench also said, âIf we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists.

World.title: A cooling-off period for MPs, MLAs who quit? SC to decide
World.content:
SC agrees to examine whether MPs and MLAs who resign voluntarily should bear by-election costs and face a five-year cooling-off period before contesting again.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a development that could impact politics of shifting loyalties, SC Monday agreed to examine whether an MLA or an MP who contests a by-election caused by their voluntary resignation should be made to bear the entire expenses incurred by Election Commission in conducting the previous poll.Senior advocate Shoeb Alam told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that six persons elected on AIADMK tickets to the Tamil Nadu assembly had resigned in May and June after declaration of results and defected to TVK. Two of them resigned, causing by-elections which they went on to win, this time as TVK candidates.Appearing for petitioner K Suthan, Alam said the court was required to examine whether a person who voluntarily resigned as an MLA or MP should be barred for five years from contesting a state or parliamentary election. SC issued notices to Centre, EC and the six AIADMK MLAs who resigned and defected.The trend of lawmakers crossing over to the party in office and quitting their seats to avoid disqualification has caught on. The petitioner has sought legislative or regulatory measures âto create a mechanism for ensuring financial accountability of elected representatives who prematurely resign from their seats without legally recognised compelling circumstances, including introduction of an âElection Expenditure Securityâ to recover cost of resultant bye-electionsâ.He has requested the court to direct Centre and EC to examine and initiate ânecessary legislative and/or regulatory measures to introduce a statutory disqualification or a reasonable cooling-off period to prevent elected representatives who voluntarily and prematurely resign from contesting subsequent pollsâ. Suthan has suggested a five-year cooling-off period.The petitioner contended that none of the vacancies in the six seats was caused by death, permanent disability, disqualification or other compelling circumstance warranting a bypoll. âPublic shouldnât be made to pay twice for polls to the same constituency because of an individualâs personal or political choice to resign,â he said.Refusing to entertain Suthanâs petition, a Madras HC bench led by CJ S A Dharmadhikari had said, âWe are being asked to design a punitive and financial regime that would operate as a fresh disqualification under Constitution and would curtail statutory right to contest election.In our opinion, the same is a matter of legislative policy, not of judicial direction.ââRight to resign a legislative seat is itself a facet of the constitutional scheme governing membership of a House and cannot be burdened with extra-statutory conditions by judicial order, however sound the underlying concern may be,â the HC had said while refusing the plea to impose a five-year cooling-off period on MPs and MLAs who voluntarily resign from their seats in the House concerned.

World.title: From Andamans to Zanskar, e-Sanjeevani bridges distances, posts 50cr consultations
World.content:
PM Modi outlines key milestones in 139th 'Mann Ki Baat' (file photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: High fever and laboured breathing threatened the life of Oho-Tahane, a child from Jarawa tribe of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. With specialist care out of reach, health workers turned to e-Sanjeevani for remote consultation. The doctor diagnosed pneumonia, and timely expert intervention helped the childâs condition improve rapidly.Oho-Tahane, a member of one of Indiaâs most vulnerable tribal groups, is among over 50 crore cases, many in far flung areas, facilitated by the national telemedicine service since its launch in Nov 2019.The serviceâs achievement was highlighted by PM Narendra Modi in his âMann Ki Baatâ address Sunday, as he also cited how e-Sanjeevani enabled a doctor to guide a medical team in treating Kunhi Koya (60) in Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, and helped ensure medical assistance for pregnant Kunjang Dolma in Himalayan region of Zanskar.Developed by C-DAC Mohali under the health ministry, e-Sanjeevani facilitates 2.5-3 lakh daily consultations, offers services in 15 languages and is available across all 36 states and UTs. Women account for 57.1% of the platformâs utilisation, while people aged 46 and above account for 40.1% of consultations. Those aged 60 and above account for 16.2%. The platform has recorded a peak of 6,30,315 consultations in a single day.Modi credited the platformâs reach to dedication of doctors, public trust and the effective use of technology. He highlighted 1.9 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, saying they were bringing healthcare closer to rural communities and evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats. Regular health check-ups were becoming more common in rural areas, he said, with e-Sanjeevani playing an important role.The PM also highlighted advances in brain research, referring to Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT-Madras, which he inaugurated this month. The centre has developed a brain imaging technology platform to create high resolution digital 3D images of human brain. Its mission is to map and study 100 human brains in detail using Param Shakti supercomputer..Modi said the initiative could deepen understanding of the brain, particularly as conditions such as Alzheimerâs disease and dementia lack a definitive cure. Data from the 100 brains will be available as an open-source resource for researchers, the PM added.

World.title: Brazil election ‘rigged’, says Trump without citing evidence
World.content:
U.S. ‌President Donald Trump ​told reporters on ⁠Monday (October 26, 2026), without citing evidence, that the Brazilian election, ‌which leftist President Luiz Inacio ‌Lula da ‌Silva ⁠won on Sunday (October 25, 2026), looked ⁠like it had been rigged.

“I didn’t take ​sides, but ‌it looked like another rigged election,” he said. “Elections have to ‌be indisputable, and ​it looked very bad to me.”

Defeated ⁠right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has refused ‌to concede defeat.

His father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a close ally of Mr. Trump’s ‌while in office.

A ​wave of recent right-wing election victories ⁠in other Latin American ⁠countries has been heralded by ‌Trump’s administration.

World.title: Kochi Corporation eyes flyover funds to fix battered footpaths
World.content:
Hard-pressed to mobilise funds for the renovation of footpaths, the Kochi Corporation is exploring the possibility of approaching the Kerala High Court with a plea seeking a direction to Cochin Smart Mission Limited (CSML) to divert funds earmarked for the beautification of two flyovers towards the more pressing task of renovating footpaths.

The Corporation’s move comes in the wake of repeated directions from the High Court regarding the condition of footpaths in the city. Though the civic body has taken up the matter with CSML, there has been no positive response. According to the Corporation, around ₹12 crore has been allocated for the beautification of the Palarivattom and Vytilla flyovers.

“Such a huge allocation for mere beautification is unjustified, especially considering the fact that both flyovers fall within the stretch covered by the National Highways Authority of India’s elevated highway project, rendering any such beautification redundant. Utilising those funds for the renovation of footpaths would be far more reasonable and logical. Since the High Court has been issuing repeated directions on ensuring safe footpaths, we are considering approaching the court through the amicus curiae with such a request,” said Mayor V.K. Minimol.

However, CSML authorities maintained that such a diversion of funds midway through the process is not permissible. The funds have been allocated under the Urban Rejuvenation and Beautification Scheme. If anything, a fresh proposal would have to be submitted for footpath renovation.

“Anyway, the proposal is on hold at present since it was to be funded through the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board [KIIFB]. Except for ongoing projects, all others have been put on hold as the State government’s position on KIIFB is yet to be clarified. Also, CSML is largely in a closure mode, having run its course,” said CSML sources.

The Ernakulam District Residents’ Associations’ Apex Council (EDRAAC) alleged that footpaths along several stretches in the city were in a deplorable condition, in violation of the Supreme Court’s directive recognising the right to walk on safe, demarcated and well-maintained footpaths as a fundamental right.

“The situation is particularly bad at several points along Shanmugham Road and M.G. Road. Tiles have come loose along many footpaths. The agency concerned should take immediate steps to repair them,” said EDRAAC president Rangadasa Prabhu.

World.title: Traffic regulations in Aluva from Oct. 28 for bridge repair work
World.content:
Traffic regulations will be in place in Aluva from October 28, 2026, to November 6, 2026, as the old Marthanda Varma Bridge will be closed for maintenance work.

Thus, all heavy vehicles travelling from Thrissur to Ernakulam should divert at Irinjalakuda and proceed via Kodungallur, North Paravur and Cheranalloor. Heavy vehicles travelling from Thrissur to Aluva must divert at Angamaly and take the Kalady-Perumbavoor road. Similarly, heavy vehicles travelling from Vyttila to Aluva must proceed towards Cheranalloor and take the North Paravur-Kodungallur road. Heavy vehicles from Kalamassery and Angamaly will not be permitted to travel towards Aluva during this period, says a release.

Buses and other heavy vehicles from Varapuzha and Kadungallur must turn at Kadungallur Junction and proceed to Aluva via UC College Road and North Paravur. Heavy vehicles travelling in the opposite direction must turn left at Thottakattukara Junction and proceed to Kadungallur. Traffic will not be permitted on the NH service road leading to Thottakattukara.

Smaller vehicles will be permitted to travel in either direction across the new Marthanda Varma Bridge, while a one-way system will be introduced in Aluva town if necessary. Those travelling to the airport should start their journeys well in advance, anticipating traffic restrictions. The public is advised to rely on public transport to reduce congestion, the release says.

World.title: CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge, ECI tells top court
World.content:
The Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners have filed a joint affidavit highlighting that any attempt to restrain the functioning of the CEC will be contrary to law.

The nearly 250-page document filed in the top court late on Monday (October 26, 2026) said a CEC cannot be removed from office except in the manner and the grounds identical to ousting a Supreme Court judge.

The affidavit said a media report on the inner frictions and alleged unilateral or authoritarian functioning of the CEC was hardly evidence in court. Petitions basing itself on media reports should not be even maintainable in court.

Petitioners who have challenged the functioning of the CEC include the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and other INDIA bloc leaders. Other petitioners include Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi.

The affidavit, which shows the CEC to be on the same page as both Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, said the Commission had “neither released nor authorised the release of any internal note or file to any news agency”.

They submitted that the multi-member Commission, in case of any “difference of opinion” would follow the rule of majority to arrive at decisions in accordance with Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

‘No unilateral decisions’

The affidavit indicated that there was no room for unilateral decision making in the ECI. Decisions were vetted at various levels.

“Decisions are first sent to one Election Commissioner and then to the other Election Commissioner and then finally to the CEC. Such approved decisions of the EC are duly noted in the files concerned of the EC and bear the signature of the Election Commissioners and the CEC. Thereafter, the decision is notified and implemented by the EC Secretariat,” the affidavit said.

However, the ECI concedes in the affidavit at one point that “in situations involving exigencies and particularly where the immediate issuance of appropriate orders is necessary, when it is not feasible for the CEC or any of the Election Commissioners to be available in person”, an approval of the members of the ECI is obtained through “electronic means” and recorded later in the official file.

“Important functions” were “directly under the Commission as a whole”. “Decisions taken in meetings of the EC or are noted in files bear the signatures of the Election Commissioners and the CEC,” the affidavit said.

An office order was issued on July 28, 2026 by an IAS officer of the rank of additional secretary who had been posted on deputation to the ECI pertaining to internal work allocation.

Indirect confirmation

The affidavit, however, indirectly confirmed that Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi had written to the Cabinet Secretary about the conduct of Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg, following a controversial July 28 order affecting levels of IT oversight over electoral rolls. The order was passed without the knowledge or consensus of the two Election Commissioners.

“On July 29, the two ECs had written separate letters to the Cabinet Secretary in relation to this order and the conduct of the officer,” the affidavit. It said that the July 28 order was “never implemented”.

The ECI denied allegations that Form 6 was amended in consecutive special intensive revision (SIR) orders of June 24, 2025; October 27, 2025 and May 14, 2026.

It reasoned that the additional declaration form requiring voters to provide details of mapping was “not part of Form 6, which is the statutory form for inclusion in the electoral roll”.

“The declaration form is one of the documents which is required to be submitted by any applicant along with Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral roll during the SIR exercise,” the affidavit said.

The poll body said the “mapping concept” in the additional declaration form only obviated the need for submitting further documents for verification. It was only a “measure taken for the assistance of voters”.

“There is no change in the Form 6,” the affidavit said.

The ECI said the 16.10 lakhappeals filed in tribunals against inclusion of voters in the West Bengal electoral rolls were indeed filed by the officers of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), West Bengal, “in their capacity as authorities under the Representation of the People Act”. The submission, the ECI said, was based on a communication from the West Bengal CEO on October 22.

“The officers had the authority to file the appeals as per the orders of the Supreme Court, and these matters were not brought to the Commission,” the affidavit said.

In Goa

As for allegations of 97 voters in Goa who were initially left out of the electoral rolls during SIR, the ECI said house visits were held, and 88 out of the 97 voters have already filled Form 6 for inclusion.

“Their applications have been accepted. Six were out of the country and three were Portuguese passport holders,” the ECI said.

World.title: A.P., Odisha on alert as cyclone ‘Arnab’ nears land
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has directed officials to evacuate people from flood-prone areas, prioritise vulnerable residents, and deploy disaster response teams in the wake of the cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has ordered heightened preparedness across the State, officials said, adding that 4,711 pregnant women will be shifted to safer healthcare facilities. They said 30,043 fishing boats have returned to the harbours.

Also read | Deep depression intensifies into Cyclonic Storm Arnab

With the cyclonic storm moving closer to land, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has issued red alerts for seven of the 28 districts in Andhra Pradesh for Tuesday (October 27, 2026). Isolated extremely heavy rainfall of 200 mm or more is likely in the districts of Kakinada, East Godavari, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, West Godavari, Alluri Sitharama Raju, and Anakapalli, while heavy to very heavy rainfall of around 70 mm to 200 mm is likely in the districts of Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Srikakulam, and Parvathipuram Manyam on Tuesday (October 26).

The storm is likely to cross the coast as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’, with wind speed gusting to 140 kmph, close to Yanam or Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh around noon on Wednesday (October 28).

The State has deputed seven National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and eight SDRF battalions to districts that are likely to be affected. The A.P. State Disaster Management Authority has cautioned the public that gales with speeds touching 110 kmph are likely over the coastal parts. Strong winds of up to 50 kmph are likely over Rayalaseema. For assistance, the public can contact 112, 1070, 18004250101, the government said.

The Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited has opened 30 divisional control rooms, in addition to 11 circle-level control rooms, to monitor the situation and coordinate emergency response. Kakinada and East Godavari have three divisional control rooms each, while Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema has two.

1,700 shelters ready

In neighbouring Odisha, the government said over 1,700 shelters are ready to accommodate people likely to be evacuated in the southern districts of Malkangiri, Koraput, Nabarangpur, Gajapati, and Rayagada, which will be impacted by the cyclone.

Addressing the media after a review meeting with Cabinet Secretary T.V. Somanathan through a video conference, Odisha Chief Secretary Anu Garg said, “We have prepared district-specific plans to face emergency situation in view of the impending cyclone. We are monitoring the health condition of roughly 3,000 pregnant women. They will be shifted to safer place if the situation warrants.”

The Centre has assured to send additional disaster response forces and provide assistance of the Army and the Navy if the situation worsens, she said.

Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil said the State has 135 permanent cyclone shelters in the vulnerable districts and 1,600 temporary shelters have been made available.

Eight NDRF teams, 40 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams, and fire services personnel have been deployed across districts.

“We are in constant touch with the Chhattisgarh government. When the cyclone curves away to Chhattisgarh, it will trigger heavy rain. This will send the Mahanadi River in spate. Since we are around the full moon day, discharge of water to the sea would not be that easy. We need to keep the plan ready for water discharge,” said Suresh Pujari, State Revenue and Disaster Management Minister.

‘Very severe cyclonic storm’

On Monday, the cyclonic storm lay centered over west-central and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal, about 520 km southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha, 540 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 620 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 720 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam, 790 km east-southeast of Bapatla, and 680 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman islands.

The IMD said it will move west-northwestwards, intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday evening, and further strengthen to form a “very severe cyclonic storm” by Tuesday. Thereafter, the system, moving northwestwards, will cross the coast close to Yanam as a “very severe cyclonic storm”.

World.title: Results of Karnataka Legislative Council polls to be announced today
World.content:
Counting of votes polled in four graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies of the Karnataka Legislative Council will get under way on Tuesday morning, and results are expected later in the day.

As many as 43 candidates, including three sitting members, are in the fray. Of the total 3.43 lakh voters across four constituencies, 2.01 lakh voters have cast their votes in the elections held on Friday.

Prominent among the candidates is five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman of the Upper House Puttanna, who is contesting on the Congress ticket to retain his seat from the Bangalore Teachers’ constituency.

The other three constituencies — Karnataka South East Graduates’, Karnataka West Graduates’ and Karnataka North East Teachers’ — are held by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) currently. Sitting members S.V. Sankanur and Sashil Namoshi are contesting from the West Graduates’ and North East Teachers’, respectively. Mr. Sankanur is being challenged by former MLC Mohan Limbikai. With the BJP sitting member of the South East Graduates’, Chidanand Gowda, opting out of the contest, the BJP has fielded K.M. Suresh against Shashi Hulkuntemutt of the Congress.

Currently, the Congress holds a majority in the 75-member Council, as it has 38 members, while National Democratic Alliance partners BJP and Janata Dal (Secular) have 24 and six members, respectively.

Five seats, for which the government has to nominate members, are currently vacant. One seat is held by the Chairman, and the other is represented by an Independent.

As part of the electoral alliance, the BJP is contesting to retain the three seats, while the JD(S) has fielded its candidate from the Bangalore Teachers’ constituency. The ruling Congress has contested all four seats.

World.title: SC pulls up Rajasthan over Jojari river pollution, warns of CBI probe
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (October 26, 2026) pulled up the Rajasthan government over the role of its officials in facilitating illegal mining affecting the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, observing that mining leases had been regularised even after violations were detected. The court warned of a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe if the State failed to take remedial steps to address the environmental damage.

“What have you done about providing statistics on illegal mining in the rivers? When illegal mining was pointed out, your officers went ahead and regularised those leases. If you don’t pull up your socks and mend your ways, we will be compelled to direct a CBI investigation. That would land many of your officers in hot water,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta told Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, appearing for the Rajasthan government.

The oral observations came during suo motu proceedings initiated by the top court last year following a news report flagging alarming levels of pollution in the Jojari river, which serves as a lifeline for nearly two million people in Rajasthan.

The court had earlier directed the State government to “seal and dismantle” all illegal and unauthorised discharge points into the river, including bypass arrangements, manholes, chambers, pipelines and conduits. The authorities were also directed to initiate appropriate proceedings against landowners or occupiers, as well as State officials, responsible for the lapses.

Mr. Raju informed the Bench on Monday (October 26, 2026) that cases had been registered over illegal mining and that the State government was taking steps to halt industrial activities along the three rivers and prevent industrial waste from being discharged directly into the river system.

The Bench, however, questioned the “bona fides” of State officials, pointing out that areas where illegal mining had earlier been detected were subsequently regularised through the grant of mining leases.

“You say that you have registered FIRs. How do you maintain the river flow if you are giving contiguous leases? We fail to understand the bona fides of your officers... You are equally responsible for the pollution by closing your eyes and supporting this illegal activity,” Justice Mehta remarked.

The Bench said it would issue detailed directions in the matter and asked the State, in the meantime, to place before it a concrete financial proposal for establishing common effluent treatment plants (CETPs) equipped with zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) technology.

Justice Mehta made it clear that the State could not leave the task of restoring the rivers entirely to industries and municipal bodies when its own authorities had failed to discharge their regulatory obligations.

“Mr. Raju, you have to convey to the State that ultimately, the polluter pays principle will apply equally to the State as well as to the industries. So, as the State and its officials have apparently failed to discharge their obligations, we will cast the first burden on the State now,” he said.

The Bench indicated that the State would have to bear part of the cost of setting up treatment facilities and laying pipelines through which treated water could be recirculated to industrial units. The industries, too, would be required to contribute towards the measures.

The court gave the State until the next hearing on November 27 to place its proposal on record. It also underlined that the economic viability of industries could not take precedence over the consequences of pollution for residents dependent on the river system.

“Making 20 lakh people live in hell cannot be compared with your economic viability and economic sustenance of a few thousand people,” Justice Mehta remarked.

The State government was accordingly asked to place before the court a workable plan for restoring the river system and ensuring that industries operate in compliance with environmental norms.

In August, the Supreme Court prohibited construction and development within 100 metres of the banks of the three rivers. It also barred hazardous industries and activities within 500 metres on either side of their existing flood lines.

The court subsequently constituted a committee headed by Justice R.M. Lodha in November to draw up a restoration and rejuvenation plan for the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system.

It has also set up an Integrated Coordination Group and a River Rejuvenation Commission or Authority, both under the chairmanship of the Rajasthan Chief Secretary. The two bodies have been tasked with scientifically demarcating the high flood lines of the three rivers and identifying encroachments along the rivers and their basins.

World.title: On Accession Day, Mehbooba reminds Centre of promises, says ‘trust broken’
World.content:
Former J&K Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti, while observing October 26 as the Accession Day, on Monday (October 26, 2026) said J&K’s accession to India “came with guarantees, not a blank cheque for their violation”. Meanwhile, the BJP also observed the day with fanfare.

October 26 was introduced as an official holiday in J&K during the Central rule in 2020, immediately after the abrogation of provisions of Article 370 in 2019.

“J&K’s accession to India was based on trust in secular leadership of Mahatma Gandhi and the assurances to protect its distinct identity, land, jobs and composite culture. The safeguards under Articles 370 and 35A remain important for protecting the region’s interests,” said Ms. Mufti, while holding a copy of the Instrument of Accession from 1947, which restricted India’s role in the region to Defence, External Affairs, Communications and Currency.

On the abrogation of Article 370, Ms. Mufti said, “The move weakened the constitutional safeguards and political rights of J&K’s people. Restrictions on protests and freedom of expression should not be mistaken for acceptance of the prevailing situation. The BJP mistakes this silence for acceptance and assumes that the situation has become normal. But this is not normality; it is fear,” said Ms. Mufti.

She said J&K joined hands with India with trust and on certain conditions, “but those promises have been broken. Instead of winning people’s hearts, the government is using laws and force to control J&K”.

She said that even after 80 years, J&K continued to face difficulties. “The region remained heavily militarised. Kashmir is witnessing passport restrictions, police summons to former militants and frequent security checks. Investigative agencies, security forces and restrictions were being used instead of dialogue,” said Ms. Mufti.

Meanwhile, in Srinagar, the BJP celebrated the 79th anniversary of the accession to the Union of India by distributing sweets. “It is a historic day that we celebrate. The Maharaja was a great visionary, as he felt the people of Jammu and Kashmir would have a secure future in the Union of India,” said BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur said.

He also praised the Doga Maharaja for “rejecting the two-nation theory and acceding to India.”

BJP Member of Parliament Jugal Kishore paid tributes to the late Brigadier Rajinder Singh at the Accession Day function held in Jammu. “Mr. Rajinder made supreme sacrifice in defeating Pakistan’s aggression which resulted in J&K’s integration with India,” said Mr. Kishore.

World.title: Pezeshkian urges 'regional unity' in meeting with Makkah pact countries in Tehran
World.content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday called for “regional unity” at a meeting in Tehran with representatives of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which recently signed the Makkah defence pact.

“I hope that the presence of representatives of important and influential Islamic countries at this meeting will help further consolidate regional unity and cohesion,” Pezeshkian said, according to a statement shared on the presidential website, urging Islamic countries to “stand together and adopt a coordinated position”.

“Muslims are brothers to one another and must stand together as a united front against threats and actions targeting Muslim nations,” he stressed.

Condemning Israel’s actions in Gaza and other regional countries, he said: “We must not allow the Israeli regime to assassinate and aggress against any individual or country whenever it desires. I am confident that if Islamic countries stand alongside each other and adopt a coordinated stance, the possibility of such actions repeating will not exist.”

The Iranian president also criticised the United States for claiming “readiness for negotiation and dialogue simultaneously with attacking Iran” during the war.

Pezeshkian stressed the need for translating political understandings into practical actions, stating: “We are determined to tread this path, but achieving this goal requires Islamic countries to reach a common understanding of their objectives, draw a clear vision, and pursue the implementation of agreements with mutual commitment until results are achieved.”

He cautioned against policies of the United States and Israel that were aimed at “creating a rift among Muslim nations”, and called for heightened vigilance.

The Iranian president also called for increased cooperation among regional countries in various fields.

Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster earlier shared a video of the meeting, saying the quadrilateral meeting on “regional security and stability” had begun. The video showed Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi sitting with Iran’s president, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

Earlier in the day, Inter-Services Public Relations had confirmed that CDF Munir was visiting Tehran, but did not share any further details.

The talks also included Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkiye’s intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin.

At the start of the meeting, Iran’s state broadcaster reported the meeting was bringing together Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to discuss “regional cooperation, the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its consequences”, among other topics.

State-run PressTV also shared pictures of the meeting.

Following the meeting, Rezaei, head of Supreme National Security Council, told state television, “Very good discussions took place between us.”

“I feel that a new atmosphere is emerging in the region … I sensed a very positive atmosphere in the discussions among the gentlemen.”

Iranian state television reported that the four countries agreed to continue talks after a “first” meeting in Tehran. It said they “agreed to continue discussions to strengthen cooperation… including on regional peace and security”.

Earlier, Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency quoted the deputy secretary of Iran’s top security body, Ali Bagheri Kani, as saying that the visit was part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia.

Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, said during a media briefing that the meeting with officials from the three countries would cover “most pressing issues threatening our region”, which included Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in Palestine and Lebanon.

He added that the topic of “top priority on the agenda would be consequences of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its ramifications for the entire region”.

IRNA further quoted him as saying that this meeting could be a prelude to further steps towards shaping “endogenous security — an issue that we have been insisting on for decades”.

“We emphasise that regional security will not be ensured except by relying on the … security considerations of the countries of the region,” he said, adding that events of the last two years, especially the past eight months, had shown that sustainable and reliable security would only be made possible by “building trust and cooperation among the countries in the region”.

Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly had also confirmed the visit in a post on X. Krimly described the visit as “part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Defence Alliance members for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis, and promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by Qatar and Pakistan”.

“The visit underscores the pivotal role of Makkah Defence Alliance members in reinforcing regional security and stability, and working with all countries in the region to achieve that goal,” he added.

The visit comes as attacks by Houthis have spiralled over recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated.

Monday’s planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under the Makkah pact, signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

CDF Munir had visited Iran last week. During the visit, Iranian leaders had conveyed that the US must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations.

According to Iran’s ISNA news agency, Baqaei said during the media briefing that the suggestion for the meeting was made during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran last week. Tehran reviewed the proposal “favourably … and it is scheduled to be held today”, he added.

War has engulfed the Middle East since late February when the US and Israel launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, just as Washington and Tehran were in the middle of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel.

Iran claims control over the strait and regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross without its authorisation, while the United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal which laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.

The war has since spread across the region to include fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.54 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.16
World.content:
The government on Monday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.54 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.16.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs379.25 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.82 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 27 (Tuesday).

On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions.

The same day, senators raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues.

PPP’s Sherry Rehman questioned petrol availability for December and Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas warned of a bleak situation amid heightening Middle East tensions.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.
